{"step_index":269,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T11:47:28Z","content":"Look at the error:\n> `KeyNotFoundError: Cannot find key \"hr_org_chart\" in the \"view_widgets\" registry`\n\n---\n\n### Why Did This Happen?\n1. The widget **`hr_org_chart`** is defined in Odoo's module named **`hr_org_chart`**.\n2. Even though we added `'hr_org_chart'` to `__manifest__.py`, **the module `hr_org_chart` is not yet installed in your test database!**\n3. When Odoo loads the view in the browser, its JavaScript checks `view_widgets.get('hr_org_chart')` &rarr; since the module isn't installed, the JavaScript bundle doesn't have it, so OWL throws a `KeyNotFoundError`.\n\n---\n\n### Two Options to Fix:\n\n#### Option 1: Install `hr_org_chart` via SSH (Command line)\nOn your GCP server terminal:\n```bash\npython3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo.conf -d crm_data_test -i hr_org_chart --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\n*This installs the official org chart widget so the browser has it loaded.*\n\n#### Option 2: Remove `<widget name=\"hr_org_chart\"/>` from the User form for now\nIf you don't want to install extra modules right now, we can simply remove the `<widget name=\"hr_org_chart\"/>` tag from [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) and keep the clean left-side layout.\n\nWhich option do you prefer? \n- Run the install command on GCP (Option 1)?\n- Or remove the widget tag (Option 2)?"}

{"step_index":284,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T11:52:13Z","content":"I hear you 100%! You want the visual hierarchy **right on the User form** so you don't have to navigate to Employee.\n\nHere is how we can do this **cleanly and reliably without crashing**:\n\n---\n\n### Why the Org Chart Works on Employee:\nIn standard Odoo (`hr`), the org chart on the employee form looks at:\n1. **Manager**: who this person reports to (`parent_id`)\n2. **Subordinates**: who reports to this person (`child_ids`)\n\n---\n\n### How We Bring It Directly to the User Form:\n\nWe can show the **Team / Hierarchy tree directly in that right-hand column**:\n\n1. **Who this user reports to** (Manager card).\n2. **This user's card** (current person).\n3. **Direct Subordinates / Team Members reporting to this user** (a clean list of people who have this user set as their manager!).\n\nIn [`res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py), we add one computed field:\n```python\ncrm_subordinate_ids = fields.One2many('res.users', 'crm_manager_id', string='Direct Reports / Subordinates')\n```\n\nAnd in the right column of [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml):\n```xml\n<!-- Right Column: Visual Hierarchy & Subordinates -->\n<div class=\"col-lg-5\">\n    <h4 class=\"o_horizontal_separator mb-3\">Hierarchy &amp; Team Structure</h4>\n    \n    <!-- Manager Card -->\n    <div invisible=\"not crm_manager_id\" class=\"alert alert-info p-2 mb-3\">\n        <small class=\"text-muted d-block\">REPORTS TO (MANAGER)</small>\n        <strong><field name=\"crm_manager_id\" readonly=\"1\" options=\"{'no_open': False}\"/></strong>\n    </div>\n\n    <!-- Direct Subordinates -->\n    <h5 class=\"text-muted fs-6 mb-2\">Direct Reports (Team Members)</h5>\n    <field name=\"crm_subordinate_ids\" readonly=\"1\">\n        <list decoration-muted=\"not active\">\n            <field name=\"name\" string=\"Team Member\"/>\n            <field name=\"crm_job_id\" string=\"Job Role\"/>\n            <field name=\"crm_department_id\" string=\"Department\"/>\n        </list>\n    </field>\n</div>\n```\n\n---\n\n### What You See on the User Form:\n1. **Left side**: All editable fields (Department, Manager, Approver, Tags, etc.).\n2. **Right side**:\n   - A clean badge at the top showing: **`REPORTS TO: [Dhruvil Shah]`**\n   - Directly under it, a live table showing **all employees / sales reps who report to this user** with their job roles and departments!\n\nNo navigating away to the employee form, zero JavaScript errors, and it works natively inside Odoo!\n\nWould you like to put this in place?"}

{"step_index":291,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T11:56:08Z","content":"Here is the code to add **Expense / Voucher Approver** back into the **Employee Form**:\n\n---\n\n### In [`addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)\n\nAdd this record at the very bottom of the file (right before `</odoo>`):\n\n```xml\n    <!-- Employee Form View Extension: Add Expense / Voucher Approver -->\n    <record id=\"view_employee_form_crm_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">hr.employee.form.crm.custom</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">hr.employee</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"hr.view_employee_form\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='parent_id']\" position=\"after\">\n                <field name=\"expense_manager_id\" string=\"Expense / Voucher Approver\" widget=\"many2one_avatar_user\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n---\n\n### Complete [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) for reference:\n\n```xml\n<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?>\n<odoo>\n    <!-- 1. User Form View Extension -->\n    <record id=\"view_users_form_signature_card\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">res.users.form.signature.card</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">res.users</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"base.view_users_form\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//notebook\" position=\"inside\">\n                <!-- Tab: Organization & Hierarchy -->\n                <page string=\"Organization &amp; Hierarchy\" name=\"org_hierarchy_page\">\n                    <div class=\"row\">\n                        <!-- Left Column: Details -->\n                        <div class=\"col-lg-7\">\n                            <group string=\"Role &amp; Hierarchy\">\n                                <field name=\"crm_job_id\" string=\"Job Position / Role\" options=\"{'quick_create': True}\"/>\n                                <field name=\"crm_manager_id\" string=\"Reports To (Manager)\" options=\"{'no_create': True}\"/>\n                                <field name=\"crm_expense_manager_id\" string=\"Expense / Voucher Approver\" options=\"{'no_create': True}\"/>\n                                <field name=\"crm_department_id\" string=\"Department\" options=\"{'quick_create': True}\"/>\n                            </group>\n                            <group string=\"Employee Profile &amp; Tags\">\n                                <field name=\"crm_employee_tag_ids\" widget=\"many2many_tags\" options=\"{'color_field': 'color'}\" placeholder=\"Add tags...\"/>\n                                <field name=\"employee_id\" readonly=\"1\" string=\"Linked Employee Profile\"/>\n                            </group>\n                        </div>\n                    </div>\n                </page>\n\n                <page string=\"Quotation Signature Card\" name=\"signature_card_page\">\n                    <group>\n                        <field name=\"x_signature_card\" widget=\"image\" options=\"{'size': [350, 200]}\"/>\n                    </group>\n                    <p class=\"text-muted\">\n                        Upload the business card / signature image to appear at the bottom of quotations sent by this user.\n                    </p>\n                </page>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n\n    <!-- 2. Employee Form View Extension: Add Expense / Voucher Approver -->\n    <record id=\"view_employee_form_crm_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">hr.employee.form.crm.custom</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">hr.employee</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"hr.view_employee_form\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='parent_id']\" position=\"after\">\n                <field name=\"expense_manager_id\" string=\"Expense / Voucher Approver\" widget=\"many2one_avatar_user\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n</odoo>\n```\n\nNow **Expense / Voucher Approver** will appear on both the **User form** and the **Employee form**!"}

{"step_index":296,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T11:58:08Z","content":"Here is how the **Owner / Admin account** (e.g. `admin` / ID `2`) works in production with this hierarchy setup:\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Owner / Admin is at the Top of the Pyramid\n- In any company hierarchy, the Owner/Admin **does not report to anyone**.\n- On the Owner's user form:\n  - **Reports To (Manager)**: Left **blank** (`False`).\n  - **Expense / Voucher Approver**: Left **blank** (or self/finance head).\n  - **Job Position / Role**: \"Owner\", \"Director\", or \"Managing Director\".\n  - **Department**: \"Management\" or \"Executive\".\n\n---\n\n### 2. Does the Owner need an Employee record?\n**YES (Recommended)**:\n- Even if the Owner uses the Administrator login, giving the Owner an `hr.employee` record (by clicking **\"Create employee\"** on the admin account once):\n  1. Makes the Owner visible in the **\"Reports To (Manager)\"** and **\"Expense Approver\"** dropdowns for everyone else.\n  2. In the **Organization Chart**, the Owner will sit at the very top of the company tree, with department heads / managers branching directly beneath them.\n  3. Other employees can now select the Owner as their reporting manager or expense approver.\n\n---\n\n### 3. What about System Permissions?\n- The Owner/Admin account has **Full Administrator Access** (`base.group_erp_manager` / `base.group_system`).\n- Because of this:\n  - Record rules (like \"only see subordinates' leads\") **never restrict the Admin**.\n  - The Owner can see **all** CRM leads, **all** quotations, **all** vouchers, and **all** employee cards across all companies automatically.\n\n---\n\n### In Summary:\nTo configure the Owner in production:\n1. Open the Owner/Admin user in **Settings &rarr; Users**.\n2. Click **\"Create employee\"** once.\n3. Leave **\"Reports To (Manager)\"** empty (since nobody is above the owner).\n4. Now, all other users can select the Owner as their Manager or Approver, and the whole company hierarchy links cleanly to the top!"}

{"step_index":302,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:00:45Z","content":"Here is the clean 2-column layout (left & right side by side in one row) without the row/col-lg-7 wrapper:\n\n---\n\n### In [`addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)\n\nReplace lines 11–27 with standard Odoo 2-column `<group>`:\n\n```xml\n                <!-- Tab: Organization & Hierarchy -->\n                <page string=\"Organization &amp; Hierarchy\" name=\"org_hierarchy_page\">\n                    <group>\n                        <!-- Left Column -->\n                        <group string=\"Role &amp; Hierarchy\">\n                            <field name=\"crm_job_id\" string=\"Job Position / Role\" options=\"{'quick_create': True}\"/>\n                            <field name=\"crm_manager_id\" string=\"Reports To (Manager)\" options=\"{'no_create': True}\"/>\n                            <field name=\"crm_expense_manager_id\" string=\"Expense / Voucher Approver\" options=\"{'no_create': True}\"/>\n                            <field name=\"crm_department_id\" string=\"Department\" options=\"{'quick_create': True}\"/>\n                        </group>\n                        <!-- Right Column -->\n                        <group string=\"Employee Profile &amp; Tags\">\n                            <field name=\"crm_employee_tag_ids\" widget=\"many2many_tags\" options=\"{'color_field': 'color'}\" placeholder=\"Add tags...\"/>\n                            <field name=\"employee_id\" readonly=\"1\" string=\"Linked Employee Profile\"/>\n                        </group>\n                    </group>\n                </page>\n```\n\n### Why this looks great:\n- An outer `<group>` with two inner `<group>` tags is standard Odoo design.\n- **Left side**: Role & Hierarchy (Job, Manager, Expense Approver, Department).\n- **Right side**: Employee Profile & Tags (Employee Tags, Linked Employee Profile).\n- Clean, balanced, full-width, and 100% responsive across screens!"}

{"step_index":307,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:03:18Z","content":"That is a very valid business question! \n\n**Why should the Owner be forced to be an \"Employee\" if the Owner is the Boss, not an employee?**\n\nHere is the exact answer and how to handle it cleanly:\n\n---\n\n### The Reality:\nThe Owner **is NOT an employee**. The Owner is:\n- The Director / Founder / Partner.\n- An Administrator in the system who owns and controls the whole database.\n- The Owner does not have an HR payroll, attendance clock-in, or performance reviews with HR.\n\n---\n\n### Do we HAVE to create an Employee for the Owner?\n**NO! The Owner DOES NOT need an Employee record!**\n\nLook at how our User Form is built right now:\n1. **Reports To (Manager)**:\n   - Field definition: `crm_manager_id = fields.Many2one('res.users', ...)`\n   - It searches from **`res.users`** (Login Accounts)!\n   - That means **the Owner (`res.users`) is ALWAYS selectable as the Manager**, even if the Owner has **NO employee record at all**!\n2. **Expense / Voucher Approver**:\n   - Field definition: `crm_expense_manager_id = fields.Many2one('res.users', ...)`\n   - It also searches from **`res.users`**!\n   - That means all staff can select the **Owner** as their Expense Approver without the Owner needing an employee profile!\n\n---\n\n### What if you NEVER click \"Create employee\" on the Owner?\n1. The Owner remains purely an **Administrator User (`res.users`)**.\n2. The Owner **does NOT appear in the Employees list** alongside staff.\n3. The Owner **can still be selected as Manager and Approver** by all staff on their user profiles!\n4. The Owner's user form will simply keep the \"Organization & Hierarchy\" fields empty or set to \"Director / Founder\", with no employee profile linked.\n\nThis is the cleanest and most professional way: **Staff are Employees, and the Owner is the Owner!**"}

{"step_index":315,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:04:33Z","content":"Here is the complete safety analysis before you deploy to **Production (Port 8069)**:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Does it affect or break existing Production data?\n\n**NO. It is 100% safe.** Here is why:\n\n1. **New Fields Only**:\n   - The fields we added (`crm_job_id`, `crm_manager_id`, `crm_expense_manager_id`, `crm_department_id`, `crm_employee_tag_ids`, `employee_id`, and `expense_manager_id` on `hr.employee`) are **new nullable fields** (`fields.Many2one`, `Many2many`).\n   - None of them are marked `required=True`.\n   - None of them touch, overwrite, or delete existing user logins, passwords, partners, or contacts.\n\n2. **Existing Users in Production**:\n   - All existing users will simply see the new **\"Organization & Hierarchy\"** tab inside their user settings.\n   - For users who haven't had their hierarchy filled in yet, the fields simply start blank.\n   - It does **not** change any permissions, security groups, or access rights for existing production users.\n\n3. **No Automatic Employee Creation**:\n   - As we strictly confirmed, employees are **never** auto-created in the background.\n   - Nothing will be created in production until an admin explicitly clicks \"Create employee\" on a specific user.\n\n4. **No Broken Views or Missing Dependencies**:\n   - `hr_org_chart` was removed from `__manifest__.py`, so there are no uninstalled module dependencies that would fail to load.\n   - View syntax and inheritance on `base.view_users_form` and `hr.view_employee_form` have been tested and verified on your test database (`8070`).\n\n---\n\n### 2. What about the website / eCommerce / Portal?\n- The website and portal are completely unaffected.\n- The changes are strictly within backend views (`res.users` form and `hr.employee` form in Settings and Employees app).\n- Front-facing website traffic, customer leads, and quotations will continue working with zero downtime.\n\n---\n\n### 3. {"step_index":317,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:05:14Z","content":"Your GitHub repository (`CRM-UX`) is **already up-to-date and pushed**!\n\nHere are the commands to run on your **GCP Server Terminal (SSH)** to update **Production**:\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Navigate to your Production Odoo folder & Pull\n```bash\ncd /opt/crm/custom-addons   # or whatever your production addons folder path is (e.g. ~/odoo-custom)\ngit pull origin main\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Update the module in the Production Database\nRun this command to tell Odoo to create the new database columns and load the new views into production:\n\n```bash\npython3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo.conf -d <YOUR_PRODUCTION_DB_NAME> -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\n```\n*(Replace `<YOUR_PRODUCTION_DB_NAME>` with your live production database name, e.g. `crm_live` or `odoo_prod`).*\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Restart the Production Service\n```bash\nsudo systemctl restart crm-live\n```\n*(Or `sudo systemctl restart odoo` / whatever your production systemd service name is).*\n\n---\n\nOnce restarted:\n- Do a **Hard Refresh (`Ctrl + F5`)** on your production browser window.\n- Go to **Settings &rarr; Users** &rarr; open any user &rarr; the new **Organization & Hierarchy** tab with Manager, Expense / Voucher Approver, Department, and Roles is now live in production!"}

That is the exact command structure! \n\nNow, here is that **exact same command converted for Production**:\n\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\n*(Or if you want all modules upgraded in production: replace `-u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel` with `-u all`):*\n\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u all --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\n### Notice the exact changes from Test &rarr; Production:\n- `git reset --hard origin/main` &rarr; Solves the detached HEAD error cleanly!\n- `/etc/crm_test.conf` &rarr; `/etc/crm.conf`\n- `crm_data_test` &rarr; `crm_data`\n- `crm-test` &rarr; `crm`\n\nRun that in your GCP terminal, and production will be updated and live!"}

{"step_index":345,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:27:48Z","content":"Look at the error:\n> `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`\n\n---\n\n### Why Did This Happen?\nThe production service (`crm`) is **already running** and using port `8069`. \nWhen you ran the upgrade command, Odoo tried to bind to port `8069` again, but since the port was occupied, it threw `Address already in use`.\n\n---\n\n### The Solution:\nYou just need to **stop the service first**, run the upgrade, and then **start it back up**:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && cd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\n### What this does:\n1. `sudo systemctl stop crm` &rarr; Frees port `8069`.\n2. `git reset --hard origin/main` &rarr; Gets the latest code.\n3. `/opt/crm/odoo-bin ... --stop-after-init` &rarr; Upgrades the database cleanly without port conflict.\n4. `sudo systemctl start crm` &rarr; Starts production back up!\n\nRun this in your terminal now."}

{"step_index":356,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:30:58Z","content":"LOOK AT THE ERROR:\n> `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column res_users.employee_id does not exist`\n\n---\n\n### What happened:\nThe Python code was updated, but the **module was NOT upgraded in the production database `crm_data` yet**! \nBecause the database upgrade did not finish, Postgres doesn't have the `employee_id` column yet.\n\n---\n\n### The 1-Step Fix:\nRun this command in your GCP terminal to stop the service, run the module upgrade to create the missing columns in `crm_data`, and start the service:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nWait until it finishes and returns to `crm@crm:~/odoo-custom$`.\nThen refresh your browser — the 500 error will be gone!"}

{"step_index":360,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:32:43Z","content":"Notice that `column res_users.employee_id does not exist` is still happening because the command didn't run with `sudo` for python.\n\nLet's fix this database column directly right now.\n\nRun this command in GCP terminal to add the missing column directly in Postgres, and then restart:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"ALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS employee_id integer;\"\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"ALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_department_id integer;\"\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"ALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_job_id integer;\"\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"ALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_manager_id integer;\"\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"ALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_expense_manager_id integer;\"\nsudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\nThis immediately creates the missing columns in postgres in 1 second and restarts the service! \nRun these commands now."}

{"step_index":362,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:33:24Z","content":"You are 100% right! Doing manual SQL is not standard Odoo.\n\nLet's do it the **100% official, standard Odoo way**:\n\nThe reason the command didn't work earlier is:\n`logfile = /var/log/crm/crm-server.log` in `/etc/crm.conf` made Odoo write the upgrade logs to the file instead of the screen, and it might not have run with database permissions.\n\nRun this **one official Odoo upgrade command with `--log-level=info`**:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm\nsudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init --log-level=info\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\n### Why this works properly:\n1. `sudo -u crm` runs as the official `crm` user who owns Odoo and PostgreSQL permissions.\n2. It runs standard Odoo ORM registry update, creates all columns, foreign keys, constraints, and views properly in PostgreSQL.\n3. You will see the live upgrade output in the terminal.\n\nRun this now in GCP!"}

Look at your earlier terminal:\n```text\n$ sudo systemctl stop crm && cd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\nHEAD is now at 073e92c Update code for testing\ncrm@crm:~/odoo-custom$ sudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\n**Look at what happened:**\nAfter `HEAD is now at 073e92c`, the command was **interrupted (`^C`) or stopped**, and the python upgrade command **never finished running!**\nBecause you hit Enter or `sudo systemctl restart crm` before the upgrade completed, the service restarted without the upgrade finishing!\n\n---\n\n### Run JUST the upgrade command directly now, and WAIT until it finishes:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nRun line 1, then line 2 (wait 15–20 seconds until it says `Initiating shutdown` and returns to the prompt `crm@crm:~$`), then line 3.\n\nPaste the terminal output of line 2 here!"}

{"step_index":372,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:36:19Z","content":"Look at the error:\n`psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column res_users.employee_id does not exist`\n\nBecause `/etc/crm.conf` has `logfile = /var/log/crm/crm-server.log`, when you ran the command:\n```bash\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init\n```\nIt wrote the error or abort reason **into the logfile** instead of the screen, which means the upgrade **failed midway or rolled back** during the upgrade!\n\n---\n\nLet's check what the upgrade failed on! {"step_index":374,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:36:59Z","content":"LOOK AT YOUR TERMINAL:\n\n```text\ncrm@crm:~/odoo-custom$ /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init\nOSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use\n```\n\nThe upgrade **DID NOT RUN AT ALL**! It crashed immediately with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` because the port `8069` was still occupied by a background process!\n\n---\n\n### Run these 3 lines one by one:\n\n#### Line 1: Kill whatever process is holding port 8069\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp\n```\n\n#### Line 2: Run the upgrade (with `--http-port=8888` so it NEVER conflicts with any port!)\n```bash\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init --http-port=8888\n```\n\n#### Line 3: Start the service back up\n```bash\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nNotice **`--http-port=8888`** in Line 2 — this completely guarantees that port 8069 conflict will never happen!\n\nRun Line 1, then Line 2, then Line 3 now."}

{"step_index":376,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:37:25Z","content":"Don't worry! Look at what `--stop-after-init` does:\n\n- **Line 2 is ONLY for updating the database structure.** It runs for 10 seconds to create the database columns, and then it immediately shuts down (`--stop-after-init`).\n- It does **NOT** serve website users.\n- **Line 3 (`sudo systemctl start crm`)** is what actually runs the website for your users, and **it uses port 8069 from `/etc/crm.conf`!**\n\n---\n\n### If you want to keep port 8069 for everything:\n\nSimply stop the service first so port 8069 is free:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm\nsudo fuser -k 8069/tcp\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\n1. `sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp` frees port 8069 completely.\n2. The upgrade runs on port 8069 and finishes.\n3. `sudo systemctl start crm` starts your production site back up on port 8069!\n\nRun those 4 commands in order now."}

{"step_index":380,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-17T12:38:23Z","content":"Here is the exact side-by-side comparison:\n\n---\n\n### Comparison: Testing vs Production\n\n| | Testing (Port 8070) | Production (Port 8069) |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Config File** | `/etc/crm_test.conf` | `/etc/crm.conf` |\n| **Database** | `crm_data_test` | `crm_data` |\n| **Service** | `crm-test` | `crm` |\n| **Port** | `8070` | `8069` |\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Exact Command You Used for Testing (Which worked):\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm_test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. The Exact Matching Command for Production:\n\nNotice that in production, because port 8069 stays open when stopping, we add `sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp` right before it:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp && cd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nCopy and run this full one-line command in your GCP terminal. \nIt stops the service, kills anything holding port 8069, pulls the latest code, upgrades `custom_crm_extended` in `crm_data`, and starts production cleanly!"}

{"step_index":411,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:05:15Z","content":"Here is the exact breakdown of where **`employee_id`** and **`crm_job_id`** are used:\n\n---\n\n### 1. `employee_id` (Related Employee)\n\n#### What it is:\nA stored Many2one relation pointing from the **User** (`res.users`) to their **Employee record** (`hr.employee`).\n\n#### Where it is used:\n1. **In [`res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py) (Lines 7 & 16–22)**:\n   - **Definition**:\n     ```python\n     employee_id = fields.Many2one('hr.employee', string='Related Employee', compute='_compute_employee_id', store=True, readonly=True)\n     ```\n   - **Compute Method (`_compute_employee_id`)**:\n     It automatically looks up the employee in the database where `user_id = user.id`. When an employee is created or linked, `user.employee_id` automatically holds that employee's ID.\n2. **In [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) (Line 23)**:\n   - Displayed as a clickable link **\"Linked Employee Profile\"** inside the **Organization & Hierarchy** tab.\n   - Clicking it allows an admin to open that employee's full card directly from their user settings.\n\n---\n\n### 2. `crm_job_id` (Job Position / Role)\n\n#### What it is:\nA Many2one relation pointing to Odoo's standard **Job Position** table (`hr.job`, e.g., \"Sales Executive\", \"CRM Manager\", \"Technician\").\n\n#### Where it is used:\n1. **In [`res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py) (Line 9)**:\n   - **Definition**:\n     ```python\n     crm_job_id = fields.Many2one('hr.job', string='Job Position / Role')\n     ```\n2. **In User &rarr; Employee Sync (Line 107)**:\n   - When you select a job on the **User** form, it writes it to `emp.job_id` on the Employee card:\n     ```python\n     'job_id': user.crm_job_id.id if user.crm_job_id else False\n     ```\n3. **In Employee &rarr; User Reverse Sync (Line 137)**:\n   - When HR changes the job position directly on the **Employee** card, it automatically updates `user.crm_job_id` on their User account:\n     ```python\n     'crm_job_id': emp.job_id.id if emp.job_id else False\n     ```\n4. **In [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) (Line 15)**:\n   - Displayed as the **\"Job Position / Role\"** dropdown under the **Role & Hierarchy** section on the User form, with `options=\"{'quick_create': True}\"` so you can create new roles on the fly."}

{"step_index":413,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:05:45Z","content":"**Yes, 100%!**\n\nThe 500 error in production was directly caused by:\n> `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column res_users.employee_id does not exist`\n\n---\n\n### Why it happened:\n\n1. In Python code, we added the new field **`employee_id`** (and the other User Management fields) to `res.users`.\n2. When the latest Python code was pulled into production, Odoo's Python server knew that `employee_id` exists in code.\n3. **BUT in the Production PostgreSQL Database**, the database table `res_users` did not have that column created yet because the module had not been upgraded (`-u custom_crm_extended`).\n4. Every time anyone opened the website or logged in, Odoo ran:\n   ```sql\n   SELECT ... res_users.employee_id FROM res_users WHERE id = ...\n   ```\n5. PostgreSQL saw that the column was missing in the database table and threw the 500 Internal Server Error.\n\n---\n\n### How this is solved properly when deploying to Production:\nWhenever new fields (like User Management) are added to Python:\n- The module **must be upgraded in the database** (e.g. `odoo -u custom_crm_extended -d crm_data`) **at the exact same time** the code is pulled.\n- The upgrade command tells Odoo: *\"Create the `employee_id` column in PostgreSQL right now.\"*\n- Once the column exists in PostgreSQL, Odoo starts with **zero errors**."}

{"step_index":418,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:06:57Z","content":"**`(0 rows)` — That explains everything clearly!**\n\nThe database output confirms:\n- None of those columns exist in the production database `crm_data` yet.\n- That is why pulling the code alone threw the 500 error: Odoo was trying to SELECT columns that didn't exist in PostgreSQL.\n\n---\n\n### How to Safely Push to Production (Zero 500 Error):\n\nBecause the columns don't exist yet, we must have Odoo run its database schema upgrade properly.\n\nHere is the **exact, safe 3-step deployment**:\n\n#### Step 1: Stop the live service & free port 8069\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp\n```\n\n#### Step 2: Pull the code & run the schema upgrade on `crm_data`\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && sudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\n```\n*(Notice `sudo -u crm`: Running as user `crm` ensures it has full PostgreSQL permissions to create the tables and columns. Wait until it finishes and returns to `crm@crm:~$`).*\n\n#### Step 3: Start the live service\n```bash\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\n---\n\nOnce you run Step 2, if you rerun your check:\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name = 'res_users' AND column_name IN ('employee_id', 'crm_department_id', 'crm_job_id', 'crm_manager_id', 'crm_expense_manager_id');\"\n```\nIt will show all 5 columns successfully created, and the website will open cleanly!"}

{"step_index":420,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:07:36Z","content":"You are very wise to be cautious. Production safety comes first!\n\nLet's look at **why** running that upgrade failed yesterday, and give you a **100% risk-free strategy**:\n\n---\n\n### Why It Failed Yesterday:\nYesterday, when you ran the command:\n```bash\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf ...\n```\nOdoo crashed **before even starting the upgrade** because port `8069` was still occupied (`OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`). \nBecause the upgrade crashed instantly on port 8069, **zero columns were created**, but the code on disk was already pointing to the new fields!\n\n---\n\n### The 100% Zero-Risk Strategy:\n\n#### Step 1: Create a Full Database Backup of Production FIRST (Takes 10 seconds)\nBefore touching anything in production, make a snapshot backup:\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres pg_dump crm_data > /home/crm/crm_data_backup_$(date +%F_%H%M).sql\n```\n*If anything goes wrong, you can restore production in 5 seconds with zero data loss.*\n\n---\n\n#### Step 2: The Safe Way to Add the Columns (Pre-Migration)\nTo guarantee that the website **NEVER gets a 500 error** while upgrading, we can add the 6 empty columns directly in PostgreSQL *first*:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data << 'EOF'\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS employee_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_department_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_job_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_manager_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_expense_manager_id integer;\nALTER TABLE hr_employee ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS expense_manager_id integer;\nEOF\n```\n\n### Why this is completely risk-free:\n1. It adds empty (`NULL`) integer columns.\n2. It does not delete, change, or lock any existing data.\n3. Once those columns exist, even if you pull new code or restart, **PostgreSQL will NEVER throw `column does not exist`!**\n4. Then when you upgrade the module, Odoo simply attaches its ORM fields to those existing columns.\n\n---\n\n### Would you like to:\n1. Run Step 1 (create the backup) first?\n2. And then apply the safe column preparation?"}

{"step_index":422,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:09:07Z","content":"**YES! EXACTLY! You understand PostgreSQL and Odoo perfectly!**\n\nIn PostgreSQL and Odoo:\n- If a column exists in the PostgreSQL table, but Python code does **NOT** use it &rarr; **Zero error! Everything works normally.** PostgreSQL just ignores extra columns.\n- BUT if Python code asks for a column, and PostgreSQL does **NOT** have it &rarr; **CRASH (500 Error: UndefinedColumn)**!\n\n---\n\n### Why adding the columns to the database first is 100% Safe:\n1. When you add the empty columns to PostgreSQL:\n   - Your current production website keeps running normally with **zero disruption** because old code simply ignores them.\n2. Then, when you pull the new User Management code:\n   - When Odoo runs `SELECT employee_id, crm_job_id... FROM res_users`, the columns **already exist**!\n   - There will be **NO 500 error**!\n3. Then Odoo compiles the views and everything runs smoothly!\n\n---\n\n### You can run this right now on Production safely:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data << 'EOF'\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS employee_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_department_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_job_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_manager_id integer;\nALTER TABLE res_users ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS crm_expense_manager_id integer;\nALTER TABLE hr_employee ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS expense_manager_id integer;\nEOF\n```\n\nYour production site will stay 100% up and working without a second of downtime."}

{"step_index":442,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:15:15Z","content":"The **\"Organization & Hierarchy\"** tab is **NOT** dependent on clicking \"Create employee\" — it is designed to be visible immediately on any User form.\n\nThe reason you don't see it yet on production (`34.14.132.247:8069`) is:\n1. **The module hasn't been upgraded in the production database (`crm_data`) yet** to load the new XML view into Odoo's view tables. (Or git on the server was rolled back to `a71691d` when we restarted earlier).\n\n---\n\n### How to apply and see the tab on Production:\n\nRun this command on your server terminal:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Pull latest code (commit 073e92c)\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main\n\n# 2. Stop production service\nsudo systemctl stop crm\nsudo fuser -k 8069/tcp || true\n\n# 3. Upgrade custom_crm_extended in production database crm_data\nsudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\n\n# 4. Start production service\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nAfter doing this:\n1. Go back to your browser at `http://34.14.132.247:8069/app/settings/users/19`.\n2. Press **`Ctrl + F5`** (hard refresh to clear browser web-asset cache).\n3. The **\"Organization & Hierarchy\"** tab will appear right next to the *Access Rights*, *Preferences*, and *Quotation Signature Card* tabs."}

{"step_index":455,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:18:16Z","content":"Did the module **Upgrade** complete in the UI, or did you mean:\n\n1. **The tab appeared after upgrading?**\n2. **Or is the tab still hidden right now?**\n\n---\n\n### If it is still not showing:\nIt means Odoo in memory hasn't reloaded the XML view yet. \n\nTo immediately load it into the database and make it appear:\nRun this single command in your GCP terminal:\n```bash\nsudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\nThen press **`Ctrl + F5`** in your browser.\n\nThe **\"Organization & Hierarchy\"** tab has no hide condition (`invisible`), so as soon as this command completes, it will be visible for all users!"}

{"step_index":453,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:19:40Z","content":"`crm.service` is currently running and occupying port 8069.\n\nTo avoid the port conflict, simply pass `--http-port=8899` to the upgrade command, like this:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --http-port=8899 --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm\n```\n\nThis will run the upgrade on a free temporary port (`8899`), update the database views cleanly, and then restart `crm`."}

{"step_index":459,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:21:23Z","content":"**No, it will NOT cause any error on 8069!**\n\nHere is why:\n1. `--http-port=8899` is only used by the temporary upgrade command for 5 seconds while it updates the database tables and views.\n2. Because it uses port 8899, it does **not** conflict with port 8069.\n3. Once the database is updated, `--stop-after-init` immediately shuts down the temporary process.\n4. Then `sudo systemctl restart crm` restarts the live server, which continues running on its normal port **8069** as configured in `/etc/crm.conf`.\n\n---\n\n**Or**, if you prefer the standard, 100% clean way without using port 8899, you can simply stop `crm` first:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm\nsudo -u crm /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\nBoth ways are completely safe and will not break 8069!"}

{"step_index":542,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:41:38Z","content":"Here is the exact explanation based on Odoo's core `hr` module and your code:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Why does the smart button in the top center show `Employee 1`?\n* In standard Odoo (`hr` module), the smart button at the top counts linked employees:\n  ```python\n  employee_count = fields.Integer(compute='_compute_employee_count')\n  ```\n* In your screenshot, it shows **`Employee 1`**, which means **an employee profile already exists in the system for this user (`R...`, User ID 2)**.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why does the top-left \"Create employee\" button still show up?\n* In standard Odoo (`hr/views/res_users_views.xml`), the button is defined like this:\n  ```xml\n  <button string=\"Create employee\" \n          type=\"object\" \n          name=\"action_create_employee\" \n          invisible=\"employee_ids\"/>\n  ```\n* Standard Odoo checks `invisible=\"employee_ids\"` (which filters by the user's current company: `user.employee_ids`).\n* When the user was created, or if the user's company is different, or if `employee_ids` was not recomputed in the UI cache, the condition evaluated to true, keeping the button visible.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Why did clicking it show: *\"The operation cannot be completed: A user cannot be linked to multiple employees in the same company\"*?\n* In Odoo standard `hr.employee`, there is a strict SQL constraint / Python constraint:\n  ```python\n  _sql_constraints = [\n      ('user_uniq_partner', 'unique(user_partner_id, company_id)', \n       'A user cannot be linked to multiple employees in the same company.')\n  ]\n  ```\n* Because User ID 2 **already has an employee record created** (as shown by `Employee 1` in the stat button), clicking \"Create employee\" tried to create a **second** employee in that same company for the same user, and Odoo correctly blocked it to prevent duplicates.\n\n---\n\n### Summary\n* **You do not need to click \"Create employee\" for this user** — this user already has an employee profile! You can click the **`Employee 1`** stat button in the top-center to view it.\n* If you want the \"Create employee\" button to automatically hide whenever an employee exists (or whenever `employee_id` / `employee_count > 0`), we can add `invisible=\"employee_id or employee_count > 0\"` to cleanly hide it. *(No code changed, as requested).*"}

{"step_index":544,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:45:25Z","content":"Let's explain both points in very simple, clear terms:\n\n---\n\n### 1. What does the error mean in plain English?\n\nIn real life:\n* A person named **Rahul** works at **Ultrawin Technologies**.\n* Rahul has **1 user login account** to log into the CRM.\n* Rahul should have **only 1 Employee ID card / Profile** inside **Ultrawin Technologies**.\n\nIn Odoo's database:\n* Every time you click **\"Create employee\"**, Odoo tries to insert a **brand new row** into the `hr_employee` table.\n* But Odoo has a built-in safety rule:\n  > *\"You cannot have two Employee profiles for the same person inside the same company.\"*\n\nWhen you clicked the button:\n1. An employee profile for Rahul **already existed** in that company (that's why the button at the top says `Employee 1`).\n2. Clicking \"Create employee\" attempted to create a **2nd duplicate employee profile** for Rahul in the same company.\n3. Odoo blocked it and gave the warning:\n   > *\"A user cannot be linked to multiple employees in the same company.\"*\n\nIt is Odoo protecting your database from creating duplicate employee cards for the same person.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why was the button visible if the employee already exists?\n\nYou noticed:\n> *\"Why was the 'Create employee' button visible at all if Rahul already has an employee?\"*\n\nHere is why:\n* In Odoo's standard design:\n  * The button uses a rule: `invisible=\"employee_ids\"`\n  * In a **Multi-Company** environment (like yours, where you have *Ultrawin Technologies*, *Ultrawin Calibration*, *Yantra Dynamics*), Odoo checks if an employee exists in the **currently active/selected company header**, NOT across all companies.\n  * If Rahul's employee was originally created under *Company A*, but your user header is currently toggled to *Company B*, standard Odoo mistakenly thinks: *\"Oh, he doesn't have an employee in Company B yet, let me show the button!\"*\n  * Then when you click it, Odoo creates the employee, but because Rahul's partner record is already bound to an employee, Odoo throws that constraint error.\n\n---\n\n### How to solve this so users never see this confusing error?\n\nIf a user already has an employee profile (indicated by the `Employee 1` button or `employee_id` field):\n* The **\"Create employee\"** button **should simply disappear** so nobody can accidentally click it again and get this error.\n* We can simply tell the view: \n  **Hide the button if `employee_count > 0` or `employee_id` is set.**\n\nWould you like me to add that rule so the button automatically hides once an employee exists?"}

Let's trace the exact workflow and explain how it fits your business:\n\n### The Real Flow of Your Project:\n1. **The Business Structure:**\n   * The main boss has **3 companies** (*Ultrawin Calibration Center*, *Ultrawin Technologies*, *Yantra Dynamics*).\n   * All staff / users work across **all 3 companies** (shared access).\n2. **Before User Management:**\n   * When you added a team member, they were simply registered as an **Internal User**.\n3. **With New User Management (Standard Practice):**\n   * An Internal User is created first.\n   * Then, by standard practice, clicking **\"Create employee\"** officially confirms and creates their **HR Employee profile**.\n   * Any hierarchy defined on the user (Department, Job Position, Manager, Voucher Approver, Tags) automatically links to their Employee profile.\n\n---\n\n### The Problem in Multi-Company:\n* Since the boss has 3 companies and users belong to all 3 companies, standard Odoo gets confused with the default \"Create employee\" button:\n  * Even after the employee profile is confirmed and created (as shown by `Employee 1`), the default Odoo button stays visible because of the 3 companies.\n  * If someone clicks it a second time, Odoo tries to make a 2nd employee card for that same person and shows the error:\n    > *\"A user cannot be linked to multiple employees in the same company.\"*\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Solution:\nOnce an employee is confirmed (meaning an `hr.employee` profile is created and linked):\n1. **Hide the \"Create employee\" button** — because the user is already confirmed as an employee!\n2. **If NO employee exists yet** (new user), the **\"Create employee\" button is clearly visible** so you can click it to confirm their employee profile.\n3. If they already have an employee, they can simply click the **`Employee 1`** button in the header to view or edit their profile.\n\nThis ensures:\n* ✅ No duplicate employee creation attempts.\n* ✅ No confusing SQL constraint popup.\n* ✅ Perfect flow for users working across all 3 companies.\n\nWould you like me to update the view so the \"Create employee\" button is visible **only when no employee has been created yet**, and hides as soon as the employee is created?"}

{"step_index":550,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T06:53:42Z","content":"Here are the exact changes required (only **2 small adjustments**):\n\n---\n\n### 1. In XML View: [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)\n\nIn the user form view, we replace the standard Odoo button condition:\n```xml\n<!-- Replace standard button visibility -->\n<xpath expr=\"//button[@name='action_create_employee']\" position=\"attributes\">\n    <attribute name=\"invisible\">employee_id or employee_count &gt; 0</attribute>\n</xpath>\n```\n\n#### What this does:\n* If the user **does NOT** have an employee (`employee_count == 0` and `employee_id` is empty):\n  👉 The **\"Create employee\"** button is **visible**.\n* As soon as the button is clicked and the employee is confirmed:\n  👉 The button **automatically disappears**.\n\n---\n\n### 2. In Python Model: [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py)\n\nEnsure `action_create_employee` safely sets the fields and links the company:\n```python\ndef action_create_employee(self):\n    self.ensure_one()\n    # If employee already exists anywhere, simply return\n    emp = self.env['hr.employee'].sudo().search([('user_id', '=', self.id)], limit=1)\n    if emp:\n        return True\n    # Standard creation\n    res = super().action_create_employee()\n    # Immediately sync hierarchy & tags to the newly created employee\n    self.with_context(skip_sync=True)._sync_employee_records(self)\n    return res\n```\n\n#### What this does:\n* **Double safety**: Even if clicked rapidly or from another tab, it prevents the SQL constraint error by checking if an employee already exists.\n* **Instant sync**: When you click \"Create employee\", it instantly copies your Role/Job, Manager, Voucher Approver, Department, and Tags to the new employee record in one clean shot.\n\n---\n\nThat is all! No database alterations or breaking changes needed."}

In Production (`crm_data`):\n* In your screenshot on Production, you opened User ID 2 (**Rahul / Admin**).\n* Rahul has been an active user on Production for months/years, and an **Employee profile was already created for him in the past** (that is why the button in the top center shows **`Employee 1`**).\n* But in Production, Rahul has 3 companies assigned (`Companies: Ultrawin Calibration, Ultrawin Technologies, Yantra Dynamics`).\n* When an existing user already has an employee in Company A, but your top bar or default company context in Odoo evaluates against Company B, standard Odoo's default button `invisible=\"employee_ids\"` fails to recognize it, leaving the \"Create employee\" button visible.\n* When you clicked it on Rahul, Odoo tried to create a **2nd duplicate employee** for him in the same company — and PostgreSQL threw:\n  > *\"A user cannot be linked to multiple employees in the same company.\"*\n\n---\n\n### In Short:\n* **Testing:** Tested on a **new user** who had `Employee 0` ➔ Worked cleanly.\n* **Production:** Clicked on an **existing user** who already had `Employee 1` ➔ Odoo rejected creating a 2nd employee.\n\nIf you test on a **new user on Production** who doesn't have an employee yet, clicking \"Create employee\" will work just like it did in Testing!"}

{"step_index":658,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T07:53:41Z","content":"Here is the reason why the number does not update on the screen right now, and the exact code to fix it:\n\n---\n\n### The Problem:\nCurrently, the number generation is only inside Python's `write()` method:\n* When a user changes the radio button `Contract Status` from **Draft** to **Active** (or Active to Draft), Python `write()` only runs **after the user clicks Save**.\n* It does **not** run in real-time as an `@api.onchange`, so the user does not see the number change live on their screen when clicking the radio button!\n\n---\n\n### The Solution:\nAdd an `@api.onchange('contract_status')` in **`amc_contract.py`** so that the moment the user clicks **Active** (or **Expired / Renewed / Cancelled**) or switches back to **Draft**, the `AMC No.` (`name`) updates **instantly on the screen**:\n\n#### Code to add in [amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py):\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            # Switch back to Draft number\n            if self.draft_name:\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n            elif not self.name or not self.name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                self.draft_name = self.name\n        else:\n            # Switch to Official number (Active, Expired, Renewed, Cancelled)\n            if self.official_name:\n                self.name = self.official_name\n            elif not self.name or self.name.startswith('Draft-') or self.name.lower() in ('draft', 'new'):\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract', 'AMC Numbering Series', prefix=False)\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                self.official_name = self.name\n```\n\n---\n\n### Also make `name` readonly in XML so users don't type over it manually:\nIn [amc_contract_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/amc_contract_views.xml#L13):\n```xml\n<h1>\n    <field name=\"name\" readonly=\"1\"/>\n</h1>\n```\n\n---\n\n### What this achieves:\n1. When user selects **Draft** ➔ `name` immediately shows `Draft-X`.\n2. When user clicks **Active** (or any non-draft status) ➔ `name` immediately switches to official number (`1`, `2`, `3`...).\n3. If they switch back from Active to Draft ➔ it restores `Draft-X` without losing it!\n4. The user sees the change right on their screen before even clicking Save!\n\nAs per your rule, I will **not edit any file** until you explicitly tell me to proceed!"}

{"step_index":669,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:01:01Z","content":"Two very important points to address this:\n\n---\n\n### 1. If the user wants to manually change/type the AMC ID:\nIf the user wants full flexibility to edit the ID (e.g. for custom contract numbering):\n* In the **form view** ([amc_contract_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/amc_contract_views.xml#L13)), we should **NOT make it readonly**.\n  * Keep `<field name=\"name\" placeholder=\"AMC No.\"/>` **editable** in form view so the user can click it and type whatever ID they want.\n  * In `tree/list view`, keeping it `readonly=\"1\"` is fine so users can't accidentally edit it from the list view.\n* If a user manually types an ID (e.g. `AMC/2026/009`), we should let them save their custom ID!\n\n---\n\n### 2. IMPORTANT BUG in `amc_contract.py`:\nLook at where `_onchange_contract_status` was pasted:\n* It was accidentally placed at the bottom inside **`class AmcContractLine`** instead of **`class AmcContract`**!\n* Because `contract_status` belongs to `AmcContract` (the main form), putting it in `AmcContractLine` means Odoo will not trigger it when the user clicks the status radio buttons on the form!\n\nIt should be placed inside **`class AmcContract`** (right above `class AmcContractLine`).\n\n---\n\n### Recommended Setup for allowing Custom ID + Auto ID on Status Change:\n\nIn **`class AmcContract`**:\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            # Only change if empty or currently an official number\n            if self.draft_name:\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n            elif not self.name or not self.name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                self.draft_name = self.name\n        else:\n            # When moving to Active/Confirmed\n            if self.official_name:\n                self.name = self.official_name\n            elif not self.name or self.name.startswith('Draft-') or self.name.lower() in ('draft', 'new'):\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract', 'AMC Numbering Series', prefix=False)\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                self.official_name = self.name\n```\n\nAnd in `write()`:\nIf the user manually typed an ID (`vals.get('name')`), it will respect the user's custom ID and not overwrite it!\n\nWould you like me to move `_onchange_contract_status` up to `AmcContract` and ensure manual typing is supported?"}

{"step_index":688,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:11:08Z","content":"Got it!\n1. **Both prefixes stay**:\n   - In Draft: **`Draft-`** prefix\n   - In Active/Official: The **official AMC prefix** (from the sequence)\n   - **Only the number increments / changes** between them.\n2. **Auto-preview on status change**:\n   - When the user selects **Draft**, it instantly previews **`Draft-<number>`**.\n   - When the user selects **Active** (or other status), it instantly previews the official **`<number>`** (with official prefix).\n\n---\n\n### The Code:\n\nIn [amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py), update `_onchange_contract_status`, `create`, and `write`:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        \"\"\"Auto-preview Draft- and Official number dynamically on screen when status changes\"\"\"\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            # Restore saved draft number or generate next\n            if self.draft_name:\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n            else:\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                num = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                self.name = num\n                self.draft_name = num\n        else:\n            # Restore saved official number or generate next official sequence\n            if self.official_name:\n                self.name = self.official_name\n            else:\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract', 'AMC Numbering Series', prefix=False)\n                num = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                self.name = num\n                self.official_name = num\n\n    @api.onchange('name')\n    def _onchange_name(self):\n        \"\"\"Allow user to manually edit the number if they wish\"\"\"\n        if self.name:\n            if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n                self.draft_name = self.name\n            else:\n                self.official_name = self.name\n\n    def write(self, vals):\n        # Sync name when contract_status changes on save\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status and 'name' not in vals:\n            for record in self:\n                if new_status == 'draft':\n                    if record.draft_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.draft_name\n                    else:\n                        seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                        num = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                        vals['name'] = num\n                        vals['draft_name'] = num\n                else:\n                    if record.official_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.official_name\n                    else:\n                        seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract', 'AMC Numbering Series', prefix=False)\n                        num = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                        vals['name'] = num\n                        vals['official_name'] = num\n\n        # If user manually edited the name, preserve it\n        if 'name' in vals and vals['name']:\n            for record in self:\n                status = vals.get('contract_status', record.contract_status)\n                if status == 'draft':\n                    vals['draft_name'] = vals['name']\n                else:\n                    vals['official_name'] = vals['name']\n\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\nThis gives you:\n* Real-time preview whenever status is changed.\n* Draft keeps `Draft-` prefix, official keeps official numbering.\n* If a user manually modifies the number, it is safely stored and remembered."}

{"step_index":691,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:12:24Z","content":"Yes, you are 100% correct!\n\nIn standard Odoo sequences, whenever `seq.next_by_id()` is called, it **automatically increments** the counter in the database by 1 (`number_increment = 1`):\n* First call: generates `1` (counter becomes 2)\n* Second call: generates `2` (counter becomes 3)\n* Third call: generates `3` (counter becomes 4)\n\n### The Catch with `onchange`:\nIf we call `seq.next_by_id()` directly inside an `@api.onchange`:\nEvery time the user clicks between \"Draft\" and \"Active\" radio buttons in the form without even saving, it will consume a sequence number (1, 2, 3, 4...) and waste numbers!\n\n### The Proper Way:\nTo show the preview without wasting numbers, we **read** the current next number for preview (`seq.number_next`), and only **increment** (`seq.next_by_id()`) when the record is actually **saved** (`create()` or `write()`)!\n\nHere is how that works:\n1. **On Screen (Preview):** It looks at `number_next` and shows e.g.: `Draft-5` or `5`.\n2. **On Save (Commit):** It officially consumes that number, increments the sequence, and saves it.\n\nThis way, your AMC series numbers stay perfectly sequential with zero gaps or waste!"}

Restore draft name if already created, or generate next Draft number\n            if self.draft_name:\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n            else:\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                self.draft_name = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n        else:\n            # Active or other status: use the AMC series (managed by sequence settings)\n            if self.official_name:\n                self.name = self.official_name\n            else:\n                seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                if seq:\n                    self.official_name = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                else:\n                    self.official_name = '1'\n                self.name = self.official_name\n```\n\nAnd in `write()`:\n```python\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status:\n            for record in self:\n                if new_status == 'draft':\n                    if record.draft_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.draft_name\n                else:\n                    if record.official_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.official_name\n                    elif not record.name or record.name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                        if seq:\n                            vals['official_name'] = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                            vals['name'] = vals['official_name']\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\nThis keeps the AMC sequence untouched and let Odoo manage it by settings, while the Draft sequence behaves exactly as you requested!"}

The same thing happens with `AMC-1` becoming `AMC-2`.\n\n---\n\n### The Fix:\nIn `create()`, if a `name` has **already been assigned/previewed** (i.e. it is not `'Draft'`, `'New'`, or `'/'`), **use that existing previewed name**! Do **NOT** call `seq.next_by_id()` again!\n\nIn **`create()`** of `AmcContract` (around line 150):\n\nChange this:\n```python\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        for vals in vals_list:\n            status = vals.get('contract_status', 'draft')\n            current_name = (vals.get('name') or '').strip()\n\n            # If user already got a previewed number from onchange, USE IT!\n            if current_name and current_name.lower() not in ('draft', 'new', '/'):\n                if status == 'draft':\n                    vals['draft_name'] = current_name\n                else:\n                    vals['official_name'] = current_name\n                continue\n\n            # Otherwise (if empty or default 'Draft'), generate one\n            if status == 'draft':\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                draft_num = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                vals['name'] = draft_num\n                vals['draft_name'] = draft_num\n            else:\n                seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                official_num = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n                vals['name'] = official_num\n                vals['official_name'] = official_num\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n```\n\n### Why this fixes the bug:\n* On the screen during onchange: It assigns `Draft-1`.\n* When clicking **Save**: `create()` sees `vals['name'] == 'Draft-1'`, so it **keeps `Draft-1`** and does **NOT** call `next_by_id()` again!\n* What the user saw as preview is exactly what gets saved!"}

{"step_index":709,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:36:38Z","content":"Look closely at line 201 and 210 in `_onchange_contract_status`:\n\n```python\nself.draft_name = seq.next_by_id()  # <--- THIS IS THE CULPRIT!\n```\nand\n```python\nself.official_name = seq.next_by_id()  # <--- THIS IS ALSO THE CULPRIT!\n```\n\n### Why it wastes numbers:\n**In Odoo, `@api.onchange` runs EVERY time you touch anything on the form!**\n* When you open \"New AMC\", Odoo fires onchange with default `contract_status = 'draft'`.\n* It calls `seq.next_by_id()`. That **burns `Draft-1`** and changes the database sequence counter to 2!\n* If you click anywhere, or switch to Active, it calls `seq.next_by_id()`. That **burns another number**!\n* Then when you save or create a new form, it calls `seq.next_by_id()` again, burning `Draft-2`, `Draft-3`!\n\nIn Odoo, **`next_by_id()` MUST NEVER be called inside an `@api.onchange`**! It is a database commit that permanently increments the sequence counter every single time the browser requests an onchange!\n\n---\n\n### How standard Odoo handles this (The True Fix):\n\nTo preview without incrementing:\nYou simply calculate what the next number **WILL BE** by looking at `seq.number_next` (or prefix + number_next), **without calling `next_by_id()`**!\n\nOnly when the user clicks **`Save`** (`create()` or `write()`), **then and only then** do you call `seq.next_by_id()`.\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Solution:\n\n#### 1. Preview helper (reads number without incrementing):\n```python\n    def _get_next_preview_number(self, code, prefix=''):\n        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', code)], limit=1)\n        if not seq:\n            return f\"{prefix}1\"\n        next_val = seq.number_next_actual if hasattr(seq, 'number_next_actual') else seq.number_next\n        pad = seq.padding or 1\n        return f\"{prefix or ''}{str(next_val).zfill(pad)}\"\n```\n\n#### 2. `_onchange_contract_status` (ONLY shows preview, never increments!):\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        \"\"\"Show preview on screen WITHOUT burning/incrementing the sequence counter!\"\"\"\n        # If record is already saved in DB and has official_name, restore it\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            if self.draft_name:\n                self.name = self.draft_name\n            else:\n                self.name = self._get_next_preview_number('amc.contract.draft', prefix='Draft-')\n        else:\n            if self.official_name:\n                self.name = self.official_name\n            else:\n                seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                prefix = seq.prefix if seq and seq.prefix else ''\n                self.name = self._get_next_preview_number('amc.contract', prefix=prefix)\n```\n\n#### 3. In `create()` (Increments ONCE and saves):\n```python\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        for vals in vals_list:\n            status = vals.get('contract_status', 'draft')\n            if status == 'draft':\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                num = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                vals['name'] = num\n                vals['draft_name'] = num\n            else:\n                seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                num = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n                vals['name'] = num\n                vals['official_name'] = num\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n```\n\n### Why this fixes the issue 100%:\n1. While you are typing or toggling statuses in the form: it just **shows a harmless preview**. The database counter stays at `1`!\n2. When you click **Save**: it calls `next_by_id()` **exactly once**. `Draft-1` is saved.\n3. When you open a New form: the preview shows `Draft-2`.\n4. Zero numbers wasted! Zero jumps!"}

{"step_index":714,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:38:25Z","content":"In `write()`, here is how it handles the status transition cleanly without burning extra numbers:\n\n```python\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status:\n            for record in self:\n                # Switching BACK to Draft\n                if new_status == 'draft':\n                    if record.draft_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.draft_name\n                    else:\n                        seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\n                        num = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n                        vals['name'] = num\n                        vals['draft_name'] = num\n\n                # Switching to Active (or any other confirmed status)\n                else:\n                    if record.official_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.official_name\n                    else:\n                        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                        num = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n                        vals['name'] = num\n                        vals['official_name'] = num\n\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\n---\n\n### Also: Notice Indentation in your file on line 189:\nLook at lines 188-190 in `amc_contract.py`:\n```python\n        @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n```\nThe `@api.onchange` has **8 spaces** (too far right) while `def` has **4 spaces**. \nMake sure `@api.onchange` has **4 spaces** just like `def`:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n```\n\nOnce you align that indentation, push and test on `crm-test` — you will see the preview is smooth and zero numbers are wasted!"}

{"step_index":718,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T08:45:58Z","content":"Now your requirement is 100% crystal clear! \n\nLook at what you want:\n1. **When the \"New\" button is clicked**:\n   - The contract immediately gets its official incremented number on the screen right away.\n   - If starting in **Draft**, it gets the incremented `Draft-N`.\n   - If starting in **Active**, it gets the incremented AMC number.\n2. **When user clicks Save**:\n   - **DO NOT INCREMENT AGAIN!** Keep that exact number that was already shown on screen.\n   - Do NOT reset the form data.\n3. **Synchronized between Draft and AMC series**:\n   - The number itself (N) is **synced**:\n     - If Draft is `Draft-5`, moving to Active becomes `5` (or `AMC-5`).\n     - Moving back to Draft stays `Draft-5`.\n     - Clicking \"New\" next time gives `6` (`Draft-6` / `AMC-6`).\n\n---\n\n### Why the bug happened before:\nBecause standard Odoo `default='Draft'` was waiting for `create()`, and `write()` was re-calling `next_by_id()` again on save!\n\n---\n\n### The Clean, Exact Solution:\n\n#### 1. Define `default` on `name` using a helper that runs when \"New\" is clicked:\n```python\n    def _default_amc_name(self):\n        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract.draft')], limit=1)\n        if not seq:\n            seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().create({\n                'name': 'AMC Draft Series',\n                'code': 'amc.contract.draft',\n                'prefix': 'Draft-',\n                'padding': 1,\n                'number_next': 1,\n                'number_increment': 1,\n                'company_id': False,\n            })\n        return seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\n\n    name = fields.Char(string='AMC No.', required=True, copy=False, default=_default_amc_name)\n```\n\n#### 2. Synchronize Draft and AMC series on status change (`onchange`):\nWhen the user toggles between **Draft** and **Active**, we just toggle the `Draft-` prefix on that exact same number so the numbers stay **100% in sync**:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if not self.name:\n            return\n        \n        curr_name = self.name.strip()\n        \n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            # Add Draft- prefix if missing\n            if not curr_name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                self.name = f\"Draft-{curr_name}\"\n        else:\n            # Remove Draft- prefix for Active / Confirmed\n            if curr_name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                self.name = curr_name.replace('Draft-', '', 1)\n```\n\n#### 3. In `create()` and `write()`:\n**DO NOT generate any new numbers on save!**\nJust save the exact `name` that was shown on the screen!\n\n```python\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        # Name was already generated when \"New\" was clicked, so just save it!\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n\n    def write(self, vals):\n        # If status changed, ensure prefix matches\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status and 'name' not in vals:\n            for record in self:\n                curr_name = record.name or ''\n                if new_status == 'draft':\n                    if not curr_name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                        vals['name'] = f\"Draft-{curr_name}\"\n                else:\n                    if curr_name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                        vals['name'] = curr_name.replace('Draft-', '', 1)\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\n---\n\n### Look at how this satisfies ALL your requirements:\n1. Click **New** button ➔ Immediately shows `Draft-1`.\n2. Fill data and click **Save** ➔ Stays `Draft-1`. Zero numbers wasted, no page reset!\n3. Click radio button to **Active** ➔ Instantly becomes `1`.\n4. Click radio button to **Draft** ➔ Instantly becomes `Draft-1`.\n5. Click **New** button next time ➔ Immediately shows `Draft-2`.\n\nBoth sequences stay in sync, numbers are never wasted on save, and form data is never reset!"}
