{"step_index":730,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T09:44:44Z","content":"Because in lines 166 and 199 it was just doing:\n```python\nself.name = curr_name.replace('Draft-', '', 1)\n```\nwhich removed `Draft-` and left only the raw number! \n\nIf your official AMC series has its own prefix (like `AMC-` or whatever prefix is configured in Odoo Settings under Sequence for `amc.contract`), it didn't put that AMC prefix on!\n\n### To keep the AMC series prefix properly:\n\nLook at the sequence for `amc.contract`:\nWhen switching from Draft to Active, we read the official AMC sequence prefix (e.g. `AMC-`):\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if not self.name:\n            return\n        \n        curr_name = self.name.strip()\n        \n        # Get AMC official prefix from sequence settings (e.g. \"AMC-\")\n        amc_seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n        amc_prefix = amc_seq.prefix if amc_seq and amc_seq.prefix else ''\n        \n        # Extract the pure number part (stripping Draft- or AMC prefix)\n        clean_num = curr_name.replace('Draft-', '', 1)\n        if amc_prefix and clean_num.startswith(amc_prefix):\n            clean_num = clean_num.replace(amc_prefix, '', 1)\n\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            # In Draft: Show Draft- + number (e.g. \"Draft-1\")\n            self.name = f\"Draft-{clean_num}\"\n        else:\n            # In Active / Other: Show AMC prefix + number (e.g. \"AMC-1\")\n            self.name = f\"{amc_prefix}{clean_num}\"\n```\n\nAnd in `write()`:\n```python\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status and 'name' not in vals:\n            for record in self:\n                curr_name = record.name or ''\n                amc_seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                amc_prefix = amc_seq.prefix if amc_seq and amc_seq.prefix else ''\n\n                clean_num = curr_name.replace('Draft-', '', 1)\n                if amc_prefix and clean_num.startswith(amc_prefix):\n                    clean_num = clean_num.replace(amc_prefix, '', 1)\n\n                if new_status == 'draft':\n                    vals['name'] = f\"Draft-{clean_num}\"\n                else:\n                    vals['name'] = f\"{amc_prefix}{clean_num}\"\n\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\n### Also, please clean up lines 169-183 in `amc_contract.py`:\nOn lines 169-183, you still have `_default_amc_name` and a duplicate `name = fields.Char(...)`. You can delete lines 169 to 184 completely because line 10 already has `name = fields.Char(...)` with `default`.\n\nOnce that is done:\n- Draft stage: always shows **`Draft-1`** (with `Draft-` prefix).\n- Active stage: always shows **`AMC-1`** (with the official sequence prefix).\n- Switching between them keeps both prefixes perfectly!"}

{"step_index":740,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T09:55:08Z","content":"Here is the complete, exact code to implement this workflow.\n\n---\n\n### Logic Summary:\n1. **In Service Ticket Wizard**:\n   * Add `has_amc` (boolean flag) and `amc_id` (Many2one to `amc.contract`).\n   * When `partner_id` or `equipment_id` is selected:\n     - Search for Active AMC contracts for that customer (and optionally matching that equipment).\n     - **If 0 AMC**: `has_amc = False` ➔ Field stays completely hidden!\n     - **If exactly 1 AMC**: `has_amc = True` ➔ Automatically selects that AMC contract directly.\n     - **If > 1 AMC**: `has_amc = True` ➔ `amc_id` remains open so user can pick from the filtered dropdown.\n   * When the ticket is created from the wizard, `amc_id` passes to the final `service.ticket`.\n\n---\n\n### 1. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/models/service_ticket.py`\nAdd `amc_id` to the `service.ticket` model (around line 20, right below `equipment_id`):\n\n```python\n    amc_id = fields.Many2one('amc.contract', string='AMC Contract', tracking=True)\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/service_ticket_wizard.py`\n\n#### A. Add fields to `ServiceTicketWizard` (around line 16, below `equipment_id`):\n```python\n    has_amc = fields.Boolean(string='Has AMC', default=False)\n    amc_id = fields.Many2one(\n        'amc.contract', \n        string='AMC Contract',\n        domain=\"['|', ('partner_id', '=', partner_id), ('partner_id.parent_id', '=', partner_id)]\"\n    )\n```\n\n#### B. In `_onchange_partner_id` / `_onchange_equipment_id` (or add onchange):\n```python\n    @api.onchange('partner_id', 'equipment_id')\n    def _onchange_partner_amc(self):\n        if not self.partner_id:\n            self.has_amc = False\n            self.amc_id = False\n            return\n\n        # Find active AMCs for this customer or parent company\n        domain = [\n            ('contract_status', '=', 'active'),\n            '|', ('partner_id', '=', self.partner_id.id), ('partner_id', '=', self.partner_id.parent_id.id if self.partner_id.parent_id else self.partner_id.id)\n        ]\n        \n        # If equipment is selected, prioritize AMCs that actually cover this equipment\n        if self.equipment_id:\n            eq_amcs = self.env['amc.contract'].search(domain + [('line_ids.equipment_id', '=', self.equipment_id.id)])\n            amcs = eq_amcs if eq_amcs else self.env['amc.contract'].search(domain)\n        else:\n            amcs = self.env['amc.contract'].search(domain)\n\n        if not amcs:\n            self.has_amc = False\n            self.amc_id = False\n        elif len(amcs) == 1:\n            self.has_amc = True\n            self.amc_id = amcs[0].id\n        else:\n            self.has_amc = True\n            self.amc_id = False  # Let user select from dropdown\n```\n\n#### C. In `action_create_ticket()` of `service_ticket_wizard.py`:\nIn the `ticket_vals` dictionary that creates the ticket, pass `amc_id`:\n```python\n    'amc_id': self.amc_id.id if self.amc_id else False,\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/views/service_ticket_wizard_views.xml`\nIn Section 1 (around line 33, right below `equipment_id`):\n\nAdd:\n```xml\n<field name=\"has_amc\" invisible=\"1\"/>\n<field name=\"amc_id\" \n       string=\"AMC Contract\" \n       options=\"{'no_create': True}\" \n       invisible=\"not has_amc\"\n       placeholder=\"Select AMC Contract...\"/>\n```\n\n---\n\n### 4. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/views/service_ticket_views.xml`\nOn the main Service Ticket form view (under Equipment Details, below `equipment_id` on line 51):\n\nAdd:\n```xml\n<field name=\"amc_id\" options=\"{'no_create': True}\" invisible=\"not amc_id\"/>\n```\n\n---\n\n### What this gives you:\n1. If the customer has **NO AMC** ➔ Nothing is shown (field is completely hidden).\n2. If the customer has **1 AMC** ➔ It instantly auto-populates that AMC contract!\n3. If the customer has **more than 1 AMC** ➔ The dropdown appears and lets the user choose between them!\n4. Saved cleanly on the final service ticket!"}

{"step_index":758,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:13:12Z","content":"In **`service_ticket_wizard.py`**, inside method **`action_save_ticket`** (around line 294), right after `'equipment_id'`:\n\n```python\n            'equipment_id': self.equipment_id.id if self.equipment_id else False,\n            'amc_id': self.amc_id.id if self.amc_id else False,\n            'site_name': self.site_name,\n```\n\n---\n\n### Also: One very important fix in `_onchange_partner_id`!\nLook at lines 123-125 in `service_ticket_wizard.py` right now:\n```python\nreturn {'domain': {'equipment_id': [('partner_id', 'in', [p.id, company_partner.id])]}}\n            \n# Check Active AMC for this partner\namcs = self.env['amc.contract'].search(...)\n```\nNotice that `return` is written **BEFORE** the AMC check!\nBecause `return` came first, Python exited the function immediately and **never reached the AMC code**!\n\nMove `return {'domain': ...}` to the very end of `_onchange_partner_id`:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('partner_id')\n    def _onchange_partner_id(self):\n        if self.partner_id:\n            p = self.partner_id\n            company_partner = p.parent_id if p.parent_id else p\n\n            self.contact_person = p.name\n            self.contact_number = getattr(p, 'phone', False) or getattr(p, 'mobile', False) or False\n            self.email = getattr(p, 'email', False) or False\n            self.site_name = getattr(p, 'x_site_name', False) or getattr(company_partner, 'x_site_name', False) or False\n\n            # Equipment domain & auto-fill\n            equipments = self.env['equipment.master'].search([\n                ('partner_id', 'in', [p.id, company_partner.id])\n            ])\n            if len(equipments) == 1:\n                eq = equipments[0]\n                self.equipment_id = eq\n                self.site_name = eq.site_name or self.site_name\n                self.contact_person = eq.contact_person or self.contact_person\n                self.contact_number = eq.contact_number or self.contact_number\n                self.email = eq.email or self.email\n                self.model_number = eq.model_number\n                self.serial_number = eq.serial_number\n                self.part_number = eq.part_number\n            else:\n                if self.equipment_id and self.equipment_id.partner_id not in (p, company_partner):\n                    self.equipment_id = False\n                    self.model_number = False\n                    self.serial_number = False\n                    self.part_number = False\n\n            # Check Active AMC for this partner\n            amcs = self.env['amc.contract'].search([\n                ('contract_status', '=', 'active'),\n                '|', ('partner_id', '=', p.id), ('partner_id', '=', company_partner.id)\n            ])\n            if not amcs:\n                self.has_amc = False\n                self.amc_id = False\n            elif len(amcs) == 1:\n                self.has_amc = True\n                self.amc_id = amcs[0].id\n            else:\n                self.has_amc = True\n                self.amc_id = False\n\n            return {'domain': {'equipment_id': [('partner_id', 'in', [p.id, company_partner.id])]}}\n        \n        self.has_amc = False\n        self.amc_id = False\n        return {'domain': {'equipment_id': []}}\n```\n\nThis ensures both the AMC check runs and `'amc_id'` is saved on ticket creation!"}
{"step_index":765,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:19:04Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\ngood now also bug in amc sync good but also wastage draft when i clickc cancel as well as amc series number also wastage serie not cintine when the stop amc also take number that draft take \n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-18T15:49:04+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\wizard\\service_ticket_wizard.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\nCursor is on line: 1\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\wizard\\service_ticket_wizard.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\views\\service_ticket_wizard_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\views\\service_ticket_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\service_ticket.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":766,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:19:04Z","content":"Look at lines 13-15 in `amc_contract.py`:\n\n```python\nname = fields.Char(\n    string='AMC No.', \n    required=True, \n    copy=False, \n    default=lambda self: self.env['ir.sequence'].next_by_code('amc.contract.draft') or 'Draft-1'\n)\n```\n\n### Why clicking \"Cancel\" (or just opening the form and leaving) wastes a number:\nIn Odoo, **`default=...` is evaluated the exact second you click the \"New\" button!**\n* When you click \"New\", Odoo runs `next_by_code('amc.contract.draft')`. That permanently burns `Draft-1` in PostgreSQL.\n* If you click **\"Cancel\"** or close the browser tab without saving, that number is **gone forever**, so the next contract gets `Draft-2`!\n\nAnd similarly:\n* If an AMC series number was generated and you cancel or stop, that number was also consumed.\n\n---\n\n### The Standard Odoo Solution for Zero Wastage:\nIn standard Odoo (Sales, Invoices, Purchase Orders), how does Odoo avoid wasting numbers on Cancel?\n\n1. **Default is always `Draft` (or `New`)** — **NEVER call `next_by_code()` in `default=`!**\n   ```python\n   name = fields.Char(string='AMC No.', required=True, copy=False, readonly=True, default='Draft')\n   ```\n2. **Only consume the sequence inside `create()` when the user actually clicks SAVE!**\n   * If user clicks \"Cancel\" or leaves ➔ `create()` NEVER runs ➔ **Zero numbers consumed! Zero waste!**\n3. **Draft sequence & AMC series separation**:\n   * If saved in **Draft**: consumes next `Draft-` sequence.\n   * If saved or confirmed to **Active**: consumes next official `amc.contract` sequence.\n   * If cancelled: no sequence was ever burned!\n\n---\n\n### The Code Fix in `amc_contract.py`:\n\n#### 1. In field definition (line 10):\n```python\n    name = fields.Char(string='AMC No.', required=True, copy=False, default='Draft')\n```\n\n#### 2. In `create()`:\n```python\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        for vals in vals_list:\n            status = vals.get('contract_status', 'draft')\n            current_name = (vals.get('name') or '').strip()\n\n            # Only generate when creating for the first time\n            if not current_name or current_name.lower() in ('draft', 'new', '/'):\n                if status == 'draft':\n                    seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract.draft')], limit=1)\n                    vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() if seq else 'Draft-1'\n                    vals['draft_name'] = vals['name']\n                else:\n                    seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                    vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n                    vals['official_name'] = vals['name']\n\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n```\n\n#### 3. In `write()` (when moving an existing saved contract from Draft to Active):\n```python\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status:\n            for record in self:\n                # If moving to Active and never had an official AMC number yet\n                if new_status != 'draft':\n                    if record.official_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.official_name\n                    elif not record.name or record.name.startswith('Draft-'):\n                        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                        if seq:\n                            vals['official_name'] = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                            vals['name'] = vals['official_name']\n                # If moving back to Draft\n                elif new_status == 'draft':\n                    if record.draft_name:\n                        vals['name'] = record.draft_name\n\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\n### Result:\n- Click **\"New\"** ➔ shows `Draft` (no sequence touched).\n- Click **\"Cancel\"** ➔ **No number wasted!**\n- Click **\"Save\"** ➔ Consumes next sequence number cleanly and permanently."}

{"step_index":768,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:19:46Z","content":"That is SO MUCH SIMPLER, cleaner, and 100% standard Odoo!\n\n### The Simple Logic:\n1. When in **Draft**: The `AMC No.` is simply **`Draft`** (no numbering at all!).\n2. If you click **\"Cancel\"**: Nothing is wasted because it's just the word `Draft`!\n3. Only when moved to **Active** (or confirmed): It generates the next official number from the **AMC series** (`AMC-1`, `AMC-2`, `AMC-3`...), working 100% independently!\n4. If moved back to **Draft**: It shows **`Draft`**.\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Code for `amc_contract.py`:\n\n#### 1. In field definition (line 10):\n```python\n    name = fields.Char(string='AMC No.', required=True, copy=False, default='Draft')\n```\n\n#### 2. In `create()`:\n```python\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        for vals in vals_list:\n            status = vals.get('contract_status', 'draft')\n            # If created directly in Active, generate AMC number; otherwise keep 'Draft'\n            if status != 'draft':\n                seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n            else:\n                vals['name'] = 'Draft'\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n```\n\n#### 3. In `write()`:\n```python\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status:\n            for record in self:\n                # If moving from Draft to Active, generate official AMC sequence\n                if new_status != 'draft' and (not record.name or record.name == 'Draft'):\n                    seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n                    vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n                # If moving back to Draft\n                elif new_status == 'draft':\n                    vals['name'] = 'Draft'\n        return super().write(vals)\n```\n\n#### 4. In `_onchange_contract_status()`:\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            self.name = 'Draft'\n        else:\n            # If already has an assigned official number in DB, keep it; else preview next AMC number\n            if self.name and self.name != 'Draft':\n                return\n            seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n            prefix = seq.prefix if seq and seq.prefix else ''\n            next_val = seq.number_next_actual if hasattr(seq, 'number_next_actual') else (seq.number_next or 1)\n            pad = seq.padding or 1\n            self.name = f\"{prefix}{str(next_val).zfill(pad)}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Why this is perfect:\n* **Zero wasted numbers**: Draft has no numbers, so clicking Cancel, closing the browser, or editing drafts never touches the sequence.\n* **AMC series is 100% independent**: Every confirmed AMC gets continuous, beautiful numbering (`AMC-1`, `AMC-2`, `AMC-3`...).\n* **Clean & simple**: Removes all complex draft sequence logic."}

It is 100% linked with the Sequence Settings!**\n\nHere is proof directly from your codebase:\n\n1. **In `amc_contract.py`**:\n   Whenever a contract is created or moved to Active, it calls:\n   ```python\n   seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n   vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id()\n   ```\n   This looks up the sequence whose Code is **`amc.contract`**.\n\n2. **In Sequence Settings UI**:\n   * If you go to **Settings ➔ Technical ➔ Sequences** (or your Series Settings), you will find the sequence with code **`amc.contract`** (named *\"AMC Numbering Series\"*).\n   * Whatever you set there:\n     - **Prefix** (e.g. `AMC/` or `AMC-` or empty)\n     - **Padding** (e.g. `0001` or `1`)\n     - **Next Number** (e.g. `1`, `100`, etc.)\n   * In [amc_contract_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/amc_contract_views.xml#L148-L157), lines 148–157 specifically customize this sequence view for `code == 'amc.contract'`.\n\nSo any change you make to the sequence in Series Settings directly controls how the AMC number generates!"}
{"step_index":794,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:28:41Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\nwhat if sereis setting nto create prefic or sequence?\n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-18T15:58:41+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\amc_contract.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\nCursor is on line: 131\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\amc_contract.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":795,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:28:42Z","content":"Great question!\n\nIf someone hasn't created the sequence yet in Settings, or if it doesn't exist, line 136 right now has a fallback:\n```python\nvals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() if seq else '1'\n```\nIt would just return `'1'` every time and never increment!\n\n---\n\n### How to ensure it ALWAYS exists automatically (even if nobody created it in Settings):\n\nWe can write a simple helper right before `create()`:\nIf the sequence `amc.contract` doesn't exist in the database, it **auto-creates the default sequence row** with Code `amc.contract`!\n\n```python\n    def _get_amc_sequence(self):\n        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n        if not seq:\n            seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().create({\n                'name': 'AMC Numbering Series',\n                'code': 'amc.contract',\n                'prefix': False,\n                'padding': 1,\n                'number_next': 1,\n                'number_increment': 1,\n                'company_id': False,\n            })\n        return seq\n```\n\nThen in `create()`, `write()`, and `_onchange_contract_status()`:\n```python\nseq = self._get_amc_sequence()\nvals['name'] = seq.next_by_id()\n```\n\n### Why this is 100% safe:\n1. **If the user already configured the sequence in Settings**: It simply finds and uses their sequence with their custom prefix/padding!\n2. **If the user NEVER touched Settings (fresh database)**: It automatically creates the sequence starting at 1, so it **NEVER fails, NEVER crashes, and ALWAYS increments**!"}
{"step_index":797,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:29:48Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\ngive proper code \n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-18T15:59:48+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\amc_contract.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\nCursor is on line: 136\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\amc_contract.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":798,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T10:29:49Z","content":"Here is the complete, proper code for lines 128 onwards in `amc_contract.py`:\n\n```python\n    @api.model\n    def _get_amc_sequence(self):\n        \"\"\"Finds existing AMC sequence from Series Settings or auto-creates default one.\"\"\"\n        seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().search([('code', '=', 'amc.contract')], limit=1)\n        if not seq:\n            seq = self.env['ir.sequence'].sudo().create({\n                'name': 'AMC Numbering Series',\n                'code': 'amc.contract',\n                'prefix': False,\n                'padding': 1,\n                'number_next': 1,\n                'number_increment': 1,\n                'company_id': False,\n            })\n        return seq\n\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        for vals in vals_list:\n            status = vals.get('contract_status', 'draft')\n            # If created directly in Active, generate AMC number; otherwise keep 'Draft'\n            if status != 'draft':\n                seq = self._get_amc_sequence()\n                vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n            else:\n                vals['name'] = 'Draft'\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n\n    def write(self, vals):\n        new_status = vals.get('contract_status')\n        if new_status:\n            for record in self:\n                # If moving from Draft to Active, generate official AMC sequence\n                if new_status != 'draft' and (not record.name or record.name == 'Draft'):\n                    seq = self._get_amc_sequence()\n                    vals['name'] = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\n                # If moving back to Draft\n                elif new_status == 'draft':\n                    vals['name'] = 'Draft'\n        return super().write(vals)\n\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\n            self.name = 'Draft'\n        else:\n            # If already has an assigned official number in DB, keep it; else preview next AMC number\n            if self.name and self.name != 'Draft':\n                return\n            seq = self._get_amc_sequence()\n            prefix = seq.prefix if seq.prefix else ''\n            next_val = seq.number_next_actual if hasattr(seq, 'number_next_actual') else (seq.number_next or 1)\n            pad = seq.padding or 1\n            self.name = f\"{prefix}{str(next_val).zfill(pad)}\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### Why this is 100% robust:\n1. **Settings integration**: If an admin sets prefix/padding in Series Settings, it immediately uses that.\n2. **Auto-fallback**: If no sequence has been created in Settings yet, `_get_amc_sequence()` automatically creates the default one in the database starting from 1.\n3. **No hard-crashes**: Even on a fresh, unconfigured database, it will always increment cleanly!"}

{"step_index":865,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:06:58Z","content":"Look at lines 158–159 in `equipment_master_wizard.py`! I found the **exact bug**:\n\n```python\nif seq:\n    self.equipment_id = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n```\n\n### Why it disappeared when you selected a product:\n1. `equipment_id` is a **`fields.Selection`** (a fixed dropdown of options!).\n2. In Odoo, a `fields.Selection` **can ONLY accept values that exist in its `selection` list!**\n3. When you selected the product *\"1000 mL Fiberlite...\"*:\n   - Its product category has a sequence that computed a preview (e.g. `CENTRI-1` or `WPS-0060`).\n   - If that value was slightly different or not formatted with the exact same string key in the selection list `_get_equipment_id_selection()`, **Odoo's OWL frontend rejects the value and blanks out the field!**\n   - That's why the field suddenly became completely empty!\n\n---\n\n### And why default did not show on \"New Equipment\":\nIn `default_get()` or `default=...`:\n`_default_equipment_id()` was returning a string that wasn't matching the active Selection options at render time.\n\n---\n\n### The Permanent Fix (Never Blank Out Again):\n\nIn `equipment_master_wizard.py`:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange(\"name\")\n    def _onchange_name(self):\n        if self.name:\n            categ = self.name.categ_id\n            self.category_id = categ.name if categ else \"\"\n            self.manufacturer = getattr(self.name, \"x_make\", \"\") or \"\"\n            self.part_number = getattr(self.name, \"default_code\", \"\") or \"\"\n\n            # Priority 1: Category sequence\n            seq = False\n            if categ:\n                seq = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n                    (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n                    (\"equipment_category_id\", \"=\", categ.id),\n                    (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n                ], limit=1)\n\n            # Priority 2: General sequence\n            if not seq:\n                seq = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n                    (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n                    (\"equipment_category_id\", \"=\", False),\n                    (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n                ], limit=1)\n\n            if seq:\n                preview = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n                # Check if this preview exists in selection options; if so, select it!\n                opts = [opt[0] for opt in self._get_equipment_id_selection()]\n                if preview in opts:\n                    self.equipment_id = preview\n                elif opts:\n                    self.equipment_id = opts[0]\n```\n\nAnd in `default_get()`:\n```python\n    @api.model\n    def default_get(self, fields_list):\n        res = super().default_get(fields_list)\n        opts = self._get_equipment_id_selection()\n        if opts and 'equipment_id' in fields_list:\n            res['equipment_id'] = opts[0][0]\n        return res\n```\n\n### Why this fixes both problems completely:\n1. **On New Equipment**: It will **ALWAYS** select the first available sequence (`WPS-0060`) by default — it will never be blank!\n2. **On Product Selection**: It matches the category sequence against the valid dropdown options and sets it safely — it will **NEVER disappear or blank out**!"}

Keep your existing `default_get` in `equipment_master_wizard.py` (around line 110):\n```python\n    @api.model\n    def default_get(self, fields_list):\n        res = super().default_get(fields_list)\n        # Ensure equipment_id gets a valid option from the dropdown options\n        opts = self._get_equipment_id_selection()\n        if opts and ('equipment_id' in fields_list or not res.get('equipment_id')):\n            res['equipment_id'] = opts[0][0]\n        return res\n```\n\n#### 2. Update `_onchange_name` in `equipment_master_wizard.py` (around line 133):\n```python\n    @api.onchange(\"name\")\n    def _onchange_name(self):\n        if self.name:\n            categ = self.name.categ_id\n            self.category_id = categ.name if categ else \"\"\n            self.manufacturer = getattr(self.name, \"x_make\", \"\") or \"\"\n            self.part_number = getattr(self.name, \"default_code\", \"\") or \"\"\n\n            # Priority 1: Category sequence\n            seq = False\n            if categ:\n                seq = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n                    (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n                    (\"equipment_category_id\", \"=\", categ.id),\n                    (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n                ], limit=1)\n\n            # Priority 2: General sequence\n            if not seq:\n                seq = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n                    (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n                    (\"equipment_category_id\", \"=\", False),\n                    (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n                ], limit=1)\n\n            if seq:\n                preview = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n                opts = [opt[0] for opt in self._get_equipment_id_selection()]\n                # If category sequence is in options, pick it!\n                if preview in opts:\n                    self.equipment_id = preview\n                elif opts:\n                    # Otherwise keep the first option instead of blanking out!\n                    self.equipment_id = opts[0]\n```\n\n### Why it was blanking out before:\nWhen you selected the bottle product, `_compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)` generated a string that wasn't in the selection list. In Odoo Web Client, selecting a value not in `fields.Selection` clears the input box completely!\nBy making sure it falls back to `opts[0]` (`WPS-0060`), the field **never disappears and never becomes empty**!"}

{"step_index":877,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:10:21Z","content":"Here is the exact explanation of why this happened on **Production** and not on **Testing**:\n\n---\n\n### The Reason: Different Data in the Databases!\n\n1. **In Testing Database (`crm_data_test`)**:\n   * In testing, only **1 sequence** existed (`WPS-`).\n   * When `_get_equipment_id_selection()` ran, it generated `[('WPS-0060', 'WPS-0060')]`.\n   * When you selected any product in Testing, it searched for category sequences, found none, fell back to General (`WPS-`), and set `self.equipment_id = 'WPS-0060'`.\n   * Because `'WPS-0060'` was the **exact same string** in the dropdown options list, Odoo displayed it happily!\n\n2. **In Production Database (`crm_data`)**:\n   * Look at your 3rd screenshot from Production:\n     The dropdown has **TWO** sequences:\n     - **`WPS-0060`**\n     - **`CENTRI-1`** (a category-specific sequence for Centrifuges!)\n   * On Production, you selected the product:\n     *`\"1000 mL Fiberlite™ PPCO High Performance Bottle...\"`*\n   * In Production, this product's Category is linked to a sequence that computed a value that **did not match the exact pre-rendered dropdown keys** in the user's browser session cache.\n   * **In Odoo's web client (OWL Framework)**:\n     If a Python `@api.onchange` sends `{'value': {'equipment_id': 'XYZ'}}`, but `'XYZ'` is not in the browser's current dropdown `<select>` options list, the browser **automatically clears the field to empty/blank**!\n\n---\n\n### How the fix solved it:\nWith the change we just made:\n```python\nopts = [opt[0] for opt in self._get_equipment_id_selection()]\nif preview in opts:\n    self.equipment_id = preview\nelif opts:\n    self.equipment_id = opts[0]\n```\nNow, before Python sends the value to the browser, it verifies that the value **strictly exists** in the browser's options list (`opts`). \n\nIf it exists, it picks it; if not, it keeps the first option (`WPS-0060`). **It will never send an invalid value that causes the browser to clear and disappear!**"}

{"step_index":881,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:11:39Z","content":"AHA! Look at your screenshot from Settings!\n\nIn Settings, the sequences are:\n1. **`BSC-`** (Category: Bio Safety Cabinets)\n2. **`EID-`** (Category: Empty / General)\n\nNow look at your other screenshot of the dropdown on screen:\nIt was showing:\n- **`WPS-0060`**\n- **`CENTRI-1`**\n\n### WHY?\nThe browser had **OLD CACHED options** from when the sequence was `WPS-` and `CENTRI-`!\nWhen you selected the product:\n- Python ran on the server and generated **`BSC-0004`** or **`EID-0006`**!\n- It returned **`BSC-0004`** to the browser.\n- BUT the browser's dropdown still only knew about `WPS-0060` and `CENTRI-1`!\n- The browser said: *\"I don't know what `BSC-0004` is, so I will clear the field and show blank!\"*\n\n---\n\n### Why does a `fields.Selection` cause this nightmare?\nIn Odoo, **`fields.Selection` options are cached by the browser when the web client loads**. \nWhenever someone changes sequence prefixes or adds new series in Settings, the browser's Selection cache does NOT automatically update unless the user does a hard reload or Odoo updates the field!\n\n### The True Odoo Solution so it NEVER breaks:\nChange `equipment_id` to a standard string/char field with a simple **datalist / widget**, OR ensure that whenever `name` or `default_get` runs:\nIf `equipment_id` is a `fields.Selection`, **the selection function must dynamically include the current value!**\n\nLook at line 123 of `equipment_master_wizard.py`:\n```python\n    def _get_equipment_id_selection(self):\n        options = []\n        seqs = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n            (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n            (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n        ], order=\"equipment_category_id desc, id desc\")\n\n        for seq in seqs:\n            preview = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n            label = preview\n            if (preview, label) not in options:\n                options.append((preview, label))\n\n        # Always make sure the currently selected/computed value is in options!\n        if hasattr(self, 'equipment_id') and self.equipment_id:\n            curr = self.equipment_id\n            if curr not in [opt[0] for opt in options]:\n                options.insert(0, (curr, curr))\n\n        if not options:\n            options = [(\"New\", \"New\")]\n        return options\n```\n\n### What this guarantees:\nWhatever sequence exists in Settings (whether `BSC-`, `EID-`, or any new series the client creates), the dropdown **will always dynamically include that exact value**, so the browser will **never** reject it and **never** blank it out!"}

{"step_index":891,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:13:49Z","content":"Look at the code on Production versus Testing!\n\nThe reason it works on Testing and NOT on Production is right here:\nOn Production, the code was **never updated with the latest wizard logic** (`e71c4ee`), OR Production database still had `WPS-` and `CENTRI-` registered in its `ir.model.fields.selection` table!\n\nLook at what happened on Production:\n1. When you opened the wizard on Production:\n   `default_get()` ran the OLD version:\n   ```python\n   res[\"equipment_id\"] = self._default_equipment_id()\n   ```\n   `_default_equipment_id()` computed `EID-0006` or `WPS-0060`.\n2. But in the browser on Production:\n   The dropdown only contained `WPS-0060` and `CENTRI-1`!\n3. When you selected the product:\n   `_onchange_name` ran and computed a category ID that wasn't in `WPS-0060` or `CENTRI-1`, so the browser blanked it out!\n\n---\n\n### The Permanent, 100% Reliable Fix for Production:\nInstead of relying on browser dropdown caches with `fields.Selection`, we make `equipment_id` a normal string field with a selection dropdown widget, OR we make sure `_get_equipment_id_selection` on the server returns **ALL active sequences in that database**!\n\nLook at lines 104-128 in `equipment_master_wizard.py`:\n```python\n    def _get_equipment_id_selection(self):\n        \"\"\"Dynamic dropdown options for equipment_id directly.\"\"\"\n        options = []\n        seqs = self.env[\"ir.sequence\"].sudo().search([\n            (\"code\", \"=\", \"crm.equipment.id\"),\n            (\"active\", \"=\", True)\n        ], order=\"equipment_category_id desc, id desc\")\n\n        for seq in seqs:\n            preview = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n            label = f\"{preview} ({seq.equipment_category_id.name})\" if seq.equipment_category_id else f\"{preview} (General)\"\n            if (preview, label) not in options:\n                options.append((preview, label))\n\n        if not options:\n            options = [(\"New\", \"New\")]\n        return options\n```\n\nAnd in `_onchange_name`:\n```python\n            if seq:\n                preview = self._compute_preview_for_sequence(seq)\n                self.equipment_id = preview\n```\n\n### Why will this work on Production?\nOnce we push this clean code to Production and run:\n`sudo systemctl restart crm`\nThe production server will re-read the production database sequences (`BSC-`, `EID-`), populate the dropdown with the real production sequences, and it will **never disappear again**!"}

In `amc_contract.py`:\n`pm` and `cm` (`Breakdown`) are currently defined as `fields.Char`:\n```python\npm = fields.Char(string='PM')\ncm = fields.Char(string='Breakdown')\n```\nBecause they are `fields.Char`, users can enter `\"4\"` or `\"2\"`. We can safely parse them with `int(amc.pm or 0)` and `int(amc.cm or 0)`!\n\n---\n\n### 2. In `service_ticket.py`:\nWe add a field to record the visit sequence number (e.g. Visit #1, Visit #2):\n```python\nvisit_number = fields.Integer(string='Visit Number', default=1, tracking=True)\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. In `service_ticket_wizard.py` (during ticket creation):\nWhen the user selects **PM** or **Breakdown** and an **AMC Contract** is linked:\n\n1. **Check remaining quota:**\n   * If `complaint_type == 'pm'`:\n     - Current remaining = `int(amc.pm or 0)`\n     - If remaining <= 0:\n       👉 Raise warning/error: **`\"Warning: This AMC Contract has 0 remaining PM visits! You cannot create more PM tickets for this contract.\"`**\n   * If `complaint_type == 'breakdown'`:\n     - Current remaining = `int(amc.cm or 0)`\n     - If remaining <= 0:\n       👉 Raise warning/error: **`\"Warning: This AMC Contract has 0 remaining Breakdown visits! You cannot create more Breakdown tickets for this contract.\"`**\n\n2. **Deduct 1 from the selected quota:**\n   * If `complaint_type == 'pm'`:\n     - New PM = remaining - 1\n     - Update AMC: `amc.sudo().write({'pm': str(new_pm)})`\n   * If `complaint_type == 'breakdown'`:\n     - New Breakdown = remaining - 1\n     - Update AMC: `amc.sudo().write({'cm': str(new_cm)})`\n\n3. **Calculate and Assign Visit Number (1, 2, 3...):**\n   * Count how many existing service tickets have been created for this `amc_id` with that same `complaint_type`:\n     ```python\n     past_tickets = self.env['service.ticket'].sudo().search_count([\n         ('amc_id', '=', amc.id),\n         ('complaint_type', '=', self.complaint_type)\n     ])\n     visit_num = past_tickets + 1  # 1 for first, 2 for second, etc.\n     ```\n   * Set `'visit_number': visit_num` on the created service ticket!\n\n---\n\n### Also on the Service Ticket Form:\nWe can display **`Visit Number`** on the form next to Complaint Type so engineers and clients see:\n`Visit Number: 1` (or 2, 3, etc.)!\n\nWhenever you are ready, I will give you the exact code to add!"}

{"step_index":903,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:28:53Z","content":"You are so right! The browser's default up/down spinner arrows on number fields are annoying, small, and cause accidental clicks.\n\nHere are the **3 best solutions** to make this smooth and headache-free for users:\n\n---\n\n### Solution 1: Use `fields.Char` (Clean text box, No Spinner Arrows!) — ⭐ **RECOMMENDED**\n* Define the field as a normal `fields.Char` (or `readonly=\"1\"`):\n  ```python\n  visit_number = fields.Char(string='Visit Number', readonly=True)\n  ```\n* **Why it's great:**\n  - Zero arrows/spinners!\n  - It displays cleanly as text: **`1`**, **`2`**, **`3`** (or even **`Visit #1`**, **`Visit #2`**).\n  - Users don't have to touch it or fight with arrows because the system automatically calculates it!\n\n---\n\n### Solution 2: If using Integer, hide the spinner arrows with standard CSS\nIf you prefer keeping an integer in the database, you simply add CSS so the browser completely hides the up/down arrows:\n```css\n/* Removes ugly number spinner up/down arrows */\ninput[type=number]::-webkit-inner-spin-button, \ninput[type=number]::-webkit-outer-spin-button { \n    -webkit-appearance: none; \n    margin: 0; \n}\ninput[type=number] {\n    -moz-appearance: textfield;\n}\n```\n* **Result:** It looks like a normal clean text input box, no arrows appear on hover or click!\n\n---\n\n### Solution 3: Badge / Tag Display (`widget=\"badge\"` or clean text)\nBecause the visit number is automatically generated by the system (1st visit, 2nd visit), users don't need to manually type or change it!\n* In XML:\n  ```xml\n  <field name=\"visit_number\" readonly=\"1\" class=\"fw-bold fs-6\"/>\n  ```\n* It displays as a neat, clean label right next to Complaint Type:\n  👉 **Complaint Type:** `Breakdown` | **Visit:** `1`\n\n---\n\n### My Recommendation:\nUse **Solution 1 or 3**: \nSet it as `readonly=\"True\"` so it auto-calculates as **`Visit #1`**, **`Visit #2`** without any up/down arrows at all!\n\nWhich display style do you like best?"}

{"step_index":905,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:30:16Z","content":"Let's trace **step-by-step** exactly how Visit #2 gets calculated and how the AMC quota is deducted:\n\n---\n\n### Real-Life Example:\n\nSuppose an AMC contract starts with:\n* **`Breakdown = 4`**\n\n---\n\n#### 📌 Scenario 1: First Service Ticket Created\n1. User opens Service Ticket Wizard.\n2. Selects Complaint Type: **`Breakdown`** (and selects that AMC contract).\n3. The system checks:\n   - Remaining in AMC: `4` (greater than 0, so valid!).\n   - Existing breakdown tickets for this AMC: `0`.\n   - Next Visit Number = `0 + 1` = **`1`**.\n4. User clicks Save:\n   - Service Ticket is saved with: **`Visit Number = 1`**.\n   - AMC contract is updated: `4 - 1` = **`3`**.\n   - Now AMC shows: **`Breakdown = 3`**.\n\n---\n\n#### 📌 Scenario 2: Second Service Ticket Created (Visit #2)\nA month later, the same customer calls for another breakdown:\n1. User opens Service Ticket Wizard.\n2. Selects Complaint Type: **`Breakdown`** (and that AMC contract).\n3. The system checks:\n   - Remaining in AMC: `3` (greater than 0, so valid!).\n   - Existing breakdown tickets for this AMC in database: **`1`** (from Scenario 1).\n   - Next Visit Number = `1 + 1` = **`2`**.\n4. User clicks Save:\n   - This new Service Ticket is saved with: **`Visit Number = 2`**.\n   - AMC contract is updated: `3 - 1` = **`2`**.\n   - Now AMC shows: **`Breakdown = 2`**.\n\n---\n\n#### 📌 Scenario 3: Third Service Ticket (Visit #3)\n1. Next Visit Number = **`3`**.\n2. AMC contract is updated: `2 - 1` = **`1`**.\n\n---\n\n#### 📌 Scenario 4: Fourth Service Ticket (Visit #4)\n1. Next Visit Number = **`4`**.\n2. AMC contract is updated: `1 - 1` = **`0`**.\n\n---\n\n#### 📌 Scenario 5: Fifth Service Ticket Attempt (Limit Reached!)\n1. User selects **`Breakdown`**.\n2. The system checks AMC: Remaining = **`0`**!\n3. The system immediately stops and warns the user:\n   > ⛔ *\"All Breakdown visits for this AMC contract have been used up (0 remaining)!\"*\n\n---\n\n### How the Python code does this automatically:\nInside `action_save_ticket`:\n```python\nif self.amc_id and self.complaint_type in ('pm', 'breakdown'):\n    amc = self.amc_id\n    \n    # 1. Count past tickets to calculate Visit Number (1, 2, 3...)\n    past_count = self.env['service.ticket'].sudo().search_count([\n        ('amc_id', '=', amc.id),\n        ('complaint_type', '=', self.complaint_type)\n    ])\n    visit_no = str(past_count + 1)  # \"1\", \"2\", \"3\" etc.\n\n    # 2. Check and Deduct Quota from AMC\n    if self.complaint_type == 'pm':\n        rem_pm = int(amc.pm or 0)\n        if rem_pm <= 0:\n            raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining PM visits!\"))\n        amc.sudo().write({'pm': str(rem_pm - 1)})\n\n    elif self.complaint_type == 'breakdown':\n        rem_cm = int(amc.cm or 0)\n        if rem_cm <= 0:\n            raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining Breakdown visits!\"))\n        amc.sudo().write({'cm': str(rem_cm - 1)})\n\n    # 3. Store Visit Number on the created ticket\n    ticket_vals['visit_number'] = visit_no\n```\n\nIt is 100% automated:\n- The user **never has to type or click any arrows**.\n- The AMC contract number automatically decreases (`4 ➔ 3 ➔ 2 ➔ 1 ➔ 0`).\n- Each ticket is automatically stamped with its visit number (`1`, `2`, `3`...)."}

{"step_index":907,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:33:09Z","content":"Ah! You are asking: **If `PM` and `Breakdown` in AMC are `fields.Char`, how do we stop the user from typing letters/alphabets like \"abc\" into the AMC form?**\n\nHere are the **2 best ways** to prevent alphabets and only allow numbers:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: Python Validation Constraint (Instant & Clean) ⭐ **RECOMMENDED**\nIn `amc_contract.py`, we add an `@api.constrains('pm', 'cm')`:\n\n```python\n    @api.constrains('pm', 'cm')\n    def _check_pm_cm_numeric(self):\n        for rec in self:\n            if rec.pm and not rec.pm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"PM must be a valid number (digits only)! You entered: '%s'\") % rec.pm)\n            if rec.cm and not rec.cm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Breakdown must be a valid number (digits only)! You entered: '%s'\") % rec.cm)\n```\n\n**How it works:**\n* If user types `4` ➔ Saved smoothly!\n* If user types `four` or `abc` or `4a` ➔ Odoo instantly blocks it and shows:\n  > ❌ *\"PM must be a valid number (digits only)!\"*\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Live HTML / Browser restriction (Input pattern)\nIn `amc_contract_views.xml`:\n```xml\n<field name=\"pm\" string=\"PM\" placeholder=\"e.g. 4\"/>\n<field name=\"cm\" string=\"Breakdown\" placeholder=\"e.g. 2\"/>\n```\nCombined with the Python `isdigit()` constraint, the user can **never enter alphabets** and your code can always safely do `int(rec.pm)` without crashing!\n\n---\n\nWould you like to add this validation so `PM` and `Breakdown` are 100% protected against alphabets?"}

{"step_index":911,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T11:43:05Z","content":"My apologies! Let's keep it strictly to **PM** and **Breakdown** — absolutely nothing else!\n\nHere is the clean, focused code:\n\n---\n\n### 1. In `amc_contract.py` (prevent alphabets in PM and Breakdown):\n```python\n    @api.constrains('pm', 'cm')\n    def _check_pm_cm_numeric(self):\n        for rec in self:\n            if rec.pm and not rec.pm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"PM must be a number only! You entered: '%s'\") % rec.pm)\n            if rec.cm and not rec.cm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Breakdown must be a number only! You entered: '%s'\") % rec.cm)\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. In `service_ticket_wizard.py` (inside `action_save_ticket`, deduct only PM or Breakdown):\n```python\n        # Check and deduct ONLY for PM or Breakdown\n        if self.amc_id:\n            if self.complaint_type == 'pm':\n                rem_pm = int(self.amc_id.pm.strip()) if self.amc_id.pm and self.amc_id.pm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                if rem_pm <= 0:\n                    raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining PM visits!\"))\n                self.amc_id.sudo().write({'pm': str(rem_pm - 1)})\n\n            elif self.complaint_type == 'breakdown':\n                rem_cm = int(self.amc_id.cm.strip()) if self.amc_id.cm and self.amc_id.cm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                if rem_cm <= 0:\n                    raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining Breakdown visits!\"))\n                self.amc_id.sudo().write({'cm': str(rem_cm - 1)})\n```\n\n---\n\nThat is strictly for **Breakdown** and **PM**:\n* Prevents letters with `isdigit()`.\n* Deducts only whichever one is selected.\n* Warns if it reaches 0.\n* No other fields or extras added."}

Please use a unique Ticket ID.\") % self.ticket_id)\n\n        elif self.step == 2:\n            # Check remaining quota immediately when leaving Step 2\n            if self.amc_id:\n                if self.complaint_type == 'pm':\n                    rem_pm = int(self.amc_id.pm.strip()) if self.amc_id.pm and self.amc_id.pm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                    if rem_pm <= 0:\n                        raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining PM visits! You cannot proceed.\"))\n                elif self.complaint_type == 'breakdown':\n                    rem_cm = int(self.amc_id.cm.strip()) if self.amc_id.cm and self.amc_id.cm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                    if rem_cm <= 0:\n                        raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining Breakdown visits! You cannot proceed.\"))\n\n        if self.step < 3:\n            self.step += 1\n        return self._reopen_wizard()\n```\n\nAnd in `action_save_ticket`, you only keep the deduction (`- 1`):\n```python\n        # Deduct ONLY for PM or Breakdown\n        if self.amc_id:\n            if self.complaint_type == 'pm':\n                rem_pm = int(self.amc_id.pm.strip()) if self.amc_id.pm and self.amc_id.pm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                if rem_pm > 0:\n                    self.amc_id.sudo().write({'pm': str(rem_pm - 1)})\n            elif self.complaint_type == 'breakdown':\n                rem_cm = int(self.amc_id.cm.strip()) if self.amc_id.cm and self.amc_id.cm.strip().isdigit() else 0\n                if rem_cm > 0:\n                    self.amc_id.sudo().write({'cm': str(rem_cm - 1)})\n```\n\nWould you like me to apply this directly to the file for you?"}

Service tickets can already be created without an AMC contract.** \n\nHere is why:\n\n1. **`amc_id` is completely optional**:\n   - In `service.ticket` and `service.ticket.wizard`, `amc_id` does not have `required=True`. {"step_index":961,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T12:12:19Z","content":"**No, minus integers are NOT allowed.**\n\nHere is why:\n\n### 1. In Service Ticket Wizard (Deduction & Validation):\n- The condition checks:\n  ```python\n  if rem_pm <= 0:\n      raise ValidationError(_(\"This AMC contract has 0 remaining PM visits!\"))\n  ```\n- Because it checks `<= 0`, it blocks **0** and any **negative number** (`-1`, `-2`, etc.). \n- Deduction only happens when visits are `> 0`, so the wizard will **never** deduct into negative numbers.\n\n---\n\n### 2. In AMC Contract Form (Manual Entry):\nCurrently, `pm` and `cm` are `fields.Char`. \nIf you want to prevent users from manually typing a minus sign (like `-5`) when saving the AMC contract, we can add this simple check in [amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py):\n\n```python\n    @api.constrains('pm', 'cm')\n    def _check_pm_cm_digits(self):\n        for rec in self:\n            if rec.pm and not rec.pm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"PM visits must be a positive number (digits only, no minus or alphabets).\"))\n            if rec.cm and not rec.cm.strip().isdigit():\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Breakdown visits must be a positive number (digits only, no minus or alphabets).\"))\n```\n*(Because Python's `.isdigit()` returns `False` for minus `-`, it rejects negative numbers as well as alphabets!)*\n\nWould you like me to add this validation to [amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py)?"}

{"step_index":985,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T12:20:40Z","content":"Here is the exact code for your single function `_check_pm_cm_numeric`. \n\nIt clearly distinguishes between **negative values (`-`)** and **non-numeric / text values**, with dedicated separate messages for when **both** are wrong:\n\n```python\n    @api.constrains('pm', 'cm')\n    def _check_pm_cm_numeric(self):\n        for rec in self:\n            pm_val = rec.pm.strip() if rec.pm else \"\"\n            cm_val = rec.cm.strip() if rec.cm else \"\"\n\n            # Detect negative values\n            pm_is_negative = pm_val.startswith('-') and pm_val[1:].isdigit()\n            cm_is_negative = cm_val.startswith('-') and cm_val[1:].isdigit()\n\n            # Detect other non-numeric / alphabet values\n            pm_is_non_numeric = bool(pm_val and not pm_val.isdigit() and not pm_is_negative)\n            cm_is_non_numeric = bool(cm_val and not cm_val.isdigit() and not cm_is_negative)\n\n            # 1. Both are negative\n            if pm_is_negative and cm_is_negative:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Negative values are not allowed! Both PM ('%s') and Breakdown ('%s') visits cannot be negative.\") % (pm_val, cm_val))\n\n            # 2. Both have text / non-numeric characters\n            if pm_is_non_numeric and cm_is_non_numeric:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Alphabets and symbols are not allowed! Both PM ('%s') and Breakdown ('%s') must be numbers only.\") % (pm_val, cm_val))\n\n            # 3. Both are wrong (one negative, one non-numeric)\n            if (pm_is_negative or pm_is_non_numeric) and (cm_is_negative or cm_is_non_numeric):\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Both PM ('%s') and Breakdown ('%s') values are invalid! Please enter positive numbers only.\") % (pm_val, cm_val))\n\n            # 4. Only PM is wrong\n            if pm_is_negative:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"PM visits cannot be negative! You entered: '%s'\") % pm_val)\n            if pm_is_non_numeric:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"PM visits must be a number only! Alphabets or symbols are not allowed: '%s'\") % pm_val)\n\n            # 5. Only Breakdown is wrong\n            if cm_is_negative:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Breakdown visits cannot be negative! You entered: '%s'\") % cm_val)\n            if cm_is_non_numeric:\n                raise ValidationError(_(\"Breakdown visits must be a number only! Alphabets or symbols are not allowed: '%s'\") % cm_val)\n```\n\n### What this covers:\n1. **Both negative** (e.g. `-2` & `-3`) $\\rightarrow$ Gives clear \"Negative values not allowed for both\" message.\n2. **Both text/alphabets** (e.g. `abc` & `xyz`) $\\rightarrow$ Gives clear \"Alphabets/symbols not allowed for both\" message.\n3. **One negative, one text** (e.g. `-2` & `abc`) $\\rightarrow$ Gives clear combined invalid message.\n4. **Only PM negative** (e.g. `-2`) $\\rightarrow$ Tells user PM cannot be negative.\n5. **Only PM text** (e.g. `abc`) $\\rightarrow$ Tells user PM must be a number.\n6. **Only Breakdown negative** (e.g. `-3`) $\\rightarrow$ Tells user Breakdown cannot be negative.\n7. **Only Breakdown text** (e.g. `xyz`) $\\rightarrow$ Tells user Breakdown must be a number."}

{"step_index":1029,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-18T12:39:41Z","content":"I understand exactly what you need! \n\nWhen a quotation has multiple products in its order lines, in the Quotation list view we want to show a **Product** column right next to Customer (`partner_id`), showing the **first product** name (with an indicator if there are more, like `Product Name (+2 more)` or just the first product name).\n\nHere is the plan:\n\n### 1. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py`:\nAdd a computed stored field:\n```python\n    x_first_product_name = fields.Char(\n        string='Product',\n        compute='_compute_first_product_name',\n        store=True,\n    )\n\n    @api.depends('order_line.product_id', 'order_line.name')\n    def _compute_first_product_name(self):\n        for order in self:\n            products = order.order_line.filtered(lambda l: not l.display_type and l.product_id)\n            if products:\n                first = products[0].product_id.display_name\n                count = len(products)\n                if count > 1:\n                    order.x_first_product_name = f\"{first} (+{count - 1} more)\"\n                else:\n                    order.x_first_product_name = first\n            else:\n                order.x_first_product_name = \"\"\n```\n*(Note: If you only want the plain first product name without `(+X more)`, we can just set `order.x_first_product_name = first`)*.\n\n---\n\n### 2. In `addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml`:\nInside the Quotations list view (`view_sale_order_list_custom`), place the column right after `partner_id`:\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='partner_id']\" position=\"after\">\n                <field name=\"x_first_product_name\" string=\"Product\" optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n---\n\n**Question for you before proceeding**:\nWould you prefer:\n1. Just the first product name alone (e.g. `Laptop Dell 5520`)\n2. Or with the extra count indicator (e.g. `Laptop Dell 5520 (+2 more)`)?\n\nAnd should I apply this change, or do you want the code snippets to add it yourself?"}

{"step_index":1032,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T04:53:52Z","content":"To find the total number of Equipment Master records in your production database, you have two quick options:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: Via Odoo User Interface (Easiest)\n1. Open your production Odoo CRM in the browser.\n2. Go to the **Equipment Master** list view (from the menu or dashboard).\n3. Look at the top-right pagination counter next to the search bar — it will show the total count (for example: `1-80 / 250` where `250` is the total number of equipment records).\n4. *(Make sure any default filter in the search bar is removed so it counts all records).*\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Via GCP SSH Terminal (Direct Query)\nIn your GCP production terminal, run this one command to check directly in PostgreSQL:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d <production_database_name> -c \"SELECT count(*) AS total_equipment FROM equipment_master;\"\n```\n*(Replace `<production_database_name>` with your actual production DB name, e.g. `crm_prod` or `crm_data_prod`).*\n\n---\n\n### Option 3: Via Odoo Shell\nIn your GCP terminal, run:\n```bash\nodoo shell -d <production_database_name>\n```\nThen inside the shell, type:\n```python\nenv['equipment.master'].search_count([])\n```\nand press Enter. It will immediately print the exact count!"}

{"step_index":1040,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T04:54:26Z","content":"In your Odoo logs from yesterday, your database name was:\n\n### **`crm_data_test`** (or `crm_data_prod` / `crm_production` depending on your setup)\n\n---\n\n### Command to get the total count right now:\n\nIn your GCP SSH terminal, run this single command:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data_test -c \"SELECT count(*) AS total_equipment FROM equipment_master;\"\n```\n\n*(If your production database is named `crm_prod` or `crm_data_prod`, you can list all databases first to confirm by running `sudo -u postgres psql -l`)*."}

{"step_index":1044,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T04:54:52Z","content":"To check the exact production database name and get the equipment count immediately, run these two quick commands in your GCP terminal:\n\n### 1. See all database names on your server:\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -l -A | grep template -v\n```\nThis lists your databases so you can see the exact production name (e.g. `crm_prod`, `crm_production`, `crm_live`, etc.).\n\n---\n\n### 2. Run the count query on your production database:\nOnce you see the production DB name from step 1, run:\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d <YOUR_PROD_DB_NAME> -c \"SELECT count(*) AS total_equipment FROM equipment_master;\"\n```\n\nWhat database name did step 1 show, or what count did it return?"}

{"step_index":1050,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T04:55:51Z","content":"To see what the Equipment series prefix starts with, its current numbering, and sample equipment IDs in production, run these two commands in GCP:\n\n### 1. Check configured Equipment sequence series (Prefix, Next Number, Padding):\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"SELECT name, code, prefix, padding, number_next_actual FROM ir_sequence WHERE code IN ('crm.equipment.id', 'crm.equipment.serial');\"\n```\n\n### 2. See the latest created Equipment IDs in production:\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"SELECT equipment_id, serial_number, name FROM equipment_master ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;\"\n```\n\nPaste the output here and we can see the exact series!"}

{"step_index":1082,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T05:20:59Z","content":"### 1. Does changing the gear icon logic affect ALL views?\n\n**YES, if you modify the standard Odoo core Gear menu (the web framework `CogMenu` / `ExportData`), it will affect ALL views across the entire CRM and Odoo (Quotations, Leads, Contacts, etc.).**\n\nIn Odoo, the gear icon's **\"Export All\"** feature comes from the global web framework (`@web/views/list/list_controller`). By standard design, it only grabs the columns currently visible in the active list view table.\n\n---\n\n### 2. How can we export all Form View fields WITHOUT affecting other views?\n\nThere are **two safe approaches**:\n\n#### Approach A: Specific Custom List Controllers for EQ, Service Ticket & AMC (Recommended & 100% Safe)\nWe can attach a custom List Controller **only to Equipment, Service Ticket, and AMC list views** (just like you already have custom controllers `equipment_form.js`, `amc_form.js`, `service_ticket_form.js`).\n- When user clicks **Export All** in the gear icon on **these 3 models**:\n  - It intercepts and exports **all fields from the form view** into Excel (empty if no data).\n- On **every other model** (Quotations, Leads, Customers, etc.):\n  - The gear icon remains 100% untouched and behaves standardly!\n\n#### Approach B: Dedicated \"Export Excel (All Fields)\" Button / Action\nInstead of modifying the gear icon, we can add a direct button on the list view header:\n- `[ Export Excel (All Details) ]`\n- User clicks it $\\rightarrow$ downloads an Excel file with all form view fields for all filtered records immediately.\n\n---\n\n### Comparison:\n- If you want the user to still click the **Gear Icon $\\rightarrow$ Export All**, we use **Approach A** with model-specific controllers. This **will NOT** affect Quotations, Leads, or any other views!\n\nWould you prefer **Approach A (keep it in the Gear icon for just these 3 models)** or **Approach B (a dedicated button)**?"}

{"step_index":1102,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-19T05:23:06Z","content":"Here is the clean, professional solution. \n\nInstead of messing with complex Odoo internal cog-menu JS templates (which risk breaking when Odoo updates), we add an **Action menu item (or Gear Cog action)**:\n👉 **\"Export All (All Fields to Excel)\"**\n\nWhen you are in the list view of **Equipment Master**, **Service Ticket**, or **AMC Contract**:\n- Click the **Gear (⚙️ Actions)** icon (or select records) $\\rightarrow$ click **\"Export All (All Fields to Excel)\"**.\n- It dynamically fetches **every single form view field**, builds an Excel `.xlsx` file, and downloads it immediately. If a field is empty in a record, it will cleanly be empty in Excel.\n- **Quotations, Leads, Customers, etc.** will NOT have this action at all.\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Create the Excel Export Controller/Action\n\nCreate a new file: `addons/custom_crm_extended/controllers/export_all_fields.py`:\n\n```python\n# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-\nimport io\nfrom odoo import http, _\nfrom odoo.http import request\ntry:\n    import xlsxwriter\nexcept ImportError:\n    xlsxwriter = None\n\n\nclass ExportAllFieldsController(http.Controller):\n\n    @http.route('/custom_crm/export_all_fields', type='http', auth='user')\n    def export_all_fields(self, model, domain='[]', **kwargs):\n        if not xlsxwriter:\n            return request.not_found()\n\n        Model = request.env[model].sudo()\n        domain = eval(domain)\n        records = Model.search(domain)\n\n        # Form fields definition for each model\n        FIELD_CONFIGS = {\n            'equipment.master': [\n                ('equipment_id', 'Equipment ID'),\n                ('name', 'Model Name'),\n                ('category_id', 'Equipment'),\n                ('manufacturer', 'Manufacturer'),\n                ('model_number', 'Equipment Owner'),\n                ('serial_number', 'Serial Number'),\n                ('part_number', 'Part Number'),\n                ('child_part_no', 'Child Part No'),\n                ('invoice_number', 'Invoice No'),\n                ('invoice_date', 'Invoice Date'),\n                ('equipment_status', 'Equipment Status'),\n                ('criticality', 'Criticality'),\n                ('partner_id', 'Customer Name'),\n                ('contact_person', 'Contact Person'),\n                ('contact_number', 'Contact Number'),\n                ('email', 'Email'),\n                ('site_name', 'Site Name'),\n                ('building', 'Building'),\n                ('floor', 'Floor'),\n                ('department', 'Department'),\n                ('room_number', 'Room Number'),\n                ('installation_date', 'Installation Date'),\n                ('warranty_start_date', 'Warranty Start Date'),\n                ('warranty_end_date', 'Warranty End Date'),\n                ('service_contract', 'Service Contract'),\n                ('firmware_version', 'Firmware Version'),\n                ('address', 'Address'),\n                ('accessories', 'Accessories'),\n                ('remarks', 'Remarks'),\n            ],\n            'service.ticket': [\n                ('ticket_id', 'Ticket ID'),\n                ('ticket_datetime', 'Ticket Date & Time'),\n                ('partner_id', 'Customer Name'),\n                ('equipment_id', 'Equipment'),\n                ('amc_id', 'AMC Contract'),\n                ('site_name', 'Site Name'),\n                ('contact_person', 'Contact Person'),\n                ('contact_number', 'Contact Number'),\n                ('email', 'Customer Email'),\n                ('model_number', 'Model Number'),\n                ('serial_number', 'Serial Number'),\n                ('part_number', 'Part Number'),\n                ('complaint_type', 'Complaint Type'),\n                ('complaint_description', 'Complaint Description'),\n                ('priority', 'Priority'),\n                ('engineer_id', 'Assigned Engineer'),\n                ('engineer_contact', 'Engineer Contact'),\n                ('engineer_email', 'Engineer Email'),\n                ('visit_date', 'Visit Date'),\n                ('ticket_status', 'Ticket Status'),\n                ('root_cause', 'Root Cause'),\n                ('corrective_action', 'Corrective Action'),\n                ('spare_parts_used', 'Spare Parts Used'),\n                ('service_start_time', 'Service Start Time'),\n                ('service_end_time', 'Service End Time'),\n            ],\n            'amc.contract': [\n                ('name', 'AMC No.'),\n                ('date', 'Date'),\n                ('contract_status', 'Contract Status'),\n                ('partner_id', 'Customer / Company Name'),\n                ('customer_address', 'Customer Address'),\n                ('gstin', 'GSTIN'),\n                ('contact_person', 'Contact Person'),\n                ('mobile', 'Mobile'),\n                ('location', 'Location'),\n                ('email', 'Email'),\n                ('warranty_start_date', 'Warranty Start Date'),\n                ('warranty_end_date', 'Warranty End Date'),\n                ('contract_start_date', 'Contract Start Date'),\n                ('contract_end_date', 'Contract End Date'),\n                ('contract_value', 'Contract Value (₹)'),\n                ('gst', 'GST (%)'),\n                ('payment_terms', 'Payment Terms'),\n                ('renewal_terms', 'Renewal Terms'),\n                ('pm', 'PM Visits'),\n                ('cm', 'Breakdown Visits'),\n            ]\n        }\n\n        fields_to_export = FIELD_CONFIGS.get(model, [])\n        output = io.BytesIO()\n        workbook = xlsxwriter.Workbook(output, {'in_memory': True})\n        worksheet = workbook.add_worksheet(model.replace('.', '_'))\n\n        # Header format\n        header_format = workbook.add_format({\n            'bold': True,\n            'bg_color': '#1A3D6E',\n            'font_color': '#FFFFFF',\n            'border': 1\n        })\n        cell_format = workbook.add_format({'border': 1})\n\n        # Write Headers\n        for col_idx, (fname, flabel) in enumerate(fields_to_export):\n            worksheet.write(0, col_idx, flabel, header_format)\n            worksheet.set_column(col_idx, col_idx, max(len(flabel) + 3, 15))\n\n        # Write Data Rows\n        for row_idx, rec in enumerate(records, start=1):\n            for col_idx, (fname, flabel) in enumerate(fields_to_export):\n                val = getattr(rec, fname, '')\n                if hasattr(val, 'display_name'):\n                    val_str = val.display_name or ''\n                elif isinstance(val, (bool)):\n                    val_str = str(val) if val else ''\n                elif val is None:\n                    val_str = ''\n                else:\n                    val_str = str(val)\n                worksheet.write(row_idx, col_idx, val_str, cell_format)\n\n        workbook.close()\n        output.seek(0)\n\n        filename = f\"{model.replace('.', '_')}_all_fields.xlsx\"\n        return request.make_response(\n            output.getvalue(),\n            headers=[\n                ('Content-Type', 'application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet'),\n                ('Content-Disposition', f'attachment; filename=\"{filename}\"'),\n            ]\n        )\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Add Model Actions in Python\n\nIn each of the three models (`equipment_master.py`, `service_ticket.py`, `amc_contract.py`):\n\n```python\n    def action_export_all_form_fields(self):\n        return {\n            'type': 'ir.actions.act_url',\n            'url': f'/custom_crm/export_all_fields?model={self._name}',\n            'target': 'self',\n        }\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Add the Action in the Gear (⚙️ Action) Menu in XML\n\nIn `equipment_master_views.xml`, `service_ticket_views.xml`, and `amc_contract_views.xml`:\n\n```xml\n    <record id=\"action_export_all_equipment\" model=\"ir.actions.server\">\n        <field name=\"name\">Export All (All Fields to Excel)</field>\n        <field name=\"model_id\" ref=\"model_equipment_master\"/>\n        <field name=\"binding_model_id\" ref=\"model_equipment_master\"/>\n        <field name=\"binding_view_types\">list</field>\n        <field name=\"state\">code</field>\n        <field name=\"code\">\naction = record.action_export_all_form_fields()\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n---\n\n### Result:\n- When on **Equipment Master** list view $\\rightarrow$ click Gear ⚙️ $\\rightarrow$ **\"Export All (All Fields to Excel)\"** $\\rightarrow$ downloads all 29 form view fields into Excel!\n- When on **Service Ticket** list view $\\rightarrow$ click Gear ⚙️ $\\rightarrow$ **\"Export All (All Fields to Excel)\"** $\\rightarrow$ downloads all 25 ticket form fields into Excel!\n- When on **AMC Contract** list view $\\rightarrow$ click Gear ⚙️ $\\rightarrow$ **\"Export All (All Fields to Excel)\"** $\\rightarrow$ downloads all 20 contract form fields into Excel!\n- Any other list view (Quotations, Leads, Contacts, etc.) has **zero changes**!\n\nWould you like me to implement this for you, or would you like to apply the code yourself?"}
