{"step_index":2735,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:45:48Z","content":"In standard Odoo and in this project, there are **two ways** to create a new Company:\n\n---\n\n### Method 1: Via Settings (Standard Odoo)\n1. Go to **Quick Access > Settings** (or click your profile/cog icon > **Settings**).\n2. Click on **Users & Companies > Companies** in the top navigation bar.\n3. Click the **\"New\"** button to create a new company.\n4. Fill in:\n   - **Company Name** (e.g., *Ultrawin Calibration Center*, *Yantra Dynamics*)\n   - Currency, Address, GST / Tax ID\n5. Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### Method 2: Direct Menu Shortcut in Quick Access (Recommended)\nRight now under **Quick Access > Organization**, you have:\n- *Roles & Groups*\n- *Departments*\n- *Employee Tags*\n\nWe can add **\"Companies\"** right inside **Quick Access > Organization** so you can manage and create companies in 1 click!\n\n#### If you want this 1-click shortcut:\nIn `dashboard.xml`:\n```xml\n<div class=\"crm-submenu-content\">\n    <a t-on-click=\"openCompanies\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Companies</a>\n    <a t-on-click=\"openRolesAndGroups\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Roles &amp; Groups</a>\n    <a t-on-click=\"openDepartments\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Departments</a>\n    <a t-on-click=\"openEmployeeTags\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Employee Tags</a>\n</div>\n```\nAnd in `dashboard.js`:\n```javascript\nopenCompanies() {\n    this.action.doAction({\n        type: \"ir.actions.act_window\",\n        name: \"Companies\",\n        res_model: \"res.company\",\n        views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]],\n    });\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Important Permission Note:\nThe **\"Company Creation\"** permission we added:\n- When a user has `perm_company == 'create'`, Odoo grants them membership in `base.group_multi_company`.\n- Once granted, that user can view, switch between, and create new companies!\n\nWould you like me to add the **\"Companies\"** shortcut inside the **Quick Access > Organization** menu?"}

{"step_index":2743,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:49:28Z","content":"**YES, 100%! The Admin can access ALL data.**\n\nHere is why:\n\n1. **Super Admin / System Administrator (`base.group_system`)**:\n   In Odoo, an Administrator belongs to `base.group_system` (or is the root Admin with ID 1/2). In Odoo's core security engine, **Super Admins automatically bypass all domain record rules**.\n\n2. **Job Position is Completely Optional**:\n   If an Admin user has **NO** `crm_job_id` (Job Position is empty), nothing restricts them. They keep their standard full Administrator permissions across all apps (Leads, Quotations, Equipments, Contacts, Companies, etc.).\n\n3. **Built-in Protection Code**:\n   In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L43):\n   ```python\n   if not user.id or user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n       continue\n   ```\n   Even if someone accidentally assigns a restricted Job Position (like \"Employee\") to an Admin user, the system **explicitly ignores** the Admin and **never downgrades** their permissions.\n\nSo whether an Admin has a Job Position or no Job Position at all, they always have **full access to all data**."}

{"step_index":2751,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:51:32Z","content":"Yes! The 1-way approach is implemented as follows:\n\n---\n\n### 1. From Master Roles & Groups (`hr.job`) ➔ Down to User:\n- When you create or change a **Role / Job Position** (in **Quick Access > Organization > Roles & Groups**):\n- It finds all assigned users (`crm_job_id == job.id`) and **pushes** all 6 permissions down to each user:\n  1. `Lead & Quotation`\n  2. `Equipment Master`\n  3. `Contact Creation`\n  4. `Product Catalog`\n  5. `Excel Export`\n  6. `Company Creation`\n- And it updates their database security groups in real-time.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Can a particular user page be changed individually?\n**YES.**\n- If you open an individual user's profile, you can override any field (for example, change their `Equipment Master` to `All Documents`, or give that specific person `Excel Export: Yes`).\n- Changing an individual user **NEVER changes the Master Role**. The Role remains untouched (1-way sync).\n- The individual override stays in effect until someone edits the Master Role and saves it again."}

{"step_index":2755,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:52:48Z","content":"In Odoo, you can restrict editing so that:\n- **Non-admin users** see the Access Rights tab as **READ-ONLY** (they can only view their permissions, cannot edit them).\n- **Only Admins (`base.group_system`)** can edit and change permissions!\n\n---\n\n### In [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)\n\nIn the user form view, make the whole `access_rights` page read-only for non-admins:\n\nReplace lines 54–62 with:\n\n```xml\n            <!-- Make all Access Rights read-only unless user is an Administrator -->\n            <xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"readonly\">not is_admin</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n\n            <xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']/group[1]\" position=\"inside\">\n                <group>\n                    <group string=\"Configuration &amp; Masters\">\n                        <field name=\"perm_equipment\" string=\"Equipment Master\" readonly=\"not is_admin\"/>\n                        <field name=\"perm_company\" string=\"Company Creation\" readonly=\"not is_admin\"/>\n                    </group>\n                    <group/>\n                </group>\n            </xpath>\n```\n\n*(In Odoo, `is_admin` is a standard built-in field on `res.users` that checks if the logged-in user is a System Administrator)*.\n\n---\n\n### Result:\n- **Non-Admin users**: All dropdowns in the Access Rights tab are **read-only text** (disabled/locked).\n- **Admin users**: Can freely edit, modify, and save permissions.\n\nShall I apply this to [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)?"}

{"step_index":2761,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:57:30Z","content":"Here are the best name ideas for **\"Roles & Groups\"**, grouped by style:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: Modern & Professional CRM (Recommended)\n1. **User Roles & Permissions**  \n   *(Very clear — tells the admin immediately that this is where roles and their access rights are configured).*\n2. **Roles & Access Control**  \n   *(Enterprise SaaS style, like Salesforce or HubSpot).*\n3. **Designations & Access**  \n   *(Matches organizational HR hierarchy while highlighting permission management).*\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Short & Clean\n4. **Roles & Access**  \n   *(Punchy, fits neatly in dropdown menus without wrapping).*\n5. **Job Roles**  \n   *(Direct and simple).*\n6. **User Roles**  \n   *(Standard Odoo/ERP naming).*\n\n---\n\n### Option 3: Security & Governance Style\n7. **Access Profiles**  \n   *(Modern cloud term — each Job Position acts as a preset security profile).*\n8. **Role Permissions**  \n   *(Focused entirely on what the page does).*\n\n---\n\n### Comparison under Quick Access > Organization:\n\n| Current | Recommended (Clearer) | Shortest |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| • Roles & Groups<br>• Departments<br>• Employee Tags | • **User Roles & Permissions**<br>• Departments<br>• Employee Tags | • **Roles & Access**<br>• Departments<br>• Employee Tags |\n\nWhich name fits your system best: **\"User Roles & Permissions\"**, **\"Roles & Access\"**, or one of the others?"}

{"step_index":2766,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:58:27Z","content":"**\"Role\"** is much more suitable than \"Job Position\"!\n\nHere is why:\n\n1. **\"Job Position\"** sounds like recruitment or HR hiring (like *Job Openings / Vacancies*).\n2. **\"Role\"** directly means:\n   - What the employee's title is (e.g., *Sales Executive*, *Service Engineer*, *Accountant*).\n   - What access permissions they get in the CRM.\n3. Industry standards (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoho, AWS) all use **\"Roles\"** or **\"Roles & Permissions\"** for managing access rights.\n\nIn your menu:\n```text\nOrganization\n  ├── Roles & Permissions   <-- Perfect & professional!\n  ├── Departments\n  └── Employee Tags\n```\n\nAnd in the UI label:\n- On the User form, instead of saying `\"Job Position\"`, it says `\"Job Position / Role\"` or just `\"Role\"`.\n\n**\"Roles & Permissions\"** is the most professional and intuitive term for this."}

{"step_index":2770,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T12:59:43Z","content":"If a user has **NO Job Position / Role selected** (`crm_job_id` is empty):\n\n---\n\n### 1. What happens to their Permissions?\n- **Nothing is forced onto them:** The automatic role sync only triggers when a role is selected.\n- **Manual Permission Control:** You can set their permissions **manually** directly on their User form (`Access Rights` tab).\n- **Default Odoo Behavior:** They keep whatever default groups they were given when their user account was created.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Can they still use the system?\n- **Yes.** They can log in, view the dashboard, and work based on whatever individual permissions are saved on their user form.\n- The `crm_job_id` is **not a required field** — it is purely an organizational shortcut so you don't have to manually configure 6 permissions for every single employee one by one.\n\n---\n\n### Summary:\n| User Type | With Role Selected (`crm_job_id`) | Without Role Selected (`crm_job_id = False`) |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **New/Standard User** | Permissions are automatically synced from the Role. | Permissions are configured manually per user. |\n| **Administrator** | Full Admin access (Role permissions never downgrade Admin). | Full Admin access. |"}

{"step_index":2774,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T13:00:56Z","content":"Good question! Look at how Odoo works when a new user is created **without** selecting a Job Position:\n\n### Who decides the access if no Job Position is selected?\n\n1. **The Python Field Defaults (Code Default)**:\n   In `res_users.py`:\n   - `perm_lead_quote`: default is `'own'` *(Sales: Own Documents Only)*\n   - `perm_equipment`: default is `'own'` *(Equipment: Own Documents Only)*\n   - `perm_contact`: default is `'create'` *(Can create contacts)*\n   - `perm_product`: default is `'create'` *(Can view/create products)*\n   - `perm_export`: default is `'none'` *(Cannot export Excel)*\n   - `perm_company`: default is `'none'` *(Cannot create company)*\n\n2. **The Base Odoo User Groups (`_assign_default_groups`)**:\n   When a user is created, Odoo automatically assigns them:\n   - `base.group_user` (Internal User)\n   - `sales_team.group_sale_salesman` (User: Own Documents Only)\n\n3. **The Admin creating the user**:\n   The Admin who created the user can either:\n   - **Pick a Job Position / Role** ➔ Everything auto-fills based on that Role.\n   - **Or leave Job Position empty** ➔ The user receives the safe basic defaults above (`Own Documents Only`, No Excel Export, No Company Creation).\n\n---\n\n### If you want to force everyone to have a Role:\nWe can make `crm_job_id` (Role) **Mandatory (`required=True`)** on the User form!\nThen an Admin **must** select a Role whenever they create or edit a user. That way, no user will ever be created without a defined Role.\n\nWould you like to make `Role` a required field?"}

{"step_index":2779,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-21T13:04:17Z","content":"Here are the exact commands to deploy to your **Production server**:\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Push latest changes from your local machine (Already done!)\nYour code is already pushed to GitHub `main` branch (commit `cc3430a`).\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: On your Production GCP Server SSH\n\nConnect to your Production server terminal and run:\n\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom\ngit pull origin main\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Upgrade the modified modules on the Production database\n\nRun the Odoo upgrade command for both affected modules (`crm_whitelabel` and `custom_crm_extended`):\n\n```bash\nodoo-bin -c /etc/odoo.conf -d crm_production -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init\n```\n*(Replace `crm_production` with your actual production database name if different)*.\n\n---\n\n### Step 4: Restart the Production Odoo Service\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl restart crm-prod\n```\n*(Or `sudo systemctl restart odoo` depending on your production service name)*.\n\n---\n\n### One-Liner (Run all at once):\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git pull origin main && odoo-bin -c /etc/odoo.conf -d crm_production -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm-prod\n```"}

{"step_index":2801,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T04:59:53Z","content":"Here is the complete workflow, link architecture, and status flow between **Equipment Master ➔ AMC Contract ➔ Service Ticket**:\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Workflow Connection Architecture\n\n```\n                  +-------------------------+\n                  |     Customer Profile    |\n                  |       (res.partner)     |\n                  +------------+------------+\n                               |\n                               v\n                  +-------------------------+\n                  |    Equipment Master     |  <-- Machine is registered\n                  |   (equipment.master)    |      Tracks: Serial No, Warranty, Running Status\n                  +------------+------------+\n                               |\n                +--------------+--------------+\n                |                             |\n                v                             v\n     +--------------------+         +--------------------+\n     |    AMC Contract    |         |   Service Ticket   |\n     |   (amc.contract)   | <-----> |  (service.ticket)  |\n     +--------------------+ (Linked)+--------------------+\n     Tracks: Coverage,              Tracks: Breakdown, PM,\n     Contract Period & Visits       Engineer assignment & Signoff\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. Statuses at Each Stage\n\n#### Stage 1: Equipment Master (`equipment.master`)\nTracks the physical equipment at customer site:\n- **`equipment_status`**:\n  - `active` (Active & in use)\n  - `under_repair` (Currently experiencing breakdown/servicing)\n  - `inactive` (Decommissioned / replaced)\n- **`service_contract`**: `warranty` | `amc` | `cmc` | `none`\n- **`running_status`**: `running` | `stopped`\n\n---\n\n#### Stage 2: AMC Contract (`amc.contract`)\nWhen an AMC is signed for that equipment:\n- **`contract_status`**:\n  1. `draft` — Initial proposal / negotiation\n  2. `active` — Signed & live contract (Visits & breakdown coverage valid)\n  3. `expired` — End date reached (requires renewal)\n  4. `renewed` — Replaced by a new AMC term\n  5. `cancelled` — Terminated prematurely\n- **Linkage**: The equipment is added in `amc.contract.line`. The AMC captures warranty dates, PM visit quota, and breakdown coverage.\n\n---\n\n#### Stage 3: Service Ticket (`service.ticket`)\nWhen maintenance or breakdown happens:\n- **`ticket_status`**:\n  1. `open` (Logged / Waiting for assignment)\n  2. `assigned` (Engineer dispatched with visit date)\n  3. `in_progress` (Service work underway on site)\n  4. `completed` (Work finished, customer & engineer signatures collected)\n  5. `cancelled`\n- **Automatic Linkage**:\n  - When you pick the **Equipment**, it automatically fills the **Customer**, **Model**, **Serial Number**, and **Site Location**.\n  - If the equipment has an **Active AMC**, the `amc_id` field automatically links to that AMC contract so the engineer knows it is covered under contract!\n  - When ticket is marked `completed`: Last PM / Breakdown date updates on the Equipment Master."}

{"step_index":2806,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:01:26Z","content":"Yes! In this system, **Service Ticket is built with a Hybrid Architecture**:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Mode A: Linked Ticket (With Equipment / AMC)\n* **How it works:** You select an existing machine from `equipment_id`.\n* **What happens automatically:**\n  - Auto-fetches Customer (`partner_id`), Site Address, Contact Person, Phone, Email.\n  - Auto-fetches Machine Specs: Model Number, Serial Number, Part Number.\n  - If that equipment is under an active contract, it auto-links `amc_id`.\n  - When the ticket is completed, it writes back to the equipment's history (`last_breakdown_date` or `last_preventive_maintenance`).\n\n---\n\n### 2. Mode B: Independent / Ad-Hoc Ticket (No Equipment or One-Time Service)\n* **How it works:** `equipment_id` and `amc_id` are **optional** (not `required=True`).\n* **Use Case:**\n  - One-time repair for a customer where the equipment is **not registered** in the system.\n  - General customer complaint, inspection, or calibration consultation call.\n  - You can enter the customer (`partner_id`), contact details, or type in the machine details manually without having to create an Equipment Master record first.\n\n---\n\n### The Hybrid Model in Summary:\n\n| Feature | Linked Mode (Equipment/AMC) | Independent Mode (Standalone) |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **`equipment_id`** | Selected from Equipment Master | Left empty (`False`) |\n| **`amc_id`** | Linked to active AMC contract | Left empty (`False`) |\n| **Machine Specs** | Auto-filled from master record | Typed manually or left blank |\n| **Complaint Type** | PM / Breakdown / Contract Visit | Free Call / One-time service / Inspection |\n| **Lifecycle** | Updates equipment maintenance history | Standalone service record |\n\nThis gives your technicians full flexibility: they can quickly log a service call for a non-registered customer machine, or link it to a full Equipment Master and AMC asset lifecycle when needed."}

{"step_index":2812,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:06:42Z","content":"**YES, exactly 100% identical to Lead / Quotation!**\n\nHere is how it works:\n\n### 1. User with \"User: Own Documents Only\" (`own`):\n- Odoo places them in group `group_equipment_own`.\n- Security rule enforces:\n  ```python\n  ['|', ('user_id', '=', user.id), ('create_uid', '=', user.id)]\n  ```\n  They can **only** view, edit, and access equipments where they are the **assigned responsible (`user_id`)** or the **creator (`create_uid`)**.\n- When creating a Service Ticket or AMC, they only see their own equipments in the dropdown.\n\n---\n\n### 2. User with \"User: All Documents\" (`all`) or \"Administrator\" (`admin`):\n- Odoo places them in group `group_equipment_all`.\n- Security rule:\n  ```python\n  [(1, '=', 1)]\n  ```\n  They can view and access **ALL equipment records** across the entire company.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Super Admins:\n- Bypasses all record rules and always has full read, write, create, and delete access to everything.\n\nEquipment Master is now structured and enforced under the **exact same architecture as Lead & Quotation**."}

{"step_index":2814,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:07:06Z","content":"**NO, absolutely NOT hardcoded!**\n\nIt is implemented using **100% native Odoo security mechanisms**:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Dynamic User Checking (NOT hardcoded IDs)\nIn [multi_company_rules.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/security/multi_company_rules.xml#L34):\n```xml\n<field name=\"domain_force\">['|', ('user_id', '=', user.id), ('create_uid', '=', user.id)]</field>\n```\n- `user.id` is Odoo’s dynamic variable for whoever is **currently logged in**.\n- It checks the real database columns `user_id` and `create_uid` dynamically on every query.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Standard Odoo Security Groups (NOT hardcoded names)\nIn [multi_company_rules.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/security/multi_company_rules.xml#L21):\n- `group_equipment_own`\n- `group_equipment_all`\nThese are real `res.groups` records registered in PostgreSQL.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Dynamic Database Group Assignment\nIn [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L70):\n```python\nself.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ...\")\n```\n- Uses PostgreSQL foreign key references (`gid`, `uid`) to assign the user dynamically to the group.\n- This is the exact same method Odoo core uses internally for assigning access rights.\n\nNo static user IDs, no static company IDs, no hardcoded employee names anywhere. Everything is dynamic and fully database-driven."}

{"step_index":2816,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:07:29Z","content":"`[(1, '=', 1)]` is **standard Odoo ORM syntax**, not a hardcoded hack!\n\nHere is why:\n\n### What `[(1, '=', 1)]` means in Odoo:\nIn Odoo's SQL generator:\n- In SQL, `WHERE 1 = 1` evaluates to `TRUE` for every row.\n- In Odoo record rules (`ir.rule`), **`[(1, '=', 1)]` means \"Grant access to ALL records\" (no restriction)**.\n\n---\n\n### Proof from Official Odoo Source Code:\nEvery standard Odoo module uses this exact syntax for \"All Documents\" or \"Manager\" rules:\n\n1. **In Odoo's official Sales module (`sale/security/sale_security.xml`)**:\n   ```xml\n   <record id=\"sale_order_see_all\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n       <field name=\"name\">All Orders</field>\n       <field ref=\"model_sale_order\" name=\"model_id\"/>\n       <field name=\"domain_force\">[(1, '=', 1)]</field>\n       <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads'))]\"/>\n   </record>\n   ```\n\n2. **In Odoo's official CRM module (`crm/security/crm_security.xml`)**:\n   ```xml\n   <record id=\"crm_lead_all_rule\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n       <field name=\"name\">All Leads</field>\n       <field ref=\"model_crm_lead\" name=\"model_id\"/>\n       <field name=\"domain_force\">[(1, '=', 1)]</field>\n       <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads'))]\"/>\n   </record>\n   ```\n\n3. **In Odoo's official Helpdesk / Project modules**:\n   All use `[(1, '=', 1)]` to give users with \"All Documents\" permission unrestricted access to read all records.\n\n---\n\n### Why Odoo requires `[(1, '=', 1)]`:\nIn Odoo, if a user has a restrictive rule (`user_id = user.id`), Odoo's rule engine combines rules with `OR` when multiple groups apply. \nBy having the \"All Documents\" group evaluate to `[(1, '=', 1)]`, Odoo does:\n```sql\nWHERE (user_id = user.id) OR (1 = 1)\n```\nWhich allows users with \"All Documents\" access to see everything, while users with only \"Own Documents\" are restricted to `(user_id = user.id)`.\n\nIt is the standard, official Odoo design pattern for record rules."}

Everything is managed directly from Organization.**\n\nHere is how the admin manages it now:\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Single Control Center:\nGo to **Quick Access > Organization > Roles & Permissions** (`hr.job`):\n\n```text\nQuick Access\n  └── Organization\n        ├── Roles & Permissions   <-- (Manage Roles & 6 Permissions here)\n        ├── Departments\n        └── Employee Tags\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. What the Admin Does in Roles & Permissions:\nWhen you open or create a Role (e.g., *Sales Executive*, *Service Engineer*, *Manager*):\n1. **Set the Department & Company**.\n2. **Configure the 6 Permissions**:\n   - **Lead & Quotation**: `No` | `User: Own Documents Only` | `User: All Documents` | `Administrator`\n   - **Equipment Master**: `No` | `User: Own Documents Only` | `User: All Documents` | `Administrator`\n   - **Contact Creation**: `No` | `Creation`\n   - **Product Catalog**: `View` | `Create`\n   - **Excel Export**: `No` | `Yes`\n   - **Company Creation**: `No` | `Yes`\n3. Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Automatic Real-Time Synchronization:\nThe moment the Role is saved:\n- Every single user assigned to that Role (`crm_job_id`) has their security groups, access rules, and permissions **automatically updated in real-time**.\n- You **never** need to configure access manually user by user.\n- Super Admins are automatically protected and never downgraded.\n\nThe entire permission and organizational structure is 100% centralized under **Quick Access > Organization > Roles & Permissions**!"}

{"step_index":2840,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:22:09Z","content":"Aha! When you selected the Job Position for the employee, **Equipment Master immediately filtered to own records** because our security rule worked!\n\nNow, here is the exact architecture to make **AMC Contracts** and **Service Tickets** also filter to \"Own Records\":\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Core Architecture for Service Tickets:\nIn `service.ticket`, a ticket belongs to a user in **two ways**:\n1. `engineer_id = user.id` (The ticket is **assigned** to that technician/engineer to work on).\n2. `create_uid = user.id` (The employee **created** the ticket).\n3. *(Optional)* `equipment_id.user_id = user.id` (The machine belongs to that sales/service rep).\n\n#### Security Rule in XML:\n```xml\n<record id=\"rule_service_ticket_own\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n    <field name=\"name\">Service Ticket: Own Records Only</field>\n    <field name=\"model_id\" ref=\"model_service_ticket\"/>\n    <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('group_equipment_own'))]\"/>\n    <field name=\"domain_force\">['|', ('engineer_id', '=', user.id), '|', ('create_uid', '=', user.id), ('equipment_id.user_id', '=', user.id)]</field>\n</record>\n\n<record id=\"rule_service_ticket_all\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n    <field name=\"name\">Service Ticket: All Records</field>\n    <field name=\"model_id\" ref=\"model_service_ticket\"/>\n    <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('group_equipment_all'))]\"/>\n    <field name=\"domain_force\">[(1, '=', 1)]</field>\n</record>\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. The Core Architecture for AMC Contracts:\nIn `amc.contract`, an AMC belongs to a user in **two ways**:\n1. `create_uid = user.id` (The employee created/sold the AMC).\n2. `line_ids.equipment_id.user_id = user.id` (The AMC covers an equipment belonging to this rep).\n\n#### Security Rule in XML:\n```xml\n<record id=\"rule_amc_contract_own\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n    <field name=\"name\">AMC Contract: Own Records Only</field>\n    <field name=\"model_id\" ref=\"model_amc_contract\"/>\n    <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('group_equipment_own'))]\"/>\n    <field name=\"domain_force\">['|', ('create_uid', '=', user.id), ('line_ids.equipment_id.user_id', '=', user.id)]</field>\n</record>\n\n<record id=\"rule_amc_contract_all\" model=\"ir.rule\">\n    <field name=\"name\">AMC Contract: All Records</field>\n    <field name=\"model_id\" ref=\"model_amc_contract\"/>\n    <field name=\"groups\" eval=\"[(4, ref('group_equipment_all'))]\"/>\n    <field name=\"domain_force\">[(1, '=', 1)]</field>\n</record>\n```\n\n---\n\n### How the Lifecycle Ties Together Automatically:\n```\n               Job Position Permission: \"Own Documents Only\"\n                                    │\n         ┌──────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────┐\n         ▼                          ▼                          ▼\n  Equipment Master            Service Ticket              AMC Contract\n Only equipments where       Only tickets where         Only AMCs where\n user is assigned or         user is assigned           user created or\n is creator                  engineer or creator        covers own equipment\n```\n\nSince the employee already belongs to `group_equipment_own` from their Job Position, adding these rules will **instantly** filter their Service Tickets, AMCs, and Dashboard counts to show **only their own records**!\n\nShall I add these security rules into `multi_company_rules.xml`?"}

{"step_index":2842,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:23:13Z","content":"Here is the practical, end-to-end operational workflow of how **Equipment, AMC Contracts, and Service Tickets** should work together in a real-world CRM business:\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Equipment Installed at Customer (`Equipment Master`)\nWhen a machine is sold or installed:\n1. It is registered in **Equipment Master** with:\n   - Customer Name (`partner_id`)\n   - Model, Serial Number (`serial_number`)\n   - **Assigned Service Engineer / Rep** (`user_id`): *e.g., Dhruvil Shah*\n   - Initial Warranty Dates (`warranty_start_date`, `warranty_end_date`)\n2. **Access Effect:** Only Dhruvil Shah (and Admin) can see and manage this machine.\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Customer Signs an Annual Contract (`AMC Contract`)\nAfter warranty expires (or alongside sale), an AMC is created:\n1. Create new **AMC Contract**:\n   - Customer: *ABC Pharma*\n   - Duration: *1 Year (01-Jan to 31-Dec)*\n   - Visited quota: *4 PM (Preventive Maintenance) visits per year*\n2. Under **Equipment Lines**, add the machine:\n   - When Dhruvil opens the Equipment dropdown, **he only sees the machines assigned to him**.\n3. **Status Flow:** `Draft` ➔ `Active`.\n4. **Access Effect:** Because Dhruvil is the assigned rep for that machine (or created the AMC), this AMC appears in Dhruvil's dashboard. Other reps do not see it.\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Service Request or Preventive Maintenance (`Service Ticket`)\nWhen a customer calls with a breakdown OR a scheduled PM visit is due:\n\n#### Scenario A: Scheduled PM Call (Contracted Visit)\n1. Rep creates **Service Ticket**:\n   - Complaint Type: **PM**\n   - Select Equipment: *WPS-0001* (Auto-fills customer, site, model, serial no).\n   - **AMC Link:** The system auto-links the active AMC contract (`amc_id`).\n   - Assign Engineer (`engineer_id`): *e.g., Dhruvil*.\n2. **Access Effect:** Only Dhruvil sees this ticket in his dashboard under \"Service Tickets\".\n\n#### Scenario B: Emergency Breakdown Call\n1. Rep/Customer logs ticket:\n   - Complaint Type: **Breakdown**\n   - Select Equipment: Auto-detects if machine is covered under warranty or AMC.\n   - Status: `Open` ➔ `In Progress`.\n2. Technician visits site, records root cause, parts used, customer signs on screen (`customer_signature`).\n3. Status: Marked `Completed`.\n4. **Auto-Update on Equipment:** \n   - Equipment Master automatically updates `last_breakdown_date` and `last_preventive_maintenance` dates!\n\n#### Scenario C: Ad-hoc / Free Call (Machine Not in Master)\n1. Technician creates a ticket without selecting an equipment (`equipment_id` is blank).\n2. Manually enters customer name, issue, and resolution.\n3. Completely independent ticket, no master asset needed.\n\n---\n\n### Summary of How the System Behaves for Users:\n\n| Role / User | Equipment Master | AMC Contracts | Service Tickets |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **Field Engineer (Dhruvil)** | Only machines assigned to Dhruvil | Only AMCs covering Dhruvil's machines | Only tickets assigned to Dhruvil or created by him |\n| **Service Manager / Admin** | All machines in company | All company AMCs | All company tickets |\n\nThis ensures complete data privacy between reps, accurate technician workloads, and seamless tracking from machine installation to AMC and breakdown service!"}

{"step_index":2844,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:27:48Z","content":"To make the workflow between **Equipment Master, AMC Contracts, and Service Tickets** 100% complete and automated, here are the **4 high-value fields** that are recommended:\n\n---\n\n### 1. In `amc.contract` (AMC Contract):\n* **`user_id` (Account Manager / Service Lead)**:\n  - *Why needed:* Right now AMC has customer and lines, but no primary assigned user field! Adding `user_id` (defaulting to current user) allows the contract to be explicitly owned by the rep who handles that account.\n* **`visit_count` / `remaining_pm_visits` (Computed Integer)**:\n  - *Why needed:* If contract has 4 PM visits, when a PM Service Ticket is marked `Completed`, this field automatically shows `Visits Completed: 1 / 4` (3 remaining).\n\n---\n\n### 2. In `service.ticket` (Service Ticket):\n* **`contract_coverage` (Computed Badge / Selection)**:\n  - *Options:* `[Under Warranty]` | `[Under Active AMC]` | `[Out of Warranty / Chargeable]`\n  - *Why needed:* When the technician selects an equipment, this badge immediately alerts them whether the service is free (under warranty/AMC) or if they must bill the customer for parts and labor.\n\n---\n\n### 3. In `equipment.master` (Equipment Master):\n* **`active_amc_id` (Many2one to `amc.contract`, Computed/Stored)**:\n  - *Why needed:* Shows directly on the equipment card which AMC contract is currently active for this machine, with a 1-click link to view the contract.\n* **`ticket_count` (Smart Button Stat)**:\n  - *Why needed:* A stat button on the equipment header showing `[3 Service Tickets]`, allowing the engineer to view the full service history of that machine in 1 click.\n\n---\n\n### Priority Recommendation:\nThe most important one right now is **`user_id` on `amc.contract`** — this completes the security rule so AMCs are seamlessly filtered for each user just like Leads and Equipments.\n\nWould you like me to add `user_id` to `amc.contract` and link the security rules for AMC & Tickets?"}

`( ) No` — Cannot view or access Service Tickets.\n   - `(o) User: Own Documents Only` — Can only view tickets assigned to them or created by them.\n   - `( ) User: All Documents` — Can view all company service tickets.\n   - `( ) Administrator` — Can assign, close, delete, and configure tickets.\n\n2. **AMC Contracts (`perm_amc`)**:\n   - `( ) No` — Cannot view or access AMC Contracts.\n   - `(o) User: Own Documents Only` — Can only view AMCs covering their own equipments or created by them.\n   - `( ) User: All Documents` — Can view all company AMC contracts.\n   - `( ) Administrator` — Full commercial control over AMC terms, renewals, and pricing.\n\n---\n\n### Code snippet ready to add into `res_users_signature_views.xml`:\n\n```xml\n<field name=\"perm_service_ticket\" widget=\"radio\" options=\"{'horizontal': true}\"/>\n<field name=\"perm_amc\" widget=\"radio\" options=\"{'horizontal': true}\"/>\n```\n\nWould you like me to add `perm_service_ticket` and `perm_amc` to `ResUsers` and `HrJob` so they appear as clean horizontal radio buttons right alongside Equipment Master?"}

Field Definitions (Added to BOTH `ResUsers` and `HrJob`)\n\nIn `addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py`:\n\n```python\n    perm_service_ticket = fields.Selection([\n        ('none', 'No'),\n        ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n        ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n        ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n    ], string='Service Tickets', default='own')\n\n    perm_amc = fields.Selection([\n        ('none', 'No'),\n        ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n        ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n        ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n    ], string='AMC Contracts', default='own')\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. Group Sync Logic (Inside `_apply_job_permissions`)\n\nIn `_apply_job_permissions(self, job)`:\n\n```python\n            # 1. Service Ticket Permissions\n            g_ticket_own = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_service_ticket_own', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            g_ticket_all = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_service_ticket_all', raise_if_not_found=False)\n\n            if g_ticket_own and g_ticket_all:\n                self.env.cr.execute(\"DELETE FROM res_groups_users_rel WHERE uid = %s AND gid IN (%s, %s)\", (user.id, g_ticket_own.id, g_ticket_all.id))\n                if job.perm_service_ticket == 'own':\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_ticket_own.id, user.id))\n                elif job.perm_service_ticket in ('all', 'admin'):\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_ticket_all.id, user.id))\n\n            # 2. AMC Contract Permissions\n            g_amc_own = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_amc_own', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            g_amc_all = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_amc_all', raise_if_not_found=False)\n\n            if g_amc_own and g_amc_all:\n                self.env.cr.execute(\"DELETE FROM res_groups_users_rel WHERE uid = %s AND gid IN (%s, %s)\", (user.id, g_amc_own.id, g_amc_all.id))\n                if job.perm_amc == 'own':\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_amc_own.id, user.id))\n                elif job.perm_amc in ('all', 'admin'):\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_amc_all.id, user.id))\n\n            # 3. Also update the user's stored permission fields\n            user.sudo().write({\n                'perm_service_ticket': job.perm_service_ticket,\n                'perm_amc': job.perm_amc,\n            })\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. In `HrJob.write()` Hook:\nAdd `perm_service_ticket` and `perm_amc` to `perm_keys` so modifying them on the Role automatically pushes to all assigned users:\n\n```python\n    perm_keys = [\n        'perm_lead_quote', 'perm_product', 'perm_contact', \n        'perm_export', 'perm_company', 'perm_equipment',\n        'perm_service_ticket', 'perm_amc'\n    ]\n```\n\nThis follows the **exact same architecture** as `perm_equipment` and `perm_lead_quote`!"}

{"step_index":2877,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:31:16Z","content":"To add **Service Tickets** and **AMC Contracts** to the Role-based permissions matrix (like Equipment Master), here is the Python logic and the exact files involved:\n\n---\n\n### 1. What is the Python Logic for?\nThe Python logic does **3 things**:\n1. **Defines the fields** on both `res.users` (single user) and `hr.job` (Role / Job Position):\n   - `perm_service_ticket`: `[('none', 'No'), ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'), ('all', 'User: All Documents'), ('admin', 'Administrator')]`\n   - `perm_amc`: `[('none', 'No'), ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'), ('all', 'User: All Documents'), ('admin', 'Administrator')]`\n2. **Assigns / Revokes Security Groups (`_apply_job_permissions`)**:\n   - When a Role has `own`, Python links the user to `group_service_ticket_own` / `group_amc_own`.\n   - When a Role has `all` or `admin`, Python links the user to `group_service_ticket_all` / `group_amc_all`.\n3. **1-Way Auto-Sync (`HrJob.write`)**:\n   - When an Admin changes the radio button on a Job Position / Role, `HrJob.write()` immediately finds all employees with that role and updates their user record + group memberships in real time.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Files Needed for the Whole Feature\nTo complete Service Tickets and AMC permissions completely, only **4 files** are touched:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| 1. [`res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py) | Python logic: fields, group syncing, and `write()` trigger |\n| 2. [`amc_contract.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py) | Add `user_id = fields.Many2one('res.users', default=lambda self: self.env.user)` so Odoo knows who owns the AMC contract |\n| 3. [`multi_company_rules.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/security/multi_company_rules.xml) | Define groups and record rules (`engineer_id == user.id` for tickets, `user_id == user.id` for AMCs) |\n| 4. [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) | XML view: Add the radio buttons on the Role (`hr.job`) form and dropdowns on User form |\n\n---\n\n### 3. Exact Python Snippet to Add in [`res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py)\n\n#### A. In `ResUsers` (around line 30):\n```python\n    perm_service_ticket = fields.Selection([\n        ('none', 'No'),\n        ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n        ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n        ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n    ], string='Service Ticket', default='own')\n\n    perm_amc = fields.Selection([\n        ('none', 'No'),\n        ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n        ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n        ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n    ], string='AMC Contract', default='own')\n```\n\n#### B. In `_apply_job_permissions` (syncing groups):\n```python\n            # Service Ticket permissions\n            g_st_own = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_service_ticket_own', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            g_st_all = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_service_ticket_all', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            if g_st_own and g_st_all:\n                self.env.cr.execute(\"DELETE FROM res_groups_users_rel WHERE uid = %s AND gid IN (%s, %s)\", (user.id, g_st_own.id, g_st_all.id))\n                if job.perm_service_ticket == 'own':\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_st_own.id, user.id))\n                elif job.perm_service_ticket in ('all', 'admin'):\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_st_all.id, user.id))\n\n            # AMC Contract permissions\n            g_amc_own = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_amc_own', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            g_amc_all = self.env.ref('custom_crm_extended.group_amc_all', raise_if_not_found=False)\n            if g_amc_own and g_amc_all:\n                self.env.cr.execute(\"DELETE FROM res_groups_users_rel WHERE uid = %s AND gid IN (%s, %s)\", (user.id, g_amc_own.id, g_amc_all.id))\n                if job.perm_amc == 'own':\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_amc_own.id, user.id))\n                elif job.perm_amc in ('all', 'admin'):\n                    self.env.cr.execute(\"INSERT INTO res_groups_users_rel (gid, uid) VALUES (%s, %s) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING\", (g_amc_all.id, user.id))\n```\n\n#### C. {"step_index":2889,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:36:55Z","content":"Understood! I have paused the previous task and saved all notes regarding **Service Tickets & AMC Contracts** permissions.\n\nNow focusing on the **Invoice Status column**:\n\n### The Problem:\nIn standard Odoo, standard `invoice_status` has values like:\n- `'no'` ➔ displays **\"Nothing to Invoice\"** (even after customer invoices are created or when an order is draft/cancelled)\n- `'to invoice'` ➔ displays **\"To Invoice\"**\n- `'invoiced'` ➔ displays **\"Fully Invoiced\"**\n\n### What You Want:\nYou want **only 2 simple statuses** shown in that column:\n1. **Invoice Created** (when customer invoice is generated/done)\n2. **Invoice Pending** (when quotation/sale order has not been invoiced yet)\n\n---\n\n### Implementation Plan:\n\n1. **Add a Custom Computed Field in [`sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/sale_order.py)**:\n   ```python\n   x_custom_invoice_status = fields.Selection([\n       ('created', 'Invoice Created'),\n       ('pending', 'Invoice Pending'),\n   ], string='Invoice Status', compute='_compute_custom_invoice_status', store=True)\n\n   @api.depends('invoice_ids', 'invoice_ids.state')\n   def _compute_custom_invoice_status(self):\n       for order in self:\n           # If there is at least one posted/draft customer invoice linked to this sale order\n           valid_invoices = order.invoice_ids.filtered(lambda inv: inv.state != 'cancel')\n           if valid_invoices:\n               order.x_custom_invoice_status = 'created'\n           else:\n               order.x_custom_invoice_status = 'pending'\n   ```\n\n2. **In the Quotation / Order List Views ([`sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml))**:\n   - Replace or override the standard `invoice_status` column with `x_custom_invoice_status` widget badge (e.g. green for `Invoice Created`, orange/muted for `Invoice Pending`).\n\nWould you like me to go ahead and implement this now?"}

{"step_index":2897,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:39:26Z","content":"In your CRM system, Quotations have these specific stages in [`sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/sale_order.py#L175-L188):\n\n1. **`draft`** (Draft)\n2. **`prepared`** (Quote Prepared)\n3. **`sent`** (Quote Sent)\n4. **`po_received`** (PO Received)\n5. **`won`** (Won / Sales Order confirmed)\n6. **`lost`** (Lost)\n\n---\n\n### Which Stages Should Show the Invoice Status?\n\nHere is the recommended logic for your business workflow:\n\n| Stage | Invoice Status Behavior | Rationale |\n|---|---|---|\n| **`draft`**, **`prepared`**, **`sent`** | **Hide / Blank** (or not shown) | The deal is still in discussion/negotiation; invoicing is not expected yet. |\n| **`po_received`** | **Invoice Pending** (or **Invoice Created** if already billed) | Customer sent PO; billing process starts now! |\n| **`won`** | **Invoice Created** or **Invoice Pending** | The deal is closed/won. Sales team needs to see clearly whether accounting has raised the invoice or if it is still pending. |\n| **`lost`** | **Hide / Blank** | Deal is lost; no invoice needed. |\n\n---\n\n### Two Options for How You Want it in the List View:\n\n1. **Option A (Show ONLY on Won & PO Received stages)**:\n   - For `draft`, `prepared`, `sent`, `lost`: column is **blank** (or `-`).\n   - For `po_received` and `won`: shows **Invoice Created** (Green) or **Invoice Pending** (Orange/Yellow).\n\n2. **Option B (Show across ALL stages)**:\n   - Every single record in the list shows either **Invoice Created** (if an invoice exists) or **Invoice Pending** (if no invoice exists yet).\n\nWhich option matches what you have in mind? (Option A or Option B?)"}

{"step_index":2915,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:41:52Z","content":"Based on your dashboard screenshot:\n\nYou have the Quotation pipeline stages:\n1. **Quotes** (`draft`)\n2. **Sent** (`sent`)\n3. **Negotiation** (`negotiation`)\n4. **Order Expected** (`order_expected`)\n5. **Won** (`won`)\n\nNotice directly above **Won**, your dashboard specifically tracks:\n- **`INVOICE CREATED`** (currently `1`)\n- **`INVOICE PENDING`** (currently `2`)\n\nAnd in the code ([`dashboard.js:L534`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L534) and [`L546`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L546)):\nBoth **Invoice Created** and **Invoice Pending** are counted **only for `Won` orders**!\n\n---\n\n### In the List View:\nYou should show this status **ONLY on the `Won` stage** (or when viewing Won Deals / Invoiced Orders):\n\n- **Quotes / Sent / Negotiation / Order Expected**: Invoice status should be **blank** (or hidden) because the deal is not won yet and cannot be invoiced.\n- **Won**: Shows exactly one of two values:\n  - 🟢 **Invoice Created** (if customer invoice is generated)\n  - 🟠 **Invoice Pending** (if customer invoice is not generated yet)\n\nThis matches your dashboard numbers 100% (1 Won is Invoiced, 2 are Invoice Pending).\n\nDoes this match what you want? If yes, I will add this exact logic and badge to the list view!"}

{"step_index":2935,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:43:31Z","content":"Got it! \n\n### Logic Breakdown for the List View:\n\n1. **Which Stage shows it?**\n   - **`Won`** stage ONLY.\n   - For other stages (*Quotes, Sent, Negotiation, Order Expected*), the column stays clean / blank because those deals haven't been won yet.\n\n2. **The 2 Statuses on Won records:**\n   - 🟢 **Invoice Created** (when `x_invoice_date` is entered or a customer invoice is generated).\n   - 🟠 **Invoice Pending** (when it is in `Won` stage, but no invoice has been created yet).\n\n---\n\n### Implementation Details:\n\n#### 1. You can either:\n\n### Option 1: Replace standard `invoice_status` (Recommended)\nThis replaces the standard column directly:\n\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Place it after `state` (if `invoice_status` is not in that tree view):\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='state']\" position=\"after\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n### Also for Sales Orders List (`view_order_tree`):\nSince Won quotes become Sales Orders, to show it in the **Sales Orders** list as well, add this block right below `view_sale_order_list_custom`:\n\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.tree.custom.invoice.status</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_order_tree\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```"}

{"step_index":2973,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:54:37Z","content":"The reason it didn't change is because of **two things**:\n\n### 1. View ID in Odoo\nYou inherited `sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding`, but the list view opened by **\"Invoiced Orders\"**, **\"Invoice Pending Orders\"**, and **\"Won Deals\"** is the **Sales Orders list view**:\n👉 `sale.view_order_tree` (which inherits `sale.view_quotation_tree`).\n\n### 2. Module Upgrade Required\nBecause you added a new Python field (`x_custom_invoice_status`) and modified XML, restarting the service alone is **not enough**—Odoo must update the database schema via module upgrade:\n```bash\n-u custom_crm_extended\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Add the view inheritance for `sale.view_order_tree`\nIn [`views/sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml), right below `view_sale_order_list_custom`, add this view so both Quotations and Orders lists get replaced:\n\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.tree.custom.invoice.status</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_order_tree\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\nAlso, in `view_sale_order_list_custom` change the target to `sale.view_quotation_tree` (or include both).\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: On GCP SSH Run:\n```bash\ngit pull\nsudo systemctl stop crm-test\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm-test\n```\n\nShall I edit [`views/sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml) with both view records for you now?"}

{"step_index":2981,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T05:57:15Z","content":"Yes, and here is **why** there are two:\n\nIn Odoo, **Quotations** and **Sales Orders** use two **different list views**:\n\n1. **`sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding`**: \n   - Used when viewing **Quotations** (New, Sent, Negotiation, Order Expected).\n2. **`sale.view_order_tree`**: \n   - Used when viewing **Won Deals**, **Invoiced Orders**, and **Invoice Pending Orders** (as seen in your screenshot).\n\nIf you only put it in the first one, the Quotation list changes, but when you click **\"Invoiced Orders\"** or **\"Invoice Pending Orders\"** from the dashboard, it opens the second view (`view_order_tree`)—which is why it was still showing the old \"Nothing to Invoice\".\n\nHaving both ensures the column is replaced everywhere!"}

{"step_index":2985,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:00:13Z","content":"There are **3 great options** to handle the other stages:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: Clean Dash `—` or \"Not Applicable\" (Recommended & Best UX)\nInstead of leaving it empty/blank, show a subtle grey badge `—` or `N/A` for early stages so the column doesn't feel missing:\n\nIn [`models/sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py):\n```python\n    x_custom_invoice_status = fields.Selection([\n        ('created', 'Invoice Created'),\n        ('pending', 'Invoice Pending'),\n        ('na', '—'),\n    ], string='Invoice Status', compute='_compute_custom_invoice_status', store=True)\n\n    @api.depends('x_quote_stage', 'x_invoice_date', 'x_invoice_number', 'invoice_ids', 'invoice_ids.state')\n    def _compute_custom_invoice_status(self):\n        for order in self:\n            if order.x_quote_stage == 'won':\n                has_inv = (\n                    bool(order.x_invoice_date) or \n                    bool(order.x_invoice_number) or \n                    bool(order.invoice_ids.filtered(lambda inv: inv.state != 'cancel'))\n                )\n                order.x_custom_invoice_status = 'created' if has_inv else 'pending'\n            else:\n                order.x_custom_invoice_status = 'na'\n```\nIn XML badge decoration:\n```xml\ndecoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \ndecoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\"\ndecoration-muted=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'na'\"\n```\n**Why this is great**: The table aligns neatly, users see a subtle grey dash `—` knowing invoicing only starts at Won.\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Remove the column entirely from Quotations (`view_quotation_tree`)\nSince Quotations (Draft, Sent, Negotiation, Order Expected) never need invoices, **only show Invoice Status in Sales Orders (`view_order_tree`)**:\n\n- In `view_sale_order_list_custom` (Quotations list): **Hide** the column completely with `<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"attributes\"><attribute name=\"column_invisible\">1</attribute></xpath>`.\n- In `view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status` (Won / Invoiced / Orders): Keep `x_custom_invoice_status`.\n\n**Why this is great**: When sales reps view raw quotations, they don't even see the invoice column taking up screen width. But when viewing Won Deals, the column is right there!\n\n---\n\n### Option 3: Dynamic Hide in List View via `column_invisible`\nHide the column automatically if the filter/domain is not viewing Won quotes.\n\n---\n\nWhich approach do you prefer:\n- **Option 1 (Show a clean `—` dash on non-won stages)**, or \n- **Option 2 (Hide the invoice column completely on Quotations and only show it on Won/Orders list)**?"}

{"step_index":2991,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:02:48Z","content":"### 1. In Which Stage is the Invoice Created?\n\nThe invoice is created **ONLY in the `Won` stage**:\n- When a deal is moved to **Won** (PO received and verified), the Quotation becomes a confirmed Sales Order.\n- The user can then:\n  1. Click **\"Create Invoice\"** to generate the customer invoice directly in Odoo accounting.\n  2. Or fill in **\"Invoice No\"** and **\"Invoice Date\"** in the **Handoff / Details** tab.\n- All prior stages (`draft`, `sent`, `negotiation`, `order_expected`) are presales/pipeline stages where **NO invoice can or should exist**.\n\n---\n\n### 2. How to Hide the Column on ALL Stages Except `Won`\n\nTo completely hide the Invoice Status column from Quotation stages (`draft`, `sent`, `negotiation`, `order_expected`) and **only show it on Won / Orders**, we simply:\n\n1. **Remove / Hide it from the Quotations list view** (`view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding`).\n2. **Keep it in the Sales Orders / Won list view** (`view_order_tree`).\n\nHere is the exact change for [`views/sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml):\n\n```xml\n    <!-- 1. QUOTATION LIST: Completely hide invoice status for draft, sent, negotiation, etc. -->\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n            <!-- Completely hide the column here -->\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"column_invisible\">1</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n\n    <!-- 2. SALES ORDERS / WON LIST: Show the 2 clean statuses (Invoice Created / Invoice Pending) -->\n    <record id=\"view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.tree.custom.invoice.status</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_order_tree\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       optional=\"show\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\n### Result:\n- When you click **Quotes, Sent, Negotiation, or Order Expected** from the dashboard: the **Invoice Status column is completely hidden** (not shown at all).\n- When you click **Won Deals**, **Invoiced Orders**, or **Invoice Pending Orders**: the column is **visible**, showing either 🟢 **Invoice Created** or 🟠 **Invoice Pending**.\n\nShall I apply this update to [`sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml) for you?"}

{"step_index":3006,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:05:33Z","content":"The reason you still see it is because **`column_invisible=\"1\"` in Odoo hides a column statically**, but if the user has previously toggled or viewed columns, or if Odoo list view evaluation sees `optional=\"show\"`, Odoo still renders the column header or falls back to default.\n\nEven better: in Odoo list views, you can hide a column **dynamically based on the stage** using `column_invisible=\"parent.x_quote_stage != 'won'\"` or by **removing the node completely** using `position=\"replace\"` with nothing (empty) on `sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding`!\n\n### Here is why:\nWhen you use:\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"attributes\">\n    <attribute name=\"column_invisible\">1</attribute>\n</xpath>\n```\nThe field is still present in the view with `optional=\"show\"` inherited from standard Odoo.\n\n### The Clean Solution:\nReplace line 11-13 in [`sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml) with:\n\n```xml\n    <!-- 1. QUOTATION LIST: Completely remove invoice_status from Quotation stages -->\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath> \n            <!-- Completely delete/remove the field from this view -->\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\"/>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\nNotice `<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\"/>` with **no content inside**:\nThis tells Odoo: **\"Completely remove this column from the Quotation table\"**.\n\nShall I update that line for you now?"}

{"step_index":3017,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:32:57Z","content":"Look at your screenshot and your code:\n\nNotice that under the column header **Invoice Status** for \"Negotiation Quotations\":\n👉 It is showing **`Invoice Created`** badge (faint green)!\n\n### Why did that happen?\nBecause when Odoo opens `views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]]` without specifying a specific view ID, Odoo uses **`sale.view_order_tree`** (Sales Order list view) as its default list view!\n\nAnd inside [`view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml#L15-L29), you put:\n```xml\n<field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" ... />\n```\n\nSo `view_order_tree` is showing that column for **EVERY stage**, including Negotiation!\n\n---\n\n### The Solution:\nIn Odoo 18, to hide this column when viewing stages other than Won, you simply add:\n```xml\ncolumn_invisible=\"x_quote_stage != 'won'\"\n```\n*(or via the list context/domain)*. \n\nOR, even cleaner, in [`models/sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py):\nCheck your `_compute_custom_invoice_status` method in [`models/sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py):\nWhy is it showing \"Invoice Created\" for REF0002 and REF0003 in Negotiation?\nLet's check lines 270-285 in [`models/sale_order.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py)."}

{"step_index":3024,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:34:36Z","content":"Two things happened here:\n\n### 1. You put `column_invisible` on `<xpath>`, which is invalid XML in Odoo\nIn Odoo, `<xpath>` cannot have `column_invisible` attribute! It belongs on `<field>` or `<attribute>` inside xpath.\n\n### 2. The view being rendered is `view_order_tree` (lines 15–29)!\nYou modified line 11 (in `view_sale_order_list_custom`), but your screen is displaying **`sale.view_order_tree`** (defined in line 20)! That is why line 21 is active:\n```xml\n<field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" ... optional=\"show\"/>\n```\n\nIn Odoo, when a column has `column_invisible`, in a list view it evaluates against the context or parent. But when you want to hide a column dynamically based on whether you are viewing Won quotes:\n\nIn [`views/sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml), on lines 21–27 inside `view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status`:\n\nPut `column_invisible=\"context.get('hide_invoice_status')\"` or `column_invisible=\"context.get('default_x_quote_stage') != 'won'\"`:\n\n```xml\n    <record id=\"view_sale_order_list_custom\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.list.custom.buttons</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_quotation_tree_with_onboarding\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//list\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"create\">true</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\"/>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n\n    <record id=\"view_order_tree_custom_invoice_status\" model=\"ir.ui.view\">\n        <field name=\"name\">sale.order.tree.custom.invoice.status</field>\n        <field name=\"model\">sale.order</field>\n        <field name=\"inherit_id\" ref=\"sale.view_order_tree\"/>\n        <field name=\"arch\" type=\"xml\">\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='invoice_status']\" position=\"replace\">\n                <field name=\"x_custom_invoice_status\" \n                       string=\"Invoice Status\" \n                       widget=\"badge\" \n                       decoration-success=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'created'\" \n                       decoration-warning=\"x_custom_invoice_status == 'pending'\" \n                       column_invisible=\"context.get('hide_invoice_status', False)\"/>\n            </xpath>\n        </field>\n    </record>\n```\n\nAnd in [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L332):\nIn `openQuoteStage(stage)`:\n```javascript\ncontext: { \n    allowed_company_ids: this.state.selectedCompanies, \n    create: false,\n    hide_invoice_status: stage !== 'won'\n}\n```\n\nThis tells Odoo:\n- If `stage !== 'won'` (like Negotiation, Quotes, Sent, Order Expected) ➔ `hide_invoice_status: true` ➔ **The entire column disappears completely**!\n- If `stage === 'won'` (or Invoiced / Invoice Pending) ➔ `hide_invoice_status: false` ➔ **The column appears with the green / orange badges**!\n\nShall I apply this exact change in both files for you?"}

{"step_index":3038,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:37:31Z","content":"I understand your frustration, and I sincerely apologize. \n\nHere is **the exact reason why it hasn't changed on your screen**:\n\nLook at `sync.ps1`:\n```bash\ngit pull && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\nA **systemctl restart only restarts the Python server**. It **NEVER re-reads or applies XML views into the Odoo database**! \nIn Odoo, XML view changes (`views/sale_order_views.xml`) are stored in the PostgreSQL database table `ir_ui_view`. When you just restart `crm-test`, Odoo loads the **old XML from the database**, completely ignoring the new XML you pushed!\n\n### The Fix Right Now:\nYou must run the **module upgrade** command on GCP SSH so Odoo actually updates the database views:\n\nRun this in GCP SSH:\n```bash\ngit pull\nsudo systemctl stop crm-test\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm-test\n```\n\nAfter this finishes and you refresh your browser, Odoo will have the updated views loaded into the database!"}

{"step_index":3041,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:38:00Z","content":"Yes, all your code is already committed and pushed to GitHub (`main`)!\n\nNow simply run this **one command** in your GCP SSH terminal to upgrade the module into the database:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm-test && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm-test\n```\n\nOnce that finishes, hard refresh your browser (`Ctrl + Shift + R`), and the views will update immediately."}

{"step_index":3050,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:38:51Z","content":"The reason is clear now! Look closely at these 2 lines in your codebase:\n\nIn [`views/sale_order_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml#L26):\n```xml\ncolumn_invisible=\"context.get('hide_invoice_status', False)\"\n```\nThis tells Odoo: **\"Only hide this column IF `hide_invoice_status` is passed in the context.\"**\n\nBUT in [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L332):\n```javascript\ncontext: { allowed_company_ids: this.state.selectedCompanies, create: false }\n```\n**`hide_invoice_status` was NEVER added to `dashboard.js`!** So `context.get('hide_invoice_status')` is always `False`, and Odoo shows the column on every single stage!\n\n---\n\n### The Fix (in 2 steps):\n\n#### 1. In [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L332):\nPass `hide_invoice_status: stage !== 'won'` when clicking any quotation stage:\n\n```javascript\n        this.go({\n            type: \"ir.actions.act_window\",\n            name: (labels[stage] || stage) + \" Quotations\",\n            res_model: \"sale.order\",\n            views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]],\n            domain: [...stageDomain, ...ud, ...cd],\n            context: { \n                allowed_company_ids: this.state.selectedCompanies, \n                create: false,\n                hide_invoice_status: stage !== 'won'\n            }\n        });\n```\n\n#### 2. {"step_index":3073,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T06:59:18Z","content":"**Yes, absolutely!** \n\nIn Odoo, **\"Customers\"** and **\"Contacts\"** are the exact same model: **`res.partner`**.\n- When you open **\"Customers\"** from the dashboard:\n  ```javascript\n  res_model: \"res.partner\", domain: [[\"customer_rank\", \">\", 0]]\n  ```\n- And in the permissions logic:\n  **Contact Creation** controls the group **`base.group_partner_manager`** (Contact Creation & Management).\n\n### How it works:\n1. If a role has **Contact Creation = `Creation` (Yes)**:\n   - The user gets permission to create both new **Contacts** and new **Customers**.\n2. {"step_index":3085,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:00:42Z","content":"**Yes, exactly!** \n\nIn [`exhibition_contact.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/exhibition_contacts/models/exhibition_contact.py#L365-L376), there is a button:\n👉 **\"Convert to Lead\"** (or `action_create_lead`):\n\nWhen clicked:\n1. New 4-level Radio Fields\nperm_service_ticket = fields.Selection([\n    ('none', 'No'),\n    ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n    ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n    ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n], string='Service Ticket', default='own')\n\nperm_amc = fields.Selection([\n    ('none', 'No'),\n    ('own', 'User: Own Documents Only'),\n    ('all', 'User: All Documents'),\n    ('admin', 'Administrator'),\n], string='AMC Contract', default='own')\n\n# 2. {"step_index":3089,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:08:36Z","content":"You asked a very sharp and fundamental question about Odoo's architecture:\n\n> **\"If permissions are defined in CSV, why do we need Python logic and UI? Doesn't the CSV manage permissions?\"**\n\nHere is the exact answer explaining how the **CSV**, **Python Logic**, and **UI** work together:\n\n---\n\n### 1. What the CSV (`ir.model.access.csv`) Actually Does\nThe CSV is **static and group-based**:\n- It simply says: \n  *\"Members of **Group A** have Create/Read/Write/Delete rights on Model X.\"*\n- **The CSV does NOT know which individual user is inside Group A.**\n- **The CSV CANNOT filter records** (e.g. it cannot say *\"Only show John his own records, but show Manager everyone's records\"*—that requires `ir.rule` record rules).\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why the UI is Needed\n- Normal managers or HR administrators in your company do **NOT** have access to the code, terminal, or raw CSV files.\n- The **UI (Roles & Permissions form)** gives administrators a clean visual screen with radio buttons and checkboxes so they can say:\n  - *Sales Executive role ➔ Customer: Create, View (No Delete)*\n  - *Service Engineer role ➔ Service Tickets: Own Documents Only*\n\n---\n\n### 3. What the Python Logic (`res_users.py`) Does (The Bridge!)\nThe Python logic is the **bridge connecting the UI to the CSV groups & rules**:\n\n```\n[Administrator clicks \"Create, View\" in UI]\n                 │\n                 ▼\n     [Python Logic in res_users.py]\n                 │\n   1. Finds the corresponding security group\n   2. Adds/removes the user into the group (res_groups_users_rel table)\n   3. Syncs the changes automatically to all employees with that role\n                 │\n                 ▼\n  [Odoo's CSV ACL & ir.rules take effect in real-time!]\n```\n\n### In Short:\n1. **The CSV** defines *what the groups are allowed to do*.\n2. **The UI** lets managers *choose permissions easily*.\n3. **The Python Logic** *assigns the correct groups/rules to users behind the scenes* based on what was selected in the UI.\n\nWithout the Python logic, changing the radio button in the UI would just be saving text on the screen without actually changing the user's real Odoo access rights!"}

{"step_index":3091,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:09:45Z","content":"I understand completely! You want an **Independent UI-driven Permission System**:\n- The Admin manages permissions **directly from the UI** (Master Role & User pages).\n- You don't want to touch CSV files or reload code every time you adjust a permission.\n- The UI choices **directly control the access**!\n\n---\n\n### How to Make UI Completely Independent:\n\nInstead of relying on hardcoded static CSV lines, we enforce permissions via **2 standard, dynamic layers directly driven by the UI fields**:\n\n#### 1. Button & Action Visibility in UI (XML & Web Client)\nWhen the user toggles a permission in the UI:\n- **`perm_customer_create` is unchecked**:\n  ➔ The **\"New\" / \"Create\"** button on Customers is automatically hidden for that user.\n- **`perm_customer_unlink` is unchecked**:\n  ➔ The **\"Delete\"** action in the Action menu is hidden.\n- **`perm_customer_write` is unchecked**:\n  ➔ The form is set to `readonly=\"1\"`.\n\n#### 2. ORM-Level Enforcement in Python (Dynamic & Bulletproof)\nIn the Python models (`res.partner`, `equipment.master`, `service.ticket`, `amc.contract`), we override `create`, `write`, `unlink`, and `check_access_rights`:\n\n```python\nclass ResPartner(models.Model):\n    _inherit = 'res.partner'\n\n    @api.model_create_multi\n    def create(self, vals_list):\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_customer_create:\n                raise UserError(_(\"Your role does not have permission to Create Customers.\"))\n        return super().create(vals_list)\n\n    def write(self, vals):\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_customer_write:\n                raise UserError(_(\"Your role does not have permission to Edit Customers.\"))\n        return super().write(vals)\n\n    def unlink(self):\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_customer_unlink:\n                raise UserError(_(\"Your role does not have permission to Delete Customers.\"))\n        return super().unlink()\n```\n\n#### 3. Data Scope (No / Own / All / Admin) via Dynamic Record Rule\nFor Service Tickets, AMC, and Equipment:\nA single dynamic rule checks the user's field value in real-time:\n- If `perm == 'own'`: Domain restricts to `[('user_id', '=', user.id)]`\n- If `perm in ('all', 'admin')`: Domain is `[(1, '=', 1)]` (sees everything)\n- If `perm == 'none'`: Domain is `[(0, '=', 1)]` (sees nothing)\n\n---\n\n### Why this is the Best Solution for You:\n1. **Zero CSV dependencies**: You never have to touch `ir.model.access.csv` to tweak permissions.\n2. **Instant & Real-Time**: The moment the Admin checks/unchecks a box or changes a radio button on the Role or User form and clicks Save, it takes effect immediately for those users.\n3. **Super Admin is Safe**: Super Admins (`base.group_system`) bypass restrictions and always retain full access.\n\nShall I proceed with setting up this independent UI-driven permission engine for you?"}
