{"step_index":3093,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:13:22Z","content":"This is the classic, powerful **Enterprise Tree Hierarchy (Reporting & Department Cascading Architecture)**!\n\nHere is the exact structure of your hierarchy rule:\n\n---\n\n### The Hierarchy Rules:\n\n```\n                  ┌──────────────────────────────┐\n                  │       OWNER / ADMIN          │ (Level 1: 100% Full Access across everything)\n                  └──────────────┬───────────────┘\n                                 │\n                  ┌──────────────┴───────────────┐\n                  │         SR. MANAGER          │ (Level 2: Sees All Junior Managers + Employees)\n                  └──────────────┬───────────────┘\n                                 │\n         ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐\n         ▼                                               ▼\n┌─────────────────────────┐                     ┌─────────────────────────┐\n│  DEPT MANAGER (Sales)   │                     │  DEPT MANAGER (Service) │ (Level 3: Sees all data in their Department)\n└────────────┬────────────┘                     └────────────┬────────────┘\n             │                                               │\n    ┌────────┴────────┐                             ┌────────┴────────┐\n    ▼                 ▼                             ▼                 ▼\n[Sales Exec 1]  [Sales Exec 2]                  [Service Eng 1]  [Service Eng 2] (Level 4: Junior - Own Records Only)\n```\n\n1. **Owner / Super Admin (Top Level)**:\n   - Has **100% full access** to all companies, all departments, and all records.\n\n2. **Sr. Managers (Level 2)**:\n   - Can see all data belonging to **Junior Managers and all employees under them**.\n   - Peers at the same Sr. level can see their respective subordinate branches.\n\n3. **Department Managers (Level 3 - Manager 1, 2, 3...)**:\n   - Each Department has a designated Manager.\n   - A Department Manager sees **all records created by or assigned to any employee in their Department** (or anyone reporting to them).\n   - Junior employees **cannot** see their Manager's records or their colleague's records.\n\n4. **Junior Employees (Level 4)**:\n   - Can **only see their own records** (`Own Documents Only`).\n\n---\n\n### How to Implement this in Python (Clean & Scalable)\n\nYou already have on `res.users`:\n- `crm_manager_id` (Reports To)\n- `crm_department_id` (Department)\n- `crm_subordinate_ids` (Subordinates)\n\nWe add a reusable Python helper method on `res.users`:\n\n```python\nclass ResUsers(models.Model):\n    _inherit = 'res.users'\n\n    def get_accessible_subordinate_user_ids(self):\n        \"\"\"\n        Recursively returns all user IDs that report directly or \n        indirectly to this user, plus all users in their department \n        if they are the department manager.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ensure_one()\n        # 1. Super Admins see everything\n        if self.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            return self.env['res.users'].search([]).ids\n\n        accessible_users = {self.id}\n\n        # 2. Check if this user is a Department Manager (e.g. Sales, Service, etc.)\n        managed_depts = self.env['hr.department'].search([('manager_id.user_id', '=', self.id)])\n        if managed_depts:\n            dept_users = self.env['res.users'].search([('crm_department_id', 'in', managed_depts.ids)])\n            accessible_users.update(dept_users.ids)\n\n        # 3. Recursive subordinate traversal (Junior Managers -> Executives)\n        def _get_subordinates(user):\n            subordinates = self.env['res.users'].search([('crm_manager_id', '=', user.id)])\n            for sub in subordinates:\n                if sub.id not in accessible_users:\n                    accessible_users.add(sub.id)\n                    _get_subordinates(sub)\n\n        _get_subordinates(self)\n        return list(accessible_users)\n```\n\n---\n\n### How the Record Rule Uses this:\n\nFor **Leads**, **Quotations**, **Service Tickets**, **Equipment**, and **AMC**:\n\nThe dynamic security domain becomes:\n```python\n['|', ('user_id', 'in', user.get_accessible_subordinate_user_ids()), ('create_uid', 'in', user.get_accessible_subordinate_user_ids())]\n```\n\n### Result:\n- **Junior Employee**: `get_accessible_subordinate_user_ids()` returns only `[JuniorId]` ➔ Sees **only own records**.\n- **Dept Manager**: returns `[ManagerId, Exec1Id, Exec2Id]` ➔ Sees **whole department**.\n- **Sr. Manager**: returns `[SrManagerId, Mgr1Id, Mgr2Id, all their staff...]` ➔ Sees **all junior branches**.\n- **Owner / Admin**: returns **all users** ➔ Sees **100% of records**.\n\nDoes this match your vision for the hierarchy?"}

{"step_index":3095,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:14:07Z","content":"Yes, absolutely understood! \n\nIn real CRM operations:\n- A **Sales Manager / Salesperson** often needs to see **Service Tickets** or **AMC Contracts** for their customers (to check ongoing service complaints, warranty, or after-sales handoffs).\n- A **Service Manager** might need to see **Won Quotations / Equipment Master** to prepare installation or PM visits.\n\n---\n\n### How to Allow Cross-Department Visibility (e.g. Sales seeing Service):\n\nWe give the **Owner / Admin** the exact controls in the UI using **two simple, flexible mechanisms**:\n\n#### Mechanism 1: Role-Based Cross-Module Permission (Recommended & Standard)\nOn the **Roles & Permissions** form (`hr.job`), you independently set each module's scope:\n- **Sales Executive Role**:\n  - `Lead & Quotation`: **Own Documents Only** (their department)\n  - `Service Ticket`: **User: All Documents** *(or Customer-linked)*\n  - `AMC Contract`: **User: All Documents**\n  - `Equipment Master`: **User: All Documents**\n- **Service Engineer Role**:\n  - `Lead & Quotation`: **No** (they don't see raw sales leads/quotes)\n  - `Service Ticket`: **Own Documents Only**\n  - `Equipment Master`: **User: All Documents**\n\n*(Because the permissions are defined per-module, an Owner can allow Sales to see Service without making them a Service Manager!)*\n\n---\n\n#### Mechanism 2: Multi-Department Access (Allowed Departments on User)\nOn the **User Form** (`res.users`), right below Department, we add:\n👉 **`Allowed Additional Departments`** (`crm_allowed_department_ids` - Many2many):\n- For example, for Sales Manager John:\n  - **Primary Department**: `Sales`\n  - **Also View Departments**: `[Service, After-Sales]`\n- The hierarchy engine automatically includes all employees in `Sales` **PLUS** all employees in `Service` in John's accessible list!\n\n---\n\n### Summary of How They Work Together:\n1. **Vertical Hierarchy**: Manager sees their subordinates automatically.\n2. **Horizontal Cross-Department**: \n   - Either by setting the module permission (e.g., Service Ticket = All Documents on the Sales Role),\n   - Or by adding the other department into their **Allowed Additional Departments**.\n\nWhich mechanism do you prefer, or should we enable both?"}

{"step_index":3114,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:18:31Z","content":"You are completely right! Opening 50 or 100 individual user forms one by one to configure who reports to whom is slow, repetitive, and painful.\n\nThe proper enterprise way is to configure the **Hierarchy directly from the Master (in Organization)**!\n\n---\n\n### How to Implement Master-Level Hierarchy Management\n\nIn **Organization ➔ Roles & Permissions** (`hr.job`), we add the Hierarchy Definition:\n\n#### 1. On the Master Role (`hr.job`), add:\n- **`Reports To Role`** (`parent_job_id` - Many2one `hr.job`):\n  - *Example*: Role \"Sales Executive\" ➔ Reports to Role **\"Sales Manager\"**.\n  - *Example*: Role \"Sales Manager\" ➔ Reports to Role **\"General Manager / Director\"**.\n- **`Hierarchy Level`** (`hierarchy_level` - Selection):\n  - `owner`: **Owner / Top Level** (100% full access to all records & companies)\n  - `senior_manager`: **Sr. Manager** (Sees all Junior Managers + their teams)\n  - `dept_manager`: **Department Manager** (Sees all users & records in their department)\n  - `executive`: **Executive / Junior** (Own records only)\n- **`Allowed Cross Departments`** (`allowed_department_ids` - Many2many `hr.department`):\n  - For example, on the \"Sales Manager\" role, you simply check **[Service]**, and all Sales Managers automatically gain visibility into the Service Department records!\n\n---\n\n### How the Magic Auto-Sync Works:\n\nWhen an employee is assigned a Job Position / Role:\n```\n[User is assigned role: \"Sales Executive\"]\n                   │\n                   ▼ (Auto-Sync)\n1. User automatically gets Department = \"Sales\" (from Role)\n2. User automatically reports to the person holding the \"Sales Manager\" role\n3. User inherits all permissions + hierarchy visibility instantly!\n```\n\n### In UI ([`hr.job` Form View](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L73-L81)):\nUnder **Organization**, the Admin sees:\n```xml\n<group string=\"Hierarchy & Organization\">\n    <field name=\"department_id\" string=\"Department\"/>\n    <field name=\"parent_job_id\" string=\"Reports To (Parent Role)\"/>\n    <field name=\"hierarchy_level\" string=\"Hierarchy Level\"/>\n    <field name=\"allowed_department_ids\" widget=\"many2many_tags\" string=\"Cross-Department Access\"/>\n</group>\n```\n\n### Benefits for You:\n1. **Manage in One Place**: Set it up once on the Role (e.g. Sales Executive reports to Sales Manager). Every current and future employee with that role is automatically configured!\n2. **Zero Manual Work on Users**: No need to open individual user pages to set managers and departments.\n3. **Owner has 100% Control**: Change the hierarchy rule in Master, and it immediately cascades to all users!\n\nShall I prepare this master-level hierarchy architecture for you?"}

{"step_index":3148,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:22:05Z","content":"All requested permission fields have been added cleanly to **both the Master Role (`hr.job`)** and the **Single User (`res.users`)** pages!\n\n---\n\n### What Was Done:\n\n1. **[`models/res_users.py`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py)**:\n   - **Service Ticket**: 4 options (`No`, `Own Documents`, `All Documents`, `Administrator`).\n   - **AMC Contract**: 4 options (`No`, `Own Documents`, `All Documents`, `Administrator`).\n   - **Product Catalog**: updated to 4 options (`No`, `Own Documents`, `All Documents`, `Administrator`).\n   - **Customer Creation**: 4 CRUD checkboxes (`Create`, `Update`, `View`, `Delete`).\n   - **Equipment Master**: 4 CRUD checkboxes (`Create`, `Update`, `View`, `Delete`).\n   - **Auto-Sync**: `_apply_job_permissions` and `HrJob.write()` updated to copy all selections and checkboxes from the Role down to all assigned users automatically.\n\n2. **[`views/res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml)**:\n   - **Master Role form (`hr.job`)**:\n     - `Lead & Quotation`, `Service Ticket`, `AMC Contract`, `Product Catalog`, `Excel Export`, `Company Creation` displayed with clean horizontal radio buttons.\n     - `Customer Creation` and `Equipment Master` displayed with horizontal `[ ] Create [ ] Update [ ] View [ ] Delete` checkboxes.\n   - **Single User form (`res.users`)**:\n     - Added all corresponding fields neatly inside the \"Configuration & Masters\" box in the Access Rights tab.\n\n---\n\n### Ready to Test:\nRun:\n```powershell\n.\\sync.ps1\n```\nAnd on GCP SSH:\n```bash\ngit pull\nsudo systemctl stop crm-test\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm-test\n```"}

{"step_index":3156,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:23:13Z","content":"In Odoo, there are **two different forms** for `res.users`:\n1. **Simplified User Form (`base.view_users_form_simple_modif`)**:\n   - Used for My Profile / Preferences (contains NO Access Rights tab, NO Organization tab, only name, email, phone).\n2. **Full Admin Settings Form (`base.view_users_form`)**:\n   - Contains all the tabs: **Access Rights**, **Organization & Hierarchy**, **Quotation Signature Card**, etc.\n\n### Why did the tabs disappear?\nLook at `openUsers()` in [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L397):\n```javascript\nopenUsers() { \n    this.go({ \n        type: \"ir.actions.act_window\", \n        name: \"Users\", \n        res_model: \"res.users\", \n        views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]], \n        domain: [[\"share\", \"=\", false]] \n    }); \n}\n```\nWhen `views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]]` is called without specifying the full admin action or view ID, Odoo defaulted to the **simple preferences form**, which has no tabs!\n\n---\n\n### The Fix in [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L397):\nWe call the official Odoo Admin Users action: **`base.action_res_users`**:\n\n```javascript\n    openUsers() { \n        this.actionService.doAction(\"base.action_res_users\"); \n    }\n```\nOR:\n```javascript\n    openUsers() { \n        this.go({ \n            type: \"ir.actions.act_window\", \n            name: \"Users\", \n            res_model: \"res.users\", \n            views: [[false, \"list\"], [false, \"form\"]], \n            domain: [[\"share\", \"=\", false]],\n            context: { search_default_filter_no_share: 1 }\n        }); \n    }\n```\nUsing `this.actionService.doAction(\"base.action_res_users\")` opens the **full Admin User management form** with all the tabs (**Access Rights**, **Organization & Hierarchy**, **Signature Card**) every single time!\n\nLet me update `openUsers` in [`dashboard.js`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js) now."}

You are the Admin, and Quick Access is **only for Admins** (`t-if=\"state.isAdmin\"`). \n\nPreviously, when Users was at the top level of Quick Access, line 40 was:\n```html\n<a href=\"/app/settings/users\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item\">Users</a>\n```\nNotice that: **`/app/settings/users`** is the direct Odoo route to the **Full Admin Settings User Management** (which loads the complete form with all the tabs: *Access Rights*, *Organization & Hierarchy*, *Signature Card*).\n\nWhen we moved it into the submenu, we used `t-on-click=\"openUsers\"`, which called a generic window action instead of that settings URL.\n\n### The Fix:\nIn [`dashboard.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/xml/dashboard.xml#L47), simply change that link to use the exact same href:\n\n```xml\n<div class=\"crm-submenu-content\">\n    <a t-on-click=\"openRolesAndGroups\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Roles &amp; Permissions</a>\n    <a href=\"/app/settings/users\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\">Users</a>\n    <a t-on-click=\"openDepartments\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Departments</a>\n    <a t-on-click=\"openEmployeeTags\" class=\"crm-admin-menu-item crm-sub-item\" style=\"cursor:pointer;\">Employee Tags</a>\n</div>\n```\n\nThis keeps **Users** inside the **Organization** submenu, and when you click it, it opens `/app/settings/users` with **all tabs fully visible**!\n\nShall I update line 47 in [`dashboard.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/xml/dashboard.xml) for you?"}

{"step_index":3189,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:30:34Z","content":"The screenshot you shared shows **Odoo's default standard \"User / Administrator\" and Companies multi-company tags**, which are placed inside:\n`<page name=\"access_rights\">`!\n\nIn Odoo, `<page name=\"access_rights\">` is designed for Odoo's core technical application groups (Sales, Inventory, Invoicing, etc.).\n\nLook at lines 54–62 in [`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L54-L62):\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']/group[1]\" position=\"inside\">\n    <group>\n        <group string=\"Configuration &amp; Masters\">\n            ...\n        </group>\n        <group/>\n    </group>\n</xpath>\n```\nBecause it is injected **inside Odoo's core `access_rights` page group**, it squeezed Odoo's standard layout into narrow distorted columns!\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Solution:\nInstead of cramming custom CRM permissions into Odoo's standard `access_rights` tab:\n\nPut **Configuration & Masters** cleanly inside the **Organization & Hierarchy** tab (or give it its own clean tab **\"Custom Permissions\"**):\n\nIn [`views/res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml):\n\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//page[@name='org_hierarchy_page']\" position=\"inside\">\n    <group string=\"Custom Permissions\">\n        <group>\n            <field name=\"perm_service_ticket\" string=\"Service Ticket\"/>\n            <field name=\"perm_amc\" string=\"AMC Contract\"/>\n            <field name=\"perm_product\" string=\"Product Catalog\"/>\n            <field name=\"perm_company\" string=\"Company Creation\"/>\n            <field name=\"perm_export\" string=\"Excel Export\"/>\n        </group>\n        <group>\n            <label for=\"perm_customer_create\" string=\"Customer Creation\"/>\n            <div class=\"d-flex gap-3 align-items-center\">\n                <field name=\"perm_customer_create\"/> <span>Create</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_customer_write\"/> <span>Update</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_customer_read\"/> <span>View</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_customer_unlink\"/> <span>Delete</span>\n            </div>\n\n            <label for=\"perm_equipment_create\" string=\"Equipment Master\"/>\n            <div class=\"d-flex gap-3 align-items-center\">\n                <field name=\"perm_equipment_create\"/> <span>Create</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_equipment_write\"/> <span>Update</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_equipment_read\"/> <span>View</span>\n                <field name=\"perm_equipment_unlink\"/> <span>Delete</span>\n            </div>\n        </group>\n    </group>\n</xpath>\n```\n\n### Why this fixes the design:\n1. **Zero distortion**: Odoo's standard Access Rights tab remains 100% untouched and clean.\n2. **All CRM fields are together**: In the **Organization & Hierarchy** tab, the Manager sees Role, Department, Reports To, and all custom permissions directly below in a balanced, wide 2-column layout!\n\nShall I apply this clean layout for you now?"}

{"step_index":3234,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:38:34Z","content":"The issue is completely fixed! \n\n### What was causing the bad layout & default color:\n1. **Color**: Odoo by default uses its purple checkbox color (`#714B67`).\n2. **Spacing**: The checkboxes had default bootstrap margins without explicit inline-flex wrappers, causing text to wrap awkwardly right next to the box.\n\n### The Fix Applied:\n1. **Custom Color (`#0C3868`)**:\n   - Added custom CSS in [`crm_hide_new.css`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css#L316-L345) to style all checkboxes matching your exact corporate brand:\n     - Checked background & border: **`#0C3868` (Dark Blue)**.\n     - Accent color: **`#0C3868`**.\n     - Unchecked border: **`1.5px solid #555555`** with smooth `3px` border-radius.\n2. **Beautiful Spacing**:\n   - Wrapped each checkbox into `.perm-checkbox-group` and `.perm-checkbox-item`.\n   - Each option has clean `1.5rem` horizontal gap and perfect alignment between the checkbox and its label text (`Create`, `Update`, `View`, `Delete`).\n3. **Both Pages Updated**:\n   - **Roles & Permissions Master Form** (`hr.job`)\n   - **User Form** (`res.users`)\n\nRun `.\\sync.ps1` and upgrade `custom_crm_extended` to see the polished design!"}

{"step_index":3263,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:41:10Z","content":"The error was caused by Odoo's view XML validator: in Odoo form views, `<label>` tags must always have a `for=\"...\"` attribute. Using HTML-style `<label class=\"perm-checkbox-item\"><field .../> ...</label>` triggers `ParseError: Label tag must contain a \"for\"`.\n\n### What Was Fixed\nIn [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L63-L79):\n- Replaced `<label class=\"perm-checkbox-item\">` with `<span class=\"perm-checkbox-item\">` for both the **Single User** (`res.users`) and **Master Role** (`hr.job`) forms.\n- The CSS in [crm_hide_new.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css#L332-L346) applies directly to `.perm-checkbox-item` (with dark blue `#0C3868` accent, clean `1.5rem` spacing, and aligned checkboxes).\n- Pushed commit `a92580e` to GitHub.\n\n---\n\n### Run This on Your GCP Server\n\nRun the upgrade command in your GCP SSH terminal:\n\n```bash\ncd ~/odoo-custom && git pull\nsudo systemctl stop crm-test\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\nsudo systemctl start crm-test\n```"}

{"step_index":3289,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T07:45:23Z","content":"I have updated the CSS in [crm_hide_new.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css#L316-L355) with responsive/dynamic values:\n\n### What was changed:\n1. **Dynamic Units (`clamp()`, `rem`, `vw`, `vh`)**:\n   - `width` / `height` / `min-width`: `clamp(1rem, 1.2vw, 1.25rem)` (dynamically scales with viewport width).\n   - `border-radius`: `clamp(3px, 0.25rem, 4px)`.\n   - `accent-color` & `background-color`: uses `var(--crm-primary-color, #0C3868)`.\n   - `.perm-checkbox-group` gap: `clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.75rem)` for clean separation between options.\n   - `.perm-checkbox-item` gap: `clamp(0.35rem, 0.6vw, 0.5rem)` between checkbox and text.\n   - Font size: `clamp(0.82rem, 0.95vw, 0.95rem)` with `white-space: nowrap`.\n\n2. **Fixed Text Overlap Bug**:\n   - Odoo 17 wraps boolean fields in `.form-check` / `.o_field_boolean` with absolute positioning or negative margins (`margin-left: -1.5em; float: left;`), causing the checkbox to sit right on top of \"Create\", \"Update\", \"View\", \"Delete\".\n   - Added:\n     ```css\n     position: static !important;\n     float: none !important;\n     margin: 0 !important;\n     ```\n     and reset `.perm-checkbox-item .form-check` / `.o_field_boolean` to `display: inline-flex !important; margin: 0 !important; padding: 0 !important;`.\n\nThe changes have been pushed to GitHub (`f9d9744`).\n\nPlease pull and restart on your server:\n```bash\ncd ~/odoo-custom && git pull && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\n*(Hard-refresh your browser with `Ctrl + F5` to reload the updated stylesheet).*"}

{"step_index":3314,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:40:57Z","content":"Here is the exact problem and logic breakdown from [crm_lead_wizard.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/crm_lead_wizard.py):\n\n---\n\n### Why it fetches the wrong Mobile & Email (or doesn't update):\n\n#### 1. In `_onchange_contact_picker_id` (Lines 187–196):\n```python\n@api.onchange('contact_picker_id')\ndef _onchange_contact_picker_id(self):\n    if self.contact_picker_id:\n        child = self.contact_picker_id\n        self.contact_name = child.name or \"\"\n        self.function = child.function or \"\"\n        if not self.email_from:\n            self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n        if not self.phone:\n            self.phone = child.phone or \"\"\n```\n\nLook closely at these **3 major flaws**:\n\n1. **`if not self.email_from:` and `if not self.phone:` guard conditions**:\n   - If an email or phone was already typed or set previously, and the user changes the contact dropdown to another person, **it does NOT overwrite them!** It keeps the old/wrong contact's email and phone!\n2. **Mobile (`x_mobile`) is completely missing**:\n   - The wizard has both `phone` and `x_mobile` fields. In `_onchange_contact_picker_id`, it **never touches `x_mobile`**! It only fetches `child.phone`. If the contact has their mobile number in `child.mobile`, it is completely ignored.\n3. **Contact vs Company Phone/Mobile fallback**:\n   - In Odoo `res.partner`, a person's mobile is stored in `mobile` and landline in `phone`. If a contact has their number in `child.mobile`, but not `child.phone`, `child.phone` is blank.\n\n---\n\n#### 2. In `_onchange_partner_company_id` (Lines 166–175):\n```python\nif len(children) == 1:\n    child = children[0]\n    self.contact_name = child.name or \"\"\n    self.function = child.function or \"\"\n    if not self.email_from:\n        self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n    if not self.phone:\n        self.phone = child.phone or \"\"\n```\n- Again, `x_mobile` is completely ignored (`self.x_mobile` is never populated).\n- If `email_from` or `phone` has any cached value, it is not updated to the new company's contact.\n- It doesn't check `child.mobile`.\n\n---\n\n#### 3. In `_onchange_partner_id` (Lines 210–222):\n```python\n@api.onchange(\"partner_id\")\ndef _onchange_partner_id(self):\n    if self.partner_id:\n        p = self.partner_id\n        ...\n        self.email_from = p.email or \"\"\n        self.phone = p.phone or \"\"\n```\n- Here too, `self.x_mobile` is never set from `p.mobile`.\n\n---\n\n### Summary of the Bug:\n1. **Old values are never cleared/updated** when selecting a different contact because of `if not self.email_from` and `if not self.phone`.\n2. **`x_mobile` (Mobile) is never fetched at all** from the selected partner/contact record (`child.mobile`).\n3. **No fallback between `mobile` and `phone`**: If the contact has their number stored in Odoo's `mobile` field, the wizard looks only at `child.phone`, leaving phone empty or keeping stale data."}

{"step_index":3322,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:43:01Z","content":"**Yes, definitely change it!** \n\nHere is why and what to change:\n\n### Why change it?\n1. In Step 1, when the user selects an **Existing Customer** (`partner_id`), it currently only sets `self.phone = p.phone or \"\"` and completely leaves `self.x_mobile` empty. \n2. In India / CRM usage, 90% of contact numbers are entered in `p.mobile`, not `p.phone`. When `x_mobile` is not fetched:\n   - Step 2 shows the Mobile box empty.\n   - If `p.phone` was blank, the user gets hit with validation errors or has to type it again manually.\n3. Also, if the contact has only `mobile` and no landline `phone`, `self.phone` can fallback to `p.mobile` so it's never empty.\n\n---\n\n### What to change in `_onchange_partner_id`:\n\n**Before:**\n```python\n    @api.onchange(\"partner_id\")\n    def _onchange_partner_id(self):\n        if self.partner_id:\n            p = self.partner_id\n            self.partner_name = p.parent_id.name if p.parent_id else p.name\n            self.contact_name = p.name if p.parent_id else \"\"\n            self.function = p.function or \"\"\n            self.email_from = p.email or \"\"\n            self.phone = p.phone or \"\"\n            self.city = p.city or \"\"\n            self.state_id = p.state_id\n            self.zip = p.zip or \"\"\n```\n\n**Recommended Update:**\n```python\n    @api.onchange(\"partner_id\")\n    def _onchange_partner_id(self):\n        if self.partner_id:\n            p = self.partner_id\n            self.partner_name = p.parent_id.name if p.parent_id else p.name\n            self.contact_name = p.name if p.parent_id else \"\"\n            self.function = p.function or \"\"\n            self.email_from = p.email or \"\"\n            self.phone = p.phone or \"\"\n            self.x_mobile = p.mobile or \"\"\n            # If phone is empty, fallback to mobile so contact info is immediately available\n            if not self.phone and p.mobile:\n                self.phone = p.mobile\n            self.city = p.city or \"\"\n            self.state_id = p.state_id\n            self.zip = p.zip or \"\"\n```\n\nAnd in **`_onchange_contact_picker_id`** (when selecting contact from dropdown in Step 2):\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contact_picker_id')\n    def _onchange_contact_picker_id(self):\n        if self.contact_picker_id:\n            child = self.contact_picker_id\n            self.contact_name = child.name or \"\"\n            self.function = child.function or \"\"\n            self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n            self.phone = child.phone or \"\"\n            self.x_mobile = child.mobile or \"\"\n            if not self.phone and child.mobile:\n                self.phone = child.mobile\n```\n*(Notice we remove `if not self.email_from` so picking a new contact actually updates email and phone instead of keeping old data).*"}

{"step_index":3328,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:44:27Z","content":"Let's look at the **entire logic** of `_onchange_contact_picker_id` line by line:\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contact_picker_id')\n    def _onchange_contact_picker_id(self):\n        if self.contact_picker_id:\n            child = self.contact_picker_id\n            self.contact_name = child.name or \"\"\n            self.function = child.function or \"\"\n            if not self.email_from:\n                self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n            if not self.phone:\n                self.phone = child.phone or \"\"\n            # Check if newly created by unauthorized user\n            allowed_ids = [2, 10, 11]  # Admin, Dhruvil, Himanshu\n            if self.env.uid not in allowed_ids:\n                # Check if this is a new record (just created)\n                # Check if the record is completely new and unsaved\n                if not self.partner_company_id.id:\n                    self.partner_company_id = False\n                    self.partner_name = False\n                    return {'warning': {\n                        'title': 'Not Allowed',\n                        'message': 'You are not allowed to create new companies. Please select an existing one.'\n                    }}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Critical Problems in this Logic:\n\n1. **Why it fails to fetch right Mobile / Phone:**\n   - **`x_mobile` is never set!** `self.x_mobile` is completely ignored here. So the mobile number of the contact (`child.mobile`) is never brought into the form.\n   - **`if not self.phone:`**: Suppose Company A has Contact 1 (Phone: `9876543210`) and Contact 2 (Phone: `9123456789`). If the user initially clicked Contact 1, `self.phone` became `9876543210`. If the user now switches the dropdown to Contact 2, `if not self.phone:` sees that `self.phone` already has a value, **so it does NOTHING!** It keeps Contact 1's phone! That is why users complain: *\"it fetches the wrong number and does not update when selecting from dropdown\"*.\n\n2. **Why it fails to fetch right Email:**\n   - **`if not self.email_from:`**: Same exact issue! Once an email is filled (from Company or Contact 1), selecting Contact 2 will **never** update `self.email_from` because `not self.email_from` is False.\n\n3. **What happens if user clears the contact dropdown (`if not self.contact_picker_id`):**\n   - If user clears `contact_picker_id`, it does nothing (leaves all fields as they were).\n\n4. **Strange permission check on `partner_company_id` inside `contact_picker_id` onchange (Lines 195–206):**\n   - The check does:\n     ```python\n     if not self.partner_company_id.id:\n     ```\n     `self.partner_company_id` was already picked in Step 1. In Step 2, `contact_picker_id` is filtered by `domain=\"[('parent_id', '=', partner_company_id), ('is_company', '=', False)]\"`, and the XML specifically has `options=\"{'no_create': True, 'no_open': True}\"`. So users cannot create contacts from here anyway.\n\n---\n\n### The Correct Logic for `_onchange_contact_picker_id`:\n\nWhen a user explicitly chooses a Contact from the dropdown:\n1. **Always update** `contact_name`, `function`, `email_from`.\n2. **Set `x_mobile`** from `child.mobile or child.phone or \"\"`.\n3. **Set `phone`** from `child.phone or child.mobile or \"\"`.\n4. If `contact_picker_id` is cleared, clear the contact-specific fields so stale data isn't left behind.\n\n```python\n    @api.onchange('contact_picker_id')\n    def _onchange_contact_picker_id(self):\n        if self.contact_picker_id:\n            child = self.contact_picker_id\n            self.contact_name = child.name or \"\"\n            self.function = child.function or \"\"\n            # Always update email with the selected contact's email\n            self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n            # Fetch both phone and mobile correctly\n            self.phone = child.phone or child.mobile or \"\"\n            self.x_mobile = child.mobile or child.phone or \"\"\n        else:\n            # If contact unselected, clear contact details\n            self.contact_name = False\n            self.function = False\n            self.email_from = False\n            self.phone = False\n            self.x_mobile = False\n```\n\nDo you want me to apply this update to `crm_lead_wizard.py`?"}

{"step_index":3333,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:45:46Z","content":"Here is the exact reason why `if not self.email_from` was causing the bug:\n\n### Example of what happens in real usage:\n\n1. A company has two contacts:\n   - **Person A**: `rahul@gmail.com`\n   - **Person B**: `amit@gmail.com`\n2. The user opens Step 2, and either by default or by clicking the dropdown, **Person A** is selected.\n   - `self.email_from` becomes `\"rahul@gmail.com\"`.\n3. Now the user realizes: *\"Wait, I need to create the lead for Amit, not Rahul.\"*\n4. The user opens the dropdown and selects **Person B (Amit)**.\n5. Because of `if not self.email_from:`:\n   ```python\n   if not self.email_from:\n       self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\n   ```\n   - `self.email_from` **is already `\"rahul@gmail.com\"`**, so `not self.email_from` evaluates to **`False`**!\n   - Python **skips** setting the email!\n   - **Result**: The dropdown shows **Person B (Amit)**, but the email field **still shows Person A's email (`rahul@gmail.com`)**!\n\nThat's why the user complained:\n> *\"in lead wizard contact select from drop down do not fetch right mobile number and email id it fetch another\"*\n\nWhen a user explicitly selects a contact from the dropdown (`contact_picker_id`), they expect the wizard to load **that selected person's email and phone**, not keep the old person's data."}

{"step_index":3371,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:53:07Z","content":"### Why the error happened:\nIn standard Odoo `base.res_partner`, the field for contact numbers is `phone` (the `mobile` field is provided by optional addons like `sms` or `partner_autocomplete` and does not exist in standard base `res.partner`). Directly doing `child.mobile` or `p.mobile` raised:\n```python\nAttributeError: 'res.partner' object has no attribute 'mobile'\n```\n\n### Fix Applied:\nIn [crm_lead_wizard.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/crm_lead_wizard.py#L170-L225):\n- Used safe `getattr()` inspection:\n  ```python\n  child_phone = getattr(child, 'phone', '') or \"\"\n  child_mobile = getattr(child, 'mobile', '') or \"\"\n  self.phone = child_phone or child_mobile\n  self.x_mobile = child_mobile or child_phone\n  ```\n- Done for:\n  1. `_onchange_contact_picker_id`\n  2. `_onchange_partner_company_id` (single child contact)\n  3. `_onchange_partner_id` (existing customer)\n\nThis ensures:\n1. No `AttributeError` crash whether `mobile` exists on the model or not.\n2. Both `phone` and `x_mobile` are correctly populated.\n3. Whenever the user switches the contact in the dropdown, the contact's actual email and phone/mobile are immediately updated.\n\nThe fix has been pushed to GitHub (`1544adf`).\n\nPlease pull and restart on the server:\n```bash\ncd ~/odoo-custom && git pull && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```"}
{"step_index":3373,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:56:16Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\ntell me what was the problme\n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-22T14:26:16+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\wizard\\crm_lead_wizard.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\nCursor is on line: 1\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\wizard\\crm_lead_wizard.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\static\\src\\css\\crm_hide_new.css (LANGUAGE_CSS)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\views\\res_users_signature_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\res_users.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\crm_whitelabel\\static\\src\\xml\\dashboard.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":3374,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T08:56:17Z","content":"Here is the exact explanation of what went wrong and why it crashed:\n\n---\n\n### Problem 1: Why it was fetching the wrong contact info previously\nIn the original code for `_onchange_contact_picker_id`:\n```python\nif not self.email_from:\n    self.email_from = child.email or \"\"\nif not self.phone:\n    self.phone = child.phone or \"\"\n```\n* **What happened:** When the user selected Contact A, `email_from` and `phone` were set. When the user changed the dropdown to Contact B, `not self.email_from` evaluated to `False` (because it already had Contact A's email). Odoo completely skipped updating the fields, leaving Contact A's details in the form.\n\n---\n\n### Problem 2: Why the server threw `AttributeError: 'res.partner' object has no attribute 'mobile'`\nWhen you added:\n```python\nself.x_mobile = child.mobile or \"\"\n```\n* **What happened:** In standard base Odoo, the `res.partner` table **only has `phone` by default**. The `mobile` field only exists if the `sms` or `phone_validation` modules are installed. \n* Because `mobile` does not exist on `res.partner` in this database, Python directly crashed with:\n  ```\n  AttributeError: 'res.partner' object has no attribute 'mobile'\n  ```\n\n---\n\n### How it was fixed:\nInstead of directly accessing `child.mobile`, we use Python's safe attribute lookup `getattr()`:\n```python\nchild_phone = getattr(child, 'phone', '') or \"\"\nchild_mobile = getattr(child, 'mobile', '') or \"\"\n\nself.phone = child_phone or child_mobile\nself.x_mobile = child_mobile or child_phone\n```\n\n1. **Safe from crashing:** If `mobile` doesn't exist on the partner model, `getattr(child, 'mobile', '')` safely returns `\"\"` instead of crashing.\n2. **Right contact fetched every time:** Removed the `if not self...` blocking conditions so selecting any contact immediately replaces the inputs with that contact's info.\n3. **No empty numbers:** If the number was entered in `phone`, both `phone` and `x_mobile` receive it, preventing empty values and validation errors."}

{"step_index":3467,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T09:40:38Z","content":"The top one under **\"MASTER DATA\"** that says:\n```\nContact Creation    Creation\n```\nis Odoo's standard group selection field for `base.group_partner_manager` (which Odoo automatically generates and displays under Application / Master Data on the User form).\n\nBecause you now have the explicit **Customer Creation checkboxes** (`Create`, `Update`, `View`, `Delete`), having that top dropdown creates duplicate confusion!\n\n### How to Hide It Cleanly Without Disturbing the Flow:\n\nIn [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml), we can simply add an xpath or CSS rule:\n\n#### Option 1: XML xpath in `res.users` form (Recommended & cleanest)\nOdoo's standard access rights fields are named `sel_groups_...` based on category. We can hide the field or xpath the category group:\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='sel_groups_...']\" position=\"attributes\">\n    <attribute name=\"invisible\">1</attribute>\n</xpath>\n```\n\n#### Option 2: CSS (Zero risk, 100% safe, never breaks any database record or Python flow)\nIn `crm_hide_new.css`, we simply hide the row in the User Form's Access Rights tab:\n```css\n/* Hide redundant Contact Creation group dropdown on res.users form */\n.o_form_sheet [name=\"access_rights\"] tr:has(label[for*=\"partner_manager\"]),\n.o_form_sheet [name=\"access_rights\"] div:has(> label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n.o_form_sheet [name=\"access_rights\"] .o_wrap_field:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")) {\n    display: none !important;\n}\n```\n\nAnd in Python ([res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L129-L136)), your backend logic already takes care of the permissions:\n```python\nif job.perm_customer_create:\n    # Grants base.group_partner_manager automatically in the background\n    ...\n```\nSo hiding it visually will **not** disturb any security, data, or user creation flow!\n\nWould you like me to hide that top \"Contact Creation\" field using the CSS rule so it cleanly disappears from the view?"}

{"step_index":3472,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T09:41:51Z","content":"In [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml), place it right after line 54, where `<xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']\" position=\"inside\">` starts!\n\nIn Odoo, the `base.view_users_form` generates the dynamic user access fields inside groups. But because that field is dynamically injected by Odoo's category mechanism into `base.view_users_form`, targeting its generated name with xpath can easily cause an XML `View error: Element '<xpath ...>' cannot be located` during server module upgrades.\n\nThe **safest, cleanest, and 100% reliable** place is in [crm_hide_new.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css):\n\n```css\n/* Hide redundant Contact Creation row from Master Data on User form */\n.o_form_sheet div[name=\"access_rights\"] tr:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n.o_form_sheet div[name=\"access_rights\"] div:has(> label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")) {\n    display: none !important;\n}\n```\n\nOr if you prefer **XML**, you place it inside the `<record id=\"view_users_form_signature_card\">` in [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L54):\n\n```xml\n            <xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']\" position=\"inside\">\n                <!-- Hide the redundant Contact Creation dropdown via inline style -->\n                <style>\n                    [name=\"access_rights\"] tr:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n                    [name=\"access_rights\"] div.o_wrap_field:has(> label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n                    [name=\"access_rights\"] .o_cell:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")) {\n                        display: none !important;\n                    }\n                </style>\n```\n\nThis way:\n1. It is placed right inside the `access_rights` page in your XML file.\n2. It immediately hides the top \"Contact Creation\" dropdown.\n3. Your new \"Customer Creation\" checkboxes below remain visible and active!"}

{"step_index":3477,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T09:42:45Z","content":"To find the exact name for `sel_groups_...`, right-click that \"Contact Creation\" field in your browser and click **Inspect**. Look at the `name` attribute of the input/dropdown (it looks like `sel_groups_1_2` or `sel_groups_24`).\n\nOnce you have the name, you place the xpath in [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L54) right before `<xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']\" position=\"inside\">`:\n\n```xml\n            <!-- 1. Hide the standard Contact Creation dropdown -->\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[@name='sel_groups_...']\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"invisible\">1</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n\n            <!-- 2. Your custom Configuration & Masters group -->\n            <xpath expr=\"//page[@name='access_rights']\" position=\"inside\">\n                <group string=\"Configuration &amp; Masters\">\n...\n```\n\n---\n\n### If you don't want to look up the dynamic group ID:\nIn Odoo 17, `sel_groups_` field names contain database IDs that change between databases (e.g., test vs production).\n\nYou can instead xpath by field attribute or label:\n```xml\n            <xpath expr=\"//field[contains(@name, 'sel_groups_') and @string='Contact Creation']\" position=\"attributes\">\n                <attribute name=\"invisible\">1</attribute>\n            </xpath>\n```\nOr use the CSS rule:\n```css\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_wrap_field:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")) {\n    display: none !important;\n}\n```"}

{"step_index":3492,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T09:46:53Z","content":"The crash happened because `sel_groups_...` is a placeholder name (the dots `...` were literally kept in the XML, which Odoo could not find). Also, in Odoo 17, `base.view_users_form` dynamically creates those fields per database, making hardcoded xpath fragile.\n\n### What was done:\n1. Removed the invalid `<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='sel_groups_...']\">` from [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml) so the module compiles cleanly without any errors.\n2. Added the clean CSS rule to [crm_hide_new.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css#L457-L463) to target and hide the redundant \"Contact Creation\" row from the Access Rights tab:\n   ```css\n   .o_form_sheet div[name=\"access_rights\"] tr:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n   .o_form_sheet div[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_wrap_field:has(> label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")),\n   .o_form_sheet div[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_cell:has(label:contains(\"Contact Creation\")) {\n       display: none !important;\n   }\n   ```\n3. Let's inspect that field on your page.\n\n### 2-Second Step to find the exact ID:\n1. In your browser on that User page, **Right-click** on the text **\"Contact Creation\"** (the one under MASTER DATA) and click **Inspect**.\n2. Look at the `<label for=\"...\">` or `<div name=\"...\">`.\n3. What is the `for=\"...\"` or `name=\"...\"` attribute? \n\nFor example, does it say:\n`for=\"sel_groups_1_2_...\"` or `name=\"sel_groups_...\"`?\n\nPlease paste that one line from Inspect element here, and we will write the exact rule or clean xpath to hide it completely!"}

I will **not** run `sync.ps1` automatically anymore—you will run it manually whenever you want.\n\n### Why only the value had hidden earlier:\nIn Odoo's two-column grid (`.o_inner_group`), the **label** is in one cell (`.o_cell.o_wrap_label`), and the **dropdown** is in the next cell (`.o_cell.o_wrap_input`). The previous rule only caught the input cell, which caused the label \"Contact Creation\" to remain and pull the next field (\"Excel Export\") onto the same row.\n\n### What is updated in [crm_hide_new.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/css/crm_hide_new.css#L459-L468):\n```css\n/* Hide duplicate standard Contact Creation field and label on res.users Access Rights tab */\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_cell:has(#field_2_0),\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_cell:has(label[for=\"field_2_0\"]),\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_cell:has([data-id=\"6\"]),\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_inner_group > .o_cell.o_wrap_label:has(label[for=\"field_2_0\"]),\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_inner_group > .o_cell.o_wrap_input:has(#field_2_0),\ndiv[name=\"access_rights\"] .o_inner_group > .o_cell.o_wrap_input:has([data-id=\"6\"]) {\n    display: none !important;\n}\n```\nNow **both** the label cell (`.o_wrap_label`) and the input cell (`.o_wrap_input`) are targeted, so the entire row disappears cleanly and the fields below align properly.\n\nYou can now run `.\\sync.ps1` whenever you are ready!"}

{"step_index":3597,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:09:20Z","content":"In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L76-L141), direct SQL was previously used because of how Odoo handles the `res.groups` relation:\n\n### 1. The Odoo ORM Recursion Problem\nWhen using the standard ORM `user.write({'groups_id': [(4, group_id)]})`, Odoo triggers:\n1. `res.users.write()`\n2. Re-computes all user security groups and implied groups.\n3. Clears and reloads the ACL cache across all worker threads.\n4. Calls `_apply_job_permissions` again (since `crm_job_id` is on `res.users`), which can create an **infinite recursion loop** or trigger `AccessDenied / Cannot modify groups of user`.\n\n### 2. Accidental Super-Admin Downgrades\nWhen doing standard ORM:\n```python\nuser.write({'groups_id': [(6, 0, [g1, g2])]})\n```\nOdoo replaces **all** groups of the user. If an Admin or Super User (`base.group_system`) has their role saved, the ORM wiped out their System Administrator rights! Direct SQL insertion into `res_groups_users_rel` with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` was originally put there to safely toggle only specific group IDs without wiping other groups.\n\n---\n\n### Can We Replace Direct SQL With Clean ORM Commands?\n**Yes!** We can replace all raw SQL with standard Odoo ORM commands using the `(4, id)` (link) and `(3, id)` (unlink) commands via `sudo()` with context `{'tracking_disable': True}`:\n\n```python\n# Instead of SQL INSERT:\nuser.sudo().write({'groups_id': [(4, g_export.id)]})\n\n# Instead of SQL DELETE:\nuser.sudo().write({'groups_id': [(3, g_export.id)]})\n```\n\nUsing `(4, id)` and `(3, id)` in the ORM:\n- Is 100% standard Odoo Python code.\n- Only adds or removes the exact group without touching other groups (so it never downgrades Admin).\n- Avoids raw SQL queries completely.\n\nWould you like me to refactor those SQL queries in `res_users.py` to clean ORM commands?"}

{"step_index":3599,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:11:16Z","content":"In Odoo, **`3`** and **`4`** are special **ORM commands** used to update Many2many relationships (like `groups_id` on users).\n\nInstead of writing SQL `INSERT` or `DELETE`, Odoo provides these command codes:\n\n| Code | Meaning | What It Does in Background | Example |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| **`(4, ID)`** | **Link (Add)** | Adds this record to the relation if not already added. Does **not** remove any existing records. | `user.write({'groups_id': [(4, group.id)]})`<br>*(Equivalent to: Give this group to user)* |\n| **`(3, ID)`** | **Unlink (Remove)** | Removes this specific record from the relation. Does **not** delete the group record from the database. | `user.write({'groups_id': [(3, group.id)]})`<br>*(Equivalent to: Remove this group from user)* |\n| **`(5, 0, 0)`** | **Clear All** | Removes all links from the relation. | |\n| **`(6, 0, [IDs])`** | **Replace All** | Wipes everything and sets only the specified list of IDs. | |\n\n---\n\n### Why `(4, ID)` and `(3, ID)` are useful:\nIf a user is already an Administrator, and you only want to grant them the **Export** group:\n- `[(4, export_group.id)]` **adds** Export without touching their Admin group.\n- `[(3, export_group.id)]` **removes** Export without touching any of their other groups.\n\nThis is the standard Odoo ORM way to manage many-to-many security groups safely."}

{"step_index":3601,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:11:43Z","content":"**Yes, it is much safer than raw SQL queries** for several reasons:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Cache Invalidation (The biggest danger with SQL)\n* **With Raw SQL (`self.env.cr.execute`)**: \n  - PostgreSQL table changes directly, but **Odoo's memory cache does NOT know**!\n  - The user's active session might still think they have the old permissions until the server is restarted or `clear_cache()` is called.\n* **With ORM `[(4, id)]` and `[(3, id)]`**:\n  - Odoo **automatically flushes its internal security cache**, invalidates user permissions immediately, and logs the change properly.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Multi-Company & Implied Groups\n* In Odoo, security groups often have **Implied Groups** (e.g., if you give *Sales / All Documents*, Odoo automatically gives *Sales / Own Documents* and *Internal User*).\n* **With SQL**: You only insert 1 row. Any parent or implied permissions are broken or missing.\n* **With ORM**: Odoo automatically resolves and assigns all necessary implied groups cleanly.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Database Portability & Upgrades\n* Odoo official guidelines advise against raw `INSERT / DELETE` on `res_groups_users_rel` because during Odoo version migrations (or multi-threaded database transactions), raw SQL queries bypass Odoo's registry locks and can cause deadlocks or silent desyncs.\n\n---\n\n### How to use `(4, id)` and `(3, id)` without the infinite loop:\nAll we need to do is pass a simple context flag (e.g. `with_context(skip_sync=True)`) so `write()` doesn't call itself in a loop:\n\n```python\nuser.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write({\n    'groups_id': [(4, group.id)]   # to add\n})\n```\n```python\nuser.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write({\n    'groups_id': [(3, group.id)]   # to remove\n})\n```\n\nIt is 100% pure standard Odoo Python, safe, and avoids raw SQL completely!"}

{"step_index":3603,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:12:16Z","content":"Here are the **two specific problems** that can happen in Odoo if not written carefully:\n\n---\n\n### Problem 1: The \"Infinite Loop\" (Recursion)\nIn [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L172-L179), you have:\n```python\ndef write(self, vals):\n    res = super().write(vals)\n    if 'crm_job_id' in vals:\n        self._apply_job_permissions(...)\n```\n* If `_apply_job_permissions` does:\n  ```python\n  user.write({'groups_id': [(4, group_id)]})\n  ```\n* That `user.write(...)` calls `write()` again!\n* Then `write()` calls `_apply_job_permissions` again... and it loops forever until Python crashes with `RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded`.\n\n#### How we prevent this:\nWe add `with_context(skip_sync=True)` when updating groups:\n```python\nuser.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write({'groups_id': [(4, group_id)]})\n```\nAnd check `if self.env.context.get('skip_sync'): return` inside `write()`. This stops any loop immediately.\n\n---\n\n### Problem 2: Accidentally Downgrading the Admin / System User\nIn Odoo, the Super Administrator (`admin` / `base.group_system`) has special master access.\n* If code uses `[(6, 0, [group_ids])]` (which means *\"delete everything and replace with this list\"*), and you didn't include the Administrator group in that list, **the Admin user gets stripped of their admin rights and gets locked out of Settings**!\n\n#### How we prevent this:\n1. **Never use `(6, 0, ...)`**.\n2. Only use **`(4, id)`** (add specific group) and **`(3, id)`** (remove specific group).\n3. Add a safety check:\n   ```python\n   # Never remove Admin/System rights from a system administrator\n   if user.has_group('base.group_system') and group == admin_group:\n       continue\n   ```\n\n---\n\n### Summary:\nUsing **`(4, id)`** and **`(3, id)`** with `with_context(skip_sync=True)` completely eliminates raw SQL queries, avoids the infinite loop, and keeps all admin rights 100% safe."}

{"step_index":3624,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:14:43Z","content":"Right now, the permissions:\n- `perm_customer_unlink` (Delete Customer/Contact)\n- `perm_product_unlink` (Delete Product)\n- `perm_equipment_unlink` (Delete Equipment)\n\nare saved on the User and Role models, but **the backend `unlink()` methods have not enforced them yet**! That means anyone with standard Odoo rights could still potentially delete records even if the checkbox is unchecked.\n\n---\n\n### How to Enforce Delete Permissions:\n\nWe can add clean, standard security checks directly in the `unlink()` methods of the respective models:\n\n#### 1. Customers & Contacts (`res.partner`):\nIn [res_partner.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_partner.py):\n```python\n    def unlink(self):\n        # Allow Super Admin\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_customer_unlink:\n                raise exceptions.UserError(\"You do not have permission to delete Customer / Contact records.\")\n        return super().unlink()\n```\n\n#### 2. Products (`product.template`):\n```python\n    def unlink(self):\n        # Allow Super Admin\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_product_unlink:\n                raise exceptions.UserError(\"You do not have permission to delete Products from the Catalog.\")\n        return super().unlink()\n```\n\n#### 3. Equipment Master (`equipment.master`):\nIn [equipment_master.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/equipment_master.py):\n```python\n    def unlink(self):\n        # Allow Super Admin\n        if not self.env.user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not self.env.user.perm_equipment_unlink:\n                raise exceptions.UserError(\"You do not have permission to delete Equipment Master records.\")\n        return super().unlink()\n```\n\n### What this achieves:\n1. If **Delete** checkbox is **unchecked** (`False`):\n   - The user cannot delete records (even if they try from Action -> Delete, Odoo shows the user error).\n2. If **Delete** checkbox is **checked** (`True`):\n   - The user is permitted to delete.\n3. System Administrators (`base.group_system`) are always allowed.\n\nWould you like me to implement these `unlink()` security checks so the Delete checkboxes are actively enforced?"}

{"step_index":3645,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:16:18Z","content":"I have implemented the delete permissions enforcement across all three models:\n\n### 1. [res_partner.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_partner.py#L12-L19) (Customer / Contact Delete Check)\n```python\ndef unlink(self):\n    for rec in self:\n        user = self.env.user\n        if not user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not getattr(user, 'perm_customer_unlink', False):\n                raise exceptions.UserError(_(\"Access Denied: You do not have permission to delete Customer / Contact records.\"))\n    return super(ResPartner, self).unlink()\n```\n\n### 2. [product_template.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/product_template.py#L9-L16) (Product Catalog Delete Check)\n```python\ndef unlink(self):\n    for rec in self:\n        user = self.env.user\n        if not user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not getattr(user, 'perm_product_unlink', False):\n                raise exceptions.UserError(_(\"Access Denied: You do not have permission to delete Product Catalog records.\"))\n    return super(ProductTemplate, self).unlink()\n```\n\n### 3. [equipment_master.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/equipment_master.py#L192-L199) (Equipment Master Delete Check)\n```python\ndef unlink(self):\n    for rec in self:\n        user = self.env.user\n        if not user.has_group('base.group_system'):\n            if not getattr(user, 'perm_equipment_unlink', False):\n                raise exceptions.UserError(_(\"Access Denied: You do not have permission to delete Equipment Master records.\"))\n    return super(EquipmentMaster, self).unlink()\n```\n\n---\n\n### How It Works:\n- **If the \"Delete\" checkbox is UNCHECKED**: Users will be blocked with a clear access denied message when attempting to delete customers, products, or equipment.\n- **If the \"Delete\" checkbox is CHECKED**: Users can delete normally.\n- **Super Administrators (`base.group_system`)**: Always have delete permission bypass so they never get locked out.\n\nI did not run `sync.ps1`. You can run your sync script whenever you want!"}

{"step_index":3729,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:23:34Z","content":"Both issues have been resolved:\n\n### 1. Missing Field: **Lead & Quotation**\n- **Cause**: In [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L56), the left column under **Configuration & Masters** only listed `perm_service_ticket`, `perm_amc`, `perm_company`, and `perm_export`, leaving out `perm_lead_quote`.\n- **Fix**: Added `<field name=\"perm_lead_quote\" string=\"Lead &amp; Quotation\"/>` as the first item in the left column so it matches the permissions layout on Role / Job Position (`hr.job`).\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why **MASTER DATA** was not removed\n- **Cause**: Odoo 17 generates group titles as `.o_horizontal_separator` elements without unique static IDs, so CSS selectors relying on specific input IDs didn't hide the entire column title and remaining fields.\n- **Fix**: Updated [user_access_labels.js](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/js/user_access_labels.js#L37-L50) to dynamically identify the `\"MASTER DATA\"` section separator and its enclosing container column, setting `display: none !important`. This completely removes the redundant top **MASTER DATA** block.\n\n---\n\n### To apply these changes:\n\n1. In PowerShell:\n   ```powershell\n   .\\sync.ps1\n   ```\n\n2. On the GCP VM:\n   ```bash\n   cd ~/odoo-custom && git pull\n   sudo systemctl stop crm-test\n   /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm-test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended --stop-after-init\n   sudo systemctl start crm-test\n   ```\n\n3. Perform a hard refresh in your browser (**Ctrl + Shift + R**)."}

{"step_index":3732,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:26:09Z","content":"Here is the exact explanation of how both fields work and which one actually controls permissions:\n\n---\n\n### **1. Top One: Standard Odoo \"Sales\" Field (Relabeled to \"Lead & Quotation\")**\n* **What it is:** This is Odoo's native security group field (`sel_groups_...`) for the **Sales** module (`sales_team.group_sale_salesman` vs `sales_team.group_sale_manager`).\n* **Does it work?** **YES.** This is the field that Odoo's built-in record rules and menus natively read to determine if the user can see only their own leads/quotations or all leads/quotations.\n\n---\n\n### **2. Bottom One: Custom `perm_lead_quote` Field**\n* **What it is:** This is the custom selection field created on `res.users` (identical to the one on Job Position / Role `hr.job`).\n* **How it was designed:** \n  - On **Job Position (`hr.job`)**, selecting this sets the default for the role.\n  - When a user is assigned that Job Position, Python code in `_apply_job_permissions` reads this value and automatically updates Odoo's security groups.\n* **Why it's duplicated here:** It was placed inside `res.users` form under \"Configuration & Masters\". However, changing this field directly on a user record does **not** automatically trigger the record rules unless a sync method runs, whereas the **top standard field** applies immediately.\n\n---\n\n### **Summary & Next Step Option**\n* **Which one is the real working one right now?**\n  👉 The **TOP one** directly assigns the active Odoo groups (`sales_team.group_sale_salesman`, etc.).\n* **Recommendation:**\n  Since the top one already does the actual job and is placed directly under the header **\"LEAD & QUOTATION\"**, we should simply **remove the bottom duplicate (`perm_lead_quote`) from the `res.users` XML view** so you don't have two identical dropdowns on the same screen.\n\nWould you like to remove the duplicate bottom one from the view?"}

{"step_index":3785,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:34:57Z","content":"To implement the hierarchy according to user requirements, we need to understand how your business hierarchy works and how data visibility (record rules) should flow.\n\nCurrently, we already have these fields in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L7-L13):\n- **Reports To (Manager)** (`crm_manager_id`)\n- **Direct Reports / Subordinates** (`crm_subordinate_ids`)\n- **Job Position / Role** (`crm_job_id`)\n- **Department** (`crm_department_id`)\n\n---\n\n### Key Questions to Define the Hierarchy:\n\n1. **What records should the hierarchy control?**\n   - **Leads & Opportunities** (`crm.lead`)\n   - **Quotations / Sales Orders** (`sale.order`)\n   - **Service Tickets** (`service.ticket`)\n   - **AMC Contracts** (`amc.contract`)\n   *(or all of the above?)*\n\n2. **How should visibility work between Manager and Subordinates?**\n   - **Top-Down Visibility:** A Manager can see **their own records PLUS all records of their direct reports and subordinates** down the tree.\n   - **Subordinate Restriction:** A team member can **only** see their own records (cannot see peer or manager records).\n   - **Department / Branch Head:** Can see all records within their assigned Department.\n\n3. **Approvals / Workflow:**\n   - Does a quotation or discount above a certain percentage require the **Reports To (Manager)**'s approval before it can be sent or confirmed?\n   - Should lead assignments automatically route through the manager to subordinates?\n\n4. **UI / Visualization:**\n   - Do you want an **Organization Chart / Hierarchy Tree View** (showing who reports to whom)?\n   - Or a filter on Lead/Order views like `\"My Team's Leads\"` / `\"My Subordinates\"`?\n\nPlease share how you envision the hierarchy working, and I will tailor the record rules, views, and logic accordingly."}

{"step_index":3791,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:36:09Z","content":"In Odoo, each **Job Position (`hr.job`)** already has a built-in field: `department_id`!\n\nConnecting **Department** and **Job Position** creates a seamless two-way workflow:\n\n---\n\n### How they connect:\n\n1. **When you pick a Department first:**\n   - The **Job Position** dropdown filters to show **only positions belonging to that Department** (e.g., selecting *Sales Department* shows only *Sales Executive*, *Sales Manager*, etc.).\n\n2. **When you pick a Job Position first:**\n   - The **Department** auto-populates from the job position's linked department (`job.department_id`).\n\n3. **Reordering the form:**\n   - Put **Department** first, followed immediately by **Job Position / Role**, so the flow is logical:\n     1. **Department**\n     2. **Job Position / Role** (filtered by Department)\n     3. **Reports To (Manager)**\n     4. **Expense / Voucher Approver**\n\n---\n\n### Proposed Change:\n\n#### 1. In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py):\n```python\n@api.onchange('crm_department_id')\ndef _onchange_crm_department_id(self):\n    if self.crm_department_id and self.crm_job_id and self.crm_job_id.department_id != self.crm_department_id:\n        self.crm_job_id = False\n\n@api.onchange('crm_job_id')\ndef _onchange_crm_job_id(self):\n    if self.crm_job_id and self.crm_job_id.department_id:\n        self.crm_department_id = self.crm_job_id.department_id\n```\n\n#### 2. In [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml):\nFilter `crm_job_id` dynamically based on selected department:\n```xml\n<field name=\"crm_department_id\" string=\"Department\" options=\"{'no_create': True, 'no_create_edit': True, 'no_open': True}\"/>\n<field name=\"crm_job_id\" string=\"Job Position / Role\" \n       domain=\"[('department_id', '=', crm_department_id)] if crm_department_id else []\"\n       options=\"{'no_create': True, 'no_create_edit': True, 'no_open': True}\"/>\n```\n\nShall I implement this Department ⇄ Job Position connection?"}

{"step_index":3793,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:37:22Z","content":"To solve the problem of **not having to open and edit every single user one by one**, the best approach is to manage hierarchy and roles **from the top down**:\n\n---\n\n### Solution: Centralized Assignment (Top-Down Management)\n\nInstead of going to `User 1` ➔ edit, `User 2` ➔ edit, `User 3` ➔ edit... we manage them directly from:\n1. **Department Screen (`hr.department`)**\n2. **Job Position / Role Screen (`hr.job`)**\n\n---\n\n### How this works in practice:\n\n#### 1. Manage from Department (`hr.department`)\nOpen **Department** (e.g. *Sales Department*):\n- **Department Manager / Head**: Select the Head of this department (e.g., *Ramesh*).\n- **Parent Department**: (e.g., *Head Office* or *Management*).\n- **Assigned Users / Employees**: A Many2many list where you can select all users in this department at once.\n- 👉 **Automatic Sync**: Any user added to this department automatically gets:\n  - Their `crm_department_id` set.\n  - Their `crm_manager_id` automatically set to the **Department Head**!\n\n#### 2. Manage from Job Position / Role (`hr.job`)\nOpen **Job Position / Role** (e.g. *Sales Executive*):\n- Linked to Department: *Sales*\n- Default Permissions: Set once for the whole role (e.g., *Lead & Quote: Own Documents*, *Customer: Create/Update/View*, etc.).\n- **Assigned Users**: A multi-select box (`user_ids`) on the Job Position form!\n  - Click **\"Add Users\"** ➔ check 5 or 10 users at once (e.g., *Amit, Priya, Rahul*).\n  - 👉 **Instant Sync**: All selected users immediately get:\n    - `crm_job_id` = *Sales Executive*\n    - `crm_department_id` = *Sales*\n    - All permissions applied automatically!\n\n#### 3. Quick Mass Edit / List View\nIn the **Users List View** (`Settings > Users` or `CRM > Team Users`):\n- Add columns: `Department`, `Job Position`, `Reports To (Manager)`.\n- You can select multiple users and use **Action > Export / Mass Update** or edit inline without opening each form!\n\n---\n\n### The Result:\n1. **Setup takes 2 minutes**: You set up the Department and Roles once.\n2. **Assign in bulk**: Add users to the Role/Department in a single click.\n3. **No manual repetition**: Users automatically inherit the Department Head as their Manager, and inherit all role permissions.\n\nWould you like me to implement this top-down assignment on **Job Position** and **Department**?"}

{"step_index":3801,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:38:57Z","content":"This is a common organizational pattern: each department has its own Head/Manager, its own distinct roles, and employees under that department report to that Head.\n\nTo handle this cleanly without opening every user record one by one, we can structure it like this:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Structure by Department (`hr.department`)\nEach Department (e.g., *Sales*, *Service*, *Finance*) has:\n* **Department Head / Manager** (`manager_user_id`)\n* **Job Positions / Roles** (e.g., *Sales Executive*, *Sales Assistant*)\n* **Department Members / Users** (`member_user_ids` multi-select)\n\n```\n                       [ Company ]\n                            │\n       ┌────────────────────┴────────────────────┐\n [ Sales Department ]                     [ Service Department ]\n Head: Ramesh (Manager)                   Head: Suresh (Manager)\n      │                                        │\n      ├── Sales Executive (Role)               ├── Service Engineer (Role)\n      │     └── Amit, Priya                          └── Rahul, Vikas\n      └── Sales Telecaller (Role)              └── AMC Coordinator (Role)\n            └── Neha                                 └── Pooja\n```\n\n---\n\n### 2. Automatic Inheritance (Zero Manual Repetition)\n\nWhen you assign a user to a **Department** or **Job Position**:\n1. **Manager Auto-Set:** If Amit is assigned to the *Sales Department*, his **\"Reports To (Manager)\"** automatically becomes **Ramesh (Sales Head)**. You don't have to fill it in manually!\n2. **Roles Filtered by Department:** When picking a role for an employee in *Sales*, only *Sales* roles appear in the dropdown.\n3. **Different Department Head = Different Manager:**\n   - Employees in *Sales* automatically report to the **Sales Head**.\n   - Employees in *Service* automatically report to the **Service Head**.\n   - If an employee has a custom team lead, you can still override the manager on their profile if needed.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Bulk Assignment Screen (Assign 10 Users at Once)\n\nOn the **Department** and **Job Position** forms:\n- Add an **\"Assigned Users\"** multi-select field (`many2many_tags` or checklist).\n- You can simply open **Sales Department** ➔ click **\"Add Members\"** ➔ select Amit, Priya, Neha ➔ **Save**.\n- All 3 users immediately get:\n  - Department = *Sales*\n  - Reports To = *Ramesh (Sales Head)*\n  - Corresponding permissions applied.\n\n---\n\n### Next Step:\nShould I implement:\n1. **Department Head** field (`manager_user_id`) on Department.\n2. **Bulk User Assignment** (`member_user_ids`) on Department and Job Position.\n3. **Auto-fill \"Reports To\"**: Setting user's manager automatically based on their Department Head."}

{"step_index":3803,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:42:18Z","content":"By standard ERP & CRM best practice design, here is **exactly which page should show what**, so it is intuitive and confusion-free:\n\n---\n\n### **PAGE 1: Department Page (`hr.department`)**\n> **Purpose:** Defines the organizational structure, who leads the department, and who belongs to it.\n\n**What you see on this page:**\n1. **Department Name** (e.g., *Sales*, *Service*, *Finance*)\n2. **Department Head / Manager** (`manager_user_id` — e.g., *Ramesh*)\n3. **Parent Department** (for sub-departments, e.g. *Sales North* reports to *Sales India*)\n4. **Department Members / Assigned Users** (`member_user_ids`):\n   - A multi-select box or list of all users in this department.\n   - **Benefit:** In 1 click, you can add 10 users to the *Sales Department*. All 10 automatically have their manager set to the Department Head (*Ramesh*).\n\n---\n\n### **PAGE 2: Roles & Permissions Page (`hr.job`)**\n> **Purpose:** Defines job titles and what actions (permissions) users in that role can perform.\n\n**What you see on this page:**\n1. **Role / Job Title** (e.g., *Sales Executive*, *Service Engineer*)\n2. **Department** (Dropdown: select *Sales*, *Service*, etc.)\n3. **Assigned Users** (`user_ids`):\n   - Multi-select box showing who holds this role.\n   - When you select a Department (e.g. *Sales*), the user list automatically shows the members of that department!\n4. **Permissions Checklist**:\n   - *Lead & Quotation* (Own / All / Admin)\n   - *Customer Creation* (Create, Update, View, Delete)\n   - *Equipment Master* (Create, Update, View, Delete)\n   - *Product Catalog* (Create, Update, View, Delete)\n   - *Service Ticket*, *AMC*, *Excel Export*, etc.\n\n---\n\n### **How the 2 Pages Work Together (Step-by-Step Flow):**\n\n| Step | Page | What you do (takes 30 seconds) |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Step 1** | **Department** | Create Department (*\"Sales\"*), pick Department Head (*\"Ramesh\"*), and select its 5 employees. |\n| **Step 2** | **Roles & Permissions** | Open *\"Sales Executive\"*, link to *\"Sales\"* Department, set permissions (View, Create, etc.), and check the users who have this role. |\n| **Step 3** | **Done!** | You **never need to open the single user form**. All 5 users automatically have the right Department, the right Manager, and the right Permissions.\n\n---\n\n### Summary:\n- **Department Page** = Sets **Who works where** and **Who reports to which Department Head**.\n- **Roles & Permissions Page** = Sets **What access/rights each job role has** and **assigns the role to users**.\n\nWould you like to review the proposed layout for these 2 pages before we implement them?"}

{"step_index":3805,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-22T10:43:54Z","content":"That's an important question. To avoid the **\"chicken-and-egg\"** problem (i.e. *“Do I create the department first, the role first, or the manager first?”*), here is the straightforward order:\n\n---\n\n### The Natural 3-Step Setup (No Confusion)\n\n#### **Step 1: Department Page (Create the Department First)**\nYou start with the department:\n1. Type Department Name (e.g., **\"Sales\"**).\n2. Select **Department Head / Manager** (dropdown shows existing users, e.g. **\"Ramesh\"**).\n3. Save.\n\n---\n\n#### **Step 2: Roles & Permissions Page (Create the Role and Link to Department)**\nNow create the role for that department:\n1. Type Role Name (e.g., **\"Sales Executive\"** or **\"Sales Manager\"**).\n2. Select Department: **\"Sales\"** (from Step 1).\n3. Tick the permission checkboxes:\n   - *Lead & Quotation: Own Documents*\n   - *Customer: Create, Update, View*\n   - *Product: View*\n4. Save.\n\n---\n\n#### **Step 3: Assign Users (All at Once!)**\nOn that same **Roles & Permissions** page:\n- In the **\"Assigned Users\"** box, simply select your employees: `Amit`, `Priya`, `Neha`.\n- Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### What happens automatically in the background:\n- `Amit`, `Priya`, and `Neha` immediately get:\n  - **Department** = *Sales*\n  - **Job Role** = *Sales Executive*\n  - **Reports To (Manager)** = *Ramesh* (auto-filled because Ramesh is the Sales Head!)\n  - **All Access Permissions** = Applied automatically.\n\n---\n\n### In Short:\n1. **Department First**: Name the department and pick who the Head/Manager is.\n2. **Role Second**: Name the role, select the department, set the checkboxes.\n3. **Select Users**: Tag the users into that role. Everything else connects automatically."}
