{"step_index":6137,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T06:38:27Z","content":"Here is your exact, step-by-step checklist to build the hierarchy starting from **Admin (Owner) down to 2 Managers and 4 Employees**:\n\n---\n\n### **LEVEL 0: ADMIN / OWNER (Already Exists)**\n- **User**: `Admin` (or Dhruvil / Himanshu).\n- This is the top of the pyramid. Everyone ultimately reports up to this level.\n\n---\n\n### **LEVEL 1: CREATE THE 2 MANAGERS**\n\n#### **Step 1: Create the Manager Users**\n1. Go to **Settings ➔ Users** (or Dashboard ➔ Admin menu ➔ Users) ➔ Click **New**:\n   - **Name**: `Sales Manager` (or person's actual name like *Ramesh*)\n   - **Email**: `sales.manager@yourcompany.com`\n   - Click **Save** ➔ ⚙️ Action ➔ **Change Password** (set their password).\n2. Click **New** again for Manager 2:\n   - **Name**: `Service Manager` (or person's actual name like *Suresh*)\n   - **Email**: `service.manager@yourcompany.com`\n   - Click **Save** ➔ ⚙️ Action ➔ **Change Password**.\n\n#### **Step 2: Assign Manager Roles in Roles & Groups**\n1. Go to **Admin Menu ➔ Roles & Groups** (or Job Positions):\n   - Open **Sales Manager** role (or click New if not created):\n     - **Primary Department**: `Sales`\n     - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON** (Checked)\n     - **Reporting Manager**: Select `Admin`\n     - **Permissions Tab**:\n       - Lead & Quotation: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n       - Excel Export: `Yes`\n       - Customer / Product / Equipment: Check `View`, `Create`, `Update`\n     - Click **Save**.\n   - Open **Service Manager** role (or click New):\n     - **Primary Department**: `Service` (or Technical)\n     - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON** (Checked)\n     - **Reporting Manager**: Select `Admin`\n     - **Permissions Tab**:\n       - Service Ticket: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n       - AMC Contract: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n       - Excel Export: `Yes`\n     - Click **Save**.\n\n#### **Step 3: Link Managers to their Departments**\n1. Go to **Departments** (or Employee ➔ Departments):\n   - Open **Sales Department**:\n     - **Department Head**: Select `Sales Manager`\n     - Click **Save**.\n   - Open **Service Department**:\n     - **Department Head**: Select `Service Manager`\n     - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **LEVEL 2: CREATE THE 2 EMPLOYEE ROLES**\n\nIn **Roles & Groups**, create the roles for the staff under those managers:\n1. **Sales Executive**:\n   - **Primary Department**: `Sales`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **OFF** (Unchecked)\n   - *Notice: Reporting Manager automatically auto-fills with `Sales Manager`!*\n   - **Permissions Tab**:\n     - Lead & Quotation: `User: Own Documents Only`\n   - Click **Save**.\n2. **Service Engineer**:\n   - **Primary Department**: `Service`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **OFF** (Unchecked)\n   - *Notice: Reporting Manager automatically auto-fills with `Service Manager`!*\n   - **Permissions Tab**:\n     - Service Ticket: `User: Own Documents Only`\n     - AMC Contract: `User: Own Documents Only`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **LEVEL 3: ADD THE 4 EMPLOYEES**\n\nNow create the 4 employees:\n1. **Sales Team (2 Staff)**:\n   - Create Employee 1A (e.g. `Hello`):\n     - Set Job Role: `Sales Executive`.\n     - *Reports To automatically becomes `Sales Manager`!*\n   - Create Employee 1B (e.g. `Vishal`):\n     - Set Job Role: `Sales Executive`.\n     - *Reports To automatically becomes `Sales Manager`!*\n\n2. **Service Team (2 Staff)**:\n   - Create Employee 2A:\n     - Set Job Role: `Service Engineer`.\n     - *Reports To automatically becomes `Service Manager`!*\n   - Create Employee 2B:\n     - Set Job Role: `Service Engineer`.\n     - *Reports To automatically becomes `Service Manager`!*\n\n---\n\n### ✅ Done!\nYou now have:\n- **Admin**: Oversees everything.\n- **Sales Manager**: Oversees Hello & Vishal.\n- **Service Manager**: Oversees the 2 Service Engineers.\n- **Employees**: Only see their own documents.\n\nStart with **Level 1 (Step 1)** by creating the two Manager users!"}

{"step_index":6139,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T06:39:39Z","content":"Here are the direct answers to your 3 questions about Admin:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Does Admin need a Job Position?\n**No, it is optional, but RECOMMENDED to give Admin a title like \"Managing Director\" or \"Owner / CEO\".**\n- Technically, Admin already has full superuser rights, so permissions don't depend on a role.\n- **BUT** if you assign Admin a Job Position like `Managing Director` (or `CEO`), it gives Admin a proper clean title everywhere across the system and in employee lists.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Does Admin need a Department?\n**Yes, set Admin's department to `Management` (or `Executive / Administration`).**\n- Setting Admin in the `Management` department keeps the organizational structure clean.\n- Sales Department and Service Department report up to `Management`.\n\n---\n\n### 3. In the Hierarchy Chart / Org Tree, will Admin be seen at the very top?\n**YES! 100% at the very top!**\n\nIn standard Odoo and in organization charts:\n- Odoo determines the top of the tree by looking for: **Who has NO manager above them? (`Reports To = Empty`)**.\n- For **Admin**:\n  - `Reports To (Manager)` = **Empty / Blank** (because nobody is above the Owner/Admin).\n- For **Managers** (Sales Manager & Service Manager):\n  - `Reports To` = **Admin**.\n- For **Employees** (Hello, Vishal, Engineers):\n  - `Reports To` = **Sales Manager / Service Manager**.\n\nBecause Admin has no manager above them, Odoo's Organization Tree automatically places **Admin at the very top root** of the chart, with the 2 Managers branching below, and the employees branching under their respective managers!"}

{"step_index":6141,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T06:41:51Z","content":"Perfect! Starting from a clean slate is the best and cleanest way.\n\nFollow these **4 Steps in exact order**:\n\n---\n\n### **STEP 1: CREATE THE DEPARTMENTS**\nGo to **Admin Menu ➔ Departments** (or HR / Employee ➔ Departments) and create 3 departments:\n\n1. **Department 1: `Management`**\n   - Name: `Management`\n   - Parent Department: *(Leave Blank)*\n   - Department Head: Select `Admin` (or Dhruvil Shah)\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n2. **Department 2: `Sales`**\n   - Name: `Sales`\n   - Parent Department: Select `Management`\n   - Department Head: *(Leave blank for now, we will link the manager in Step 3)*\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n3. **Department 3: `Service`**\n   - Name: `Service`\n   - Parent Department: Select `Management`\n   - Department Head: *(Leave blank for now)*\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **STEP 2: CREATE THE 2 MANAGER JOB POSITIONS**\nGo to **Admin Menu ➔ Roles & Groups** (Job Positions) ➔ Click **New**:\n\n1. **Role 1: `Sales Manager`**\n   - Job Position: `Sales Manager`\n   - Primary Department: Select `Sales`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON** (Checked)\n   - Reporting Manager: Select `Admin`\n   - **Permissions Tab**:\n     - Lead & Quotation: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n     - Excel Export: `Yes`\n     - Customer Creation: Check `Create`, `Update`, `View`\n     - Product Catalog: Check `View`\n     - Equipment Master: Check `View`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n2. **Role 2: `Service Manager`**\n   - Job Position: `Service Manager`\n   - Primary Department: Select `Service`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON** (Checked)\n   - Reporting Manager: Select `Admin`\n   - **Permissions Tab**:\n     - Service Ticket: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n     - AMC Contract: `User: All Documents` (or Administrator)\n     - Excel Export: `Yes`\n     - Customer Creation: Check `View`\n     - Equipment Master: Check `Create`, `Update`, `View`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **STEP 3: CREATE THE 2 MANAGER USERS & LINK TO DEPARTMENTS**\nGo to **Settings ➔ Users** (or Dashboard ➔ Admin ➔ Users):\n\n1. **Create Sales Manager User**:\n   - Click **New**\n   - Name: `Sales Manager` (or the person's name)\n   - Email: `salesmanager@gmail.com`\n   - In **Organization & Hierarchy tab**:\n     - Role: Select `Sales Manager`\n     - Department: Auto-fills with `Sales`\n     - Reports To: Auto-fills with `Admin`\n   - Click **Save** ➔ ⚙️ Action ➔ **Change Password** (set their password).\n\n2. **Create Service Manager User**:\n   - Click **New**\n   - Name: `Service Manager` (or the person's name)\n   - Email: `servicemanager@gmail.com`\n   - In **Organization & Hierarchy tab**:\n     - Role: Select `Service Manager`\n     - Department: Auto-fills with `Service`\n     - Reports To: Auto-fills with `Admin`\n   - Click **Save** ➔ ⚙️ Action ➔ **Change Password**.\n\n3. **Link them as Heads in Departments**:\n   - Go back to **Departments**:\n     - Open **Sales Department** ➔ Set **Department Head** = `Sales Manager` ➔ Save.\n     - Open **Service Department** ➔ Set **Department Head** = `Service Manager` ➔ Save.\n\n---\n\n### **STEP 4: CREATE EMPLOYEE ROLES & ASSIGN STAFF**\n\n1. **Create the Employee Roles in Roles & Groups**:\n   - Role: `Sales Executive`\n     - Department: `Sales`\n     - Is Manager / Head: **OFF** (Unchecked)\n     - *(Notice: Reporting Manager auto-fills with `Sales Manager`!)*\n     - Permissions: Lead & Quotation = `User: Own Documents Only`\n     - Click **Save**.\n   - Role: `Service Engineer`\n     - Department: `Service`\n     - Is Manager / Head: **OFF** (Unchecked)\n     - *(Notice: Reporting Manager auto-fills with `Service Manager`!)*\n     - Permissions: Service Ticket = `User: Own Documents Only`, AMC = `User: Own Documents Only`\n     - Click **Save**.\n\n2. **Assign or Create the 4 Employees**:\n   - Open **Hello** ➔ Set Role: `Sales Executive` (Reports To = `Sales Manager`).\n   - Open **Vishal** ➔ Set Role: `Sales Executive` (Reports To = `Sales Manager`).\n   - Create Service Engineer 1 ➔ Set Role: `Service Engineer` (Reports To = `Service Manager`).\n   - Create Service Engineer 2 ➔ Set Role: `Service Engineer` (Reports To = `Service Manager`).\n\n---\n\nTell me once you finish **Step 1 (creating the 3 departments)** and we will verify!"}

{"step_index":6161,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T06:54:04Z","content":"Here is exactly why Reporting Manager is empty in your screenshot:\n\n### What the system is looking for:\nWhen you turn **\"Is Manager / Head\" = ON** for the `Sales` department:\nThe system looks at:\n1. `Sales Department` ➔ **Parent Department** (which is `Management`).\n2. Inside `Management`, it looks for **Department Head** (`manager_user_id` or `manager_id`).\n\nBecause `Management` department does not have its Department Head selected yet, it finds nobody and stays blank!\n\n---\n\n### How to make it auto-fill:\n1. Go to **Departments**:\n2. Open **Management**:\n   - Set **Department Head** = `Admin` (or Dhruvil Shah).\n   - Click **Save**.\n3. Also set **Parent Department** of `Sales` = `Management`.\n\nThe moment `Management` has `Admin` as its Head, then on any Manager role with \"Is Manager / Head\" = ON, **Reporting Manager will automatically auto-fill with `Admin`**!\n\n---\n\n### Even better fallback:\nIf a department doesn't have a parent manager set yet, we can make the system automatically **fall back to the Company Admin / Superuser (Admin)** so Reporting Manager is NEVER left empty!\n\nShall I add that fallback to `Admin` right now?"}

{"step_index":6172,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T06:59:02Z","content":"You are 100% right! \n\nIf the Department **already has the Manager set**, asking the admin to pick the manager again on the Job Position page is completely redundant and causes double work.\n\n### How it should work:\nThe Department is the **Single Source of Truth**:\n1. In **Department Settings**:\n   - You set **Department Head** (e.g. *Sales Manager*).\n   - You set **Reporting / Senior Manager** (e.g. *Admin*).\n2. On the **Job Position (Role) page**:\n   - The admin only picks the **Primary Department** (e.g. `Sales`) and toggles **\"Is Manager / Head\"**.\n   - **Reporting Manager should be 100% automatically fetched from the Department**:\n     - If \"Is Manager\" is **ON** ➔ System auto-shows the Department's **Reporting / Senior Manager** (`senior_manager_user_id` or parent department head).\n     - If \"Is Manager\" is **OFF** ➔ System auto-shows the Department's **Department Head** (`manager_user_id`).\n   - The field stays read-only/display-only, so the admin **NEVER has to select it again**!\n\n### Why it was empty in your screenshot:\nIn your `Sales` department, the **Reporting Manager / Senior Manager** (`senior_manager_user_id`) field was still empty! \n\nIf you open **Departments ➔ Sales**:\n- Set **Senior / Reporting Manager** = `Admin` (or set Parent Department = `Management` where Admin is head).\n- Once saved in Department, the Job Position page **automatically pulls and displays it with ZERO extra clicks**!"}

{"step_index":6174,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:00:04Z","content":"Here is the exact, fail-proof checklist to finish the whole hierarchy:\n\n---\n\n### **TASK 1: Configure Departments (Single Source of Truth)**\nGo to **Admin Menu ➔ Departments**:\n\n1. **Department: `Management`**\n   - Department Name: `Management`\n   - Department Head: Select `Admin`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n2. **Department: `Sales`**\n   - Department Name: `Sales`\n   - Parent Department: Select `Management`\n   - Reporting / Senior Manager: Select `Admin`\n   - Department Head: *(Leave empty until we create the Sales Manager user in Task 3)*\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n3. **Department: `Service`**\n   - Department Name: `Service`\n   - Parent Department: Select `Management`\n   - Reporting / Senior Manager: Select `Admin`\n   - Department Head: *(Leave empty until we create the Service Manager user in Task 3)*\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **TASK 2: Create Job Positions (Roles & Groups)**\nGo to **Admin Menu ➔ Roles & Groups**:\n\n1. **Role 1: `Sales Manager`**\n   - Primary Department: Select `Sales`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON**\n   - *(Notice: Reporting Manager automatically displays `Admin`!)*\n   - Set Permissions (e.g. Lead & Quote = Administrator, Export = Yes).\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n2. **Role 2: `Service Manager`**\n   - Primary Department: Select `Service`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **ON**\n   - *(Notice: Reporting Manager automatically displays `Admin`!)*\n   - Set Permissions (e.g. Ticket = Administrator, AMC = Administrator).\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n3. **Role 3: `Sales Executive`**\n   - Primary Department: Select `Sales`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **OFF**\n   - *(Notice: Will auto-link to Sales Manager)*\n   - Permissions: Lead & Quote = `User: Own Documents Only`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n4. **Role 4: `Service Engineer`**\n   - Primary Department: Select `Service`\n   - **Is Manager / Head**: **OFF**\n   - *(Notice: Will auto-link to Service Manager)*\n   - Permissions: Ticket = `User: Own Documents Only`\n   - Click **Save**.\n\n---\n\n### **TASK 3: Create Manager Users & Appoint as Dept Heads**\nGo to **Settings ➔ Users**:\n\n1. **Create `Sales Manager` User**:\n   - Name: `Sales Manager` (or person's name)\n   - Email: `salesmanager@gmail.com`\n   - Assign Role: `Sales Manager` (auto-assigns Department `Sales` and Manager `Admin`).\n   - Click **Save** ➔ Change Password.\n2. **Create `Service Manager` User**:\n   - Name: `Service Manager`\n   - Email: `servicemanager@gmail.com`\n   - Assign Role: `Service Manager`.\n   - Click **Save** ➔ Change Password.\n\n3. **Appoint them as Department Heads**:\n   - Go to **Departments ➔ Sales**: Set **Department Head** = `Sales Manager` ➔ Save.\n   - Go to **Departments ➔ Service**: Set **Department Head** = `Service Manager` ➔ Save.\n\n---\n\n### **TASK 4: Assign Frontline Staff (Executives & Engineers)**\nGo to **Users**:\n1. Open **Hello**: Set Role = `Sales Executive` ➔ Reports To automatically fills with `Sales Manager`.\n2. Open **Vishal**: Set Role = `Sales Executive` ➔ Reports To automatically fills with `Sales Manager`.\n3. Create Service Engineer 1: Set Role = `Service Engineer` ➔ Reports To automatically fills with `Service Manager`.\n4. Create Service Engineer 2: Set Role = `Service Engineer` ➔ Reports To automatically fills with `Service Manager`.\n\n---\n\nStart with **TASK 1** right now (set `Admin` as Senior Manager in Sales & Service departments) and save!"}

{"step_index":6195,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:10:26Z","content":"On the **Department form**, because the hierarchy and reporting manager are now handled via **Parent Department** (or via the **Job Position**), the field you can remove or hide from the department page is:\n\n### 1. The Redundant Field in the Department Form:\nIn `res_users_signature_views.xml`:\n- **`senior_manager_user_id` (\"Reporting Manager\")**:\n  Since reporting manager is automatically derived from the **Parent Department** (`parent_id`) and set on the Job Position, having a manual \"Reporting Manager\" field directly on the Department form is redundant and causes confusion.\n\n---\n\n### If you want to remove/hide it from the Department view:\n\nIn [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L224-L227):\n\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//field[@name='manager_id']\" position=\"after\">\n    <field name=\"manager_user_id\" string=\"Department Head\" options=\"{'no_create': True, 'no_open': True}\"/>\n</xpath>\n```\n*(Removing `<field name=\"senior_manager_user_id\" .../>`)*\n\n---\n\n### What stays on the Department Form:\n1. **Department Name** (e.g., *Sales*)\n2. **Parent Department** (e.g., *Management*)\n3. **Department Head** (`manager_user_id` — optional, for assigning the head)\n4. Standard **Company** field\n\nWould you like me to remove `senior_manager_user_id` from the Department view XML for you now?"}

{"step_index":6200,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:12:45Z","content":"In your screenshot, under **DEPARTMENT ORGANIZATION**, it shows:\n```\nManagement   [ 0 ]\n  Sales      [ 0 ]\n```\n\n### Why are both showing `0`?\nThe badge `[ 0 ]` in Odoo's standard department tree widget counts **`hr.employee`** records (the Employees module records), **not** `res.users`!\n\n1. When you select **Department Head = Hello** (or Administrator), it updates `manager_user_id` on the department, but **no `hr.employee` record has been linked or counted yet**.\n2. Neither **Admin** nor **Hello** has a linked `hr.employee` record assigned to that department yet, or their job role hasn't been set on their user profile.\n\n---\n\n### How to make the count show `1`?\n\n1. Go to the **User form** for **Hello** (or **Admin**):\n   - Set **Department** = `Sales` (or `Management`)\n   - Set **Job Position** = `Sales Manager`\n   - Save.\n2. In our custom CRM code, the system will link them and reflect them under **Department Members** tab at the bottom!\n3. The hierarchy structure itself:\n   ```\n   Management\n      └── Sales\n   ```\n   is **100% correct and connected**! The numbers `[ 0 ]` will update as soon as the users are assigned their department and job positions."}

{"step_index":6202,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:17:08Z","content":"Looking at your screenshot, **this is completely solved and working properly!** 🎉\n\n- **Management** has child departments:\n  - **Sales** `[ 1 ]` ✅ (1 member counted)\n  - **Service** `[ 1 ]` ✅ (1 member counted)\n\n### Why is `Management` showing `0`?\nOnly because **Administrator** hasn't been assigned `Department = Management` on their user/employee profile yet. \n\nIf you want `Management` to show `[ 1 ]` as well:\n1. {"step_index":6204,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:18:43Z","content":"Yes, that is the proper design! To get a **clear 3-level hierarchy** across all 3 tiers (Top Admin -> Department Managers -> Field Staff):\n\n---\n\n### 1. The 3 Levels of Job Positions to Create:\n\n| Level | Job Position Name | Primary Department | Is Manager / Head? | Reporting Manager (Auto-fetched) |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Level 1 (Top)** | **Managing Director / CEO** | `Management` | **ON** | *(None / Top Level)* |\n| **Level 2 (Middle)** | **Sales Manager** | `Management / Sales` | **ON** | **Administrator** |\n| **Level 2 (Middle)** | **Service Manager** | `Management / Service` | **ON** | **Administrator** |\n| **Level 3 (Staff)** | **Sales Executive** | `Management / Sales` | **OFF** | **Sales Manager** (Hello) |\n| **Level 3 (Staff)** | **Service Engineer** | `Management / Service` | **OFF** | **Service Manager** |\n\n---\n\n### 2. Assign the Users to Each Position:\n\n1. **Level 1 (Top)**:\n   - User: **Administrator**\n   - Department: `Management`\n   - Job Position: `Managing Director / CEO`\n   - *(Now Management will show `[ 1 ]`)*\n\n2. **Level 2 (Department Managers)**:\n   - User: **Hello** (or your Sales Manager user)\n     - Department: `Sales`\n     - Job Position: `Sales Manager`\n     - Reporting Manager: `Administrator`\n   - User: **Service Manager user**\n     - Department: `Service`\n     - Job Position: `Service Manager`\n     - Reporting Manager: `Administrator`\n\n3. **Level 3 (Staff / Executives)**:\n   - User: **Sales Executive 1 & 2**\n     - Department: `Sales`\n     - Job Position: `Sales Executive`\n     - Reporting Manager: **Hello** (Sales Manager)\n   - User: **Service Engineer 1 & 2**\n     - Department: `Service`\n     - Job Position: `Service Engineer`\n     - Reporting Manager: **Service Manager**\n\n---\n\n### Result in Organization & Hierarchy:\n```\nAdministrator (Managing Director) [Management: 1]\n ├── Hello (Sales Manager) [Sales: 3]\n │    ├── Sales Executive 1\n │    └── Sales Executive 2\n └── Service Manager [Service: 3]\n      ├── Service Engineer 1\n      └── Service Engineer 2\n```\n\nEvery manager count, department count, and reporting chain will link up cleanly through all 3 tiers."}

{"step_index":6206,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T07:22:10Z","content":"**\"Managed Sub-Departments\" is specifically for top-level roles like Managing Director!**\n\nHere is exactly what it does:\n\n### 1. For **Managing Director**:\n- Since the Managing Director sits in the top department (`Management`), but also oversees and needs visibility/authority over **Sales** and **Service**:\n  - In **Managed Sub-Departments**, select:\n    - **`Sales`**\n    - **`Service`**\n- This gives the Managing Director direct management scope over both child departments!\n\n---\n\n### 2. For **Sales Manager** & **Service Manager**:\n- **Leave it Empty!**\n  - A Sales Manager only manages their own primary department (`Sales`).\n  - A Service Manager only manages their own primary department (`Service`).\n  - Unless Sales has further sub-teams (like *Domestic Sales* and *International Sales*), managers leave this blank.\n\n---\n\n### 3. For **Sales Executive** & **Service Engineer**:\n- This field is **hidden** automatically (because `Is Manager / Head` is turned OFF).\n\n---\n\n### What to do on your current screen:\n1. In **Managed Sub-Departments**, select **Sales** and **Service**.\n2. Click **Save**!"}

{"step_index":6257,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T08:28:53Z","tool_calls":[{"name":"replace_file_content","args":{"AllowMultiple":false,"Description":"Add parent_job_id, child_job_ids, and hierarchy HTML compute to hr.job","EndLine":430,"Instruction":"Add parent_job_id and child_job_ids fields, along with job_hierarchy_html compute field to render a clean tree on the right side of the Job Position form","ReplacementContent":"    # Job Position Hierarchy: Parent Job (Reporting Job) & Subordinate Jobs\n    parent_job_id = fields.Many2one(\n        'hr.job',\n        string='Parent Job Position',\n        compute='_compute_parent_job_id',\n        store=True,\n        readonly=False,\n        help='The senior job position that this role reports to.'\n    )\n\n    child_job_ids = fields.One2many(\n        'hr.job',\n        'parent_job_id',\n        string='Subordinate Roles'\n    )\n\n    job_hierarchy_html = fields.Html(\n        string='Role Hierarchy',\n        compute='_compute_job_hierarchy_html',\n        help='Visual hierarchy tree of job positions.'\n    )\n\n    @api.depends('is_manager_role', 'department_id', 'department_id.parent_id')\n    def _compute_parent_job_id(self):\n        for job in self:\n            if not job.department_id:\n                job.parent_job_id = False\n                continue\n\n            if job.is_manager_role:\n                # Department Manager reports to the Parent Department's Manager Role (e.g. Managing Director)\n                parent_dept = job.department_id.parent_id\n                if parent_dept:\n                    parent_job = self.search([\n                        ('department_id', '=', parent_dept.id),\n                        ('is_manager_role', '=', True)\n                    ], limit=1)\n                    job.parent_job_id = parent_job.id if parent_job else False\n                else:\n                    job.parent_job_id = False\n            else:\n                # Regular staff role reports to this department's Manager Role\n                mgr_job = self.search([\n                    ('department_id', '=', job.department_id.id),\n                    ('is_manager_role', '=', True)\n                ], limit=1)\n                job.parent_job_id = mgr_job.id if mgr_job else False\n\n    def _compute_job_hierarchy_html(self):\n        for job in self:\n            # Find the top root job in this branch\n            root = job\n            visited = set()\n            while root.parent_job_id and root.id not in visited:\n                visited.add(root.id)\n                root = root.parent_job_id\n\n            def render_node(node, current_id):\n                is_active = (node.id == current_id)\n                active_style = \"font-weight: 700; color: #1e3a8a; background: #e0f2fe; padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; border-left: 3px solid #0284c7;\" if is_active else \"color: #374151; padding: 0.15rem 0.45rem;\"\n                badge_style = \"background: #f1f5f9; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 0.05rem 0.45rem; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #475569; margin-left: 0.4rem; font-weight: 600;\"\n                \n                # Count users in this role\n                cnt = self.env['res.users'].sudo().search_count([('crm_job_id', '=', node.id), ('share', '=', False)])\n                if node.is_manager_role and node.department_id and (node.department_id.manager_user_id or node.department_id.manager_id):\n                    cnt = max(cnt, 1)\n\n                html = f'<div style=\"margin: 0.25rem 0;\"><span style=\"{active_style}\">{node.name or \"Untitled\"}</span><span style=\"{badge_style}\">{cnt}</span>'\n                \n                children = self.search([('parent_job_id', '=', node.id)])\n                if children:\n                    html += '<div style=\"margin-left: 1.25rem; border-left: 2px solid #e2e8f0; padding-left: 0.75rem; margin-top: 0.25rem;\">'\n                    for child in children:\n                        html += render_node(child, current_id)\n                    html += '</div>'\n                html += '</div>'\n                return html\n\n            tree_html = render_node(root, job.id)\n            job.job_hierarchy_html = f'''\n                <div style=\"font-family: inherit; font-size: clamp(0.85rem, 0.95vw, 0.95rem); line-height: 1.5; padding: 0.5rem 0;\">\n                    {tree_html}\n                </div>\n            '''\n","StartLine":382,"TargetContent":"    parent_department_id = fields.Many2one(\n        'hr.department',\n        related='department_id.parent_id',\n        string='Parent Department',\n        readonly=True\n    )\n","TargetFile":"d:/CRM Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py","toolAction":"Adding job position hierarchy fields and computation","toolSummary":"Add job hierarchy tree to hr.job model"}}]}

{"step_index":6261,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T08:29:38Z","content":"I have implemented the **Job Position Hierarchy Tree** directly on the right side of the Job Position form!\n\n### What was added:\n1. **In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L380-L460)**:\n   - Added `parent_job_id` (automatically connects staff roles to their department manager, and department managers to the Managing Director).\n   - Added `child_job_ids` (subordinate roles).\n   - Added `job_hierarchy_html` which renders an interactive role hierarchy tree showing:\n     - The complete Job Position branch from Top Level (e.g., Managing Director) down to Manager and Staff roles.\n     - Highlights the **current Job Position** with a clean active tag.\n     - Displays the badge count of employees in each role.\n\n2. **In [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L106-L108)**:\n   - Placed the **Job Position Hierarchy** right beside the Organization Scope:\n     ```\n     Managing Director [ 1 ]\n       └── Service Manager [ 1 ]\n             └── Service Engineer [ 1 ]  <-- Current Role highlighted\n     ```\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test it!"}

{"step_index":6265,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T08:31:36Z","content":"**No**, by default Odoo **does NOT** have a Job Position Hierarchy!\n\n### In Standard Odoo:\n- **`hr.department`** has a hierarchy (`parent_id` and the standard Department Organization tree widget).\n- **`hr.job`** (Job Positions) has **no hierarchy at all** in standard Odoo. Standard Odoo only treats job positions as a flat list with recruitment fields (vacancies, target dates, etc.).\n\n### In Our Custom Implementation:\nWe built this custom hierarchy system specifically for your CRM:\n1. **`parent_job_id` & `child_job_ids`**: Links staff roles under manager roles, and manager roles under the top Managing Director.\n2. **`job_hierarchy_html`**: Dynamically builds the interactive visual tree (with active node highlighting and user counts) so you can see the complete multi-tier position hierarchy on the screen just like in departments!"}

{"step_index":6293,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T08:45:35Z","content":"I found the exact issue and fixed it!\n\n### What was happening:\nWhen you selected **Hello** as **Department Head** on the **Sales** department page, it saved `manager_user_id` on the department, but it was **not automatically pushing** the `Job Position: Sales Manager` and `Reporting Manager: Administrator` back onto Hello's User profile!\n\n### What I fixed in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L775-L817):\n- Added `_sync_head_to_user()`: Whenever a user is selected as **Department Head** on a department (e.g., Hello on Sales, or Vishal on Service), the system now **automatically updates the user's profile**:\n  1. Sets **Job Position / Role** = `Sales Manager` (or `Service Manager`)\n  2. Sets **Department** = `Management / Sales`\n  3. Sets **Reports To (Manager)** = `Administrator`\n  4. Automatically applies all Manager permissions.\n\nNow you never have to manually edit the manager user's profile — selecting them as Department Head sets everything up automatically.\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test!"}

{"step_index":6345,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T09:00:50Z","content":"### The Cause:\n`widget=\"many2one_avatar_user\"` only works on `Many2one` relational fields. \nBecause `name` on `res.users` is a direct text string (`Char`), Odoo failed to parse it as an avatar relation and displayed `\"Unnamed\"` with a broken image icon.\n\n### The Fix:\nI removed the `many2one_avatar_user` widget from `<field name=\"name\"/>` in [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L36). \n\nNow it will properly display the user's actual name (e.g. **Pratham**).\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test!"}

{"step_index":6354,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T09:03:05Z","content":"### Why it was showing `Management / Sales`:\nBy default in standard Odoo, any model that has a `parent_id` (like `hr.department`) automatically prepends every parent department name separated by slashes (`Parent / Child / Sub-child`), which gets very long and cluttered as you add more hierarchy levels.\n\n### The Fix:\nIn [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L864-L877), I added:\n```python\ndef name_get(self):\n    return [(dept.id, dept.name or '') for dept in self]\n\n@api.depends('name')\ndef _compute_display_name(self):\n    for dept in self:\n        dept.display_name = dept.name or ''\n```\n\nNow, across all dropdowns, tables, and views:\n- Instead of `Management / Sales` ➡️ it will simply display **`Sales`**\n- Instead of `Management / Service` ➡️ it will simply display **`Service`**\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test!"}

{"step_index":6422,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T09:38:11Z","content":"I have fixed the issue!\n\n### What was happening:\nWhen the HTML was rendered inside Odoo's HTML field, external CSS classes can sometimes be stripped or delayed by browser CSS caching.\n\n### What I did in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L423-L455):\n1. **Guaranteed Pill Badge Visibility**: Added direct inline styles to `.org_badge` (`background-color: #dee2e6; color: #212529; border-radius: 50rem; min-width: 1.75rem; height: 1.45rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; margin-left: auto;`) so the pill badge is **always visible and pushed to the right edge**, regardless of CSS cache!\n2. **Proper L-Shaped Branch Corner**: Positioned the connecting corner line (`top: -0.4rem; left: -1.25rem; width: 1.05rem; height: 1.45rem; border-left: 1px solid #c9d1d9; border-bottom: 1px solid #c9d1d9;`) so the left-bottom line hooks accurately under each parent role.\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test it!"}

{"step_index":6426,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T09:40:48Z","content":"I will not change any code until you review and permit it. Here is the exact problem:\n\n---\n\n### The Problem:\n1. In Odoo forms, `<field name=\"job_hierarchy_html\" widget=\"html\"/>` is rendered inside an **isolated container / iframe / clean HTML sanitizer** that has a wrapper with `max-width: 100%` or table cell constraints.\n2. Because of this wrapper:\n   - **The Badge (`.org_badge`)**: Is getting squished or hidden off to the right because the container wrapper in the group doesn't have an explicit `min-width` or `display: block`.\n   - **The L-Shaped Branch Line (`.org_branch_line`)**: Is an empty `<span></span>`. When Odoo cleans HTML or renders it, empty `<span>` tags without content have `0` width and height unless styled with `display: inline-block` and correct positioning relative to the line height.\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Solution (Only in `form_custom.css`):\nWe do **not** touch `res_users.py` at all! Your `res_users.py` with clean class names (`.crm_job_org_tree`, `.org_node`, `.org_row`, `.org_name`, `.org_badge`, `.org_children`, `.org_branch_line`) is the right way.\n\nWe only add the precise CSS rules in `form_custom.css`:\n\n```css\n/* 1. Ensure the container takes full column width */\n.crm_job_org_tree {\n  width: 100% !important;\n  max-width: 20rem !important;\n}\n\n/* 2. Position the row so name is left, pill badge is far right */\n.crm_job_org_tree .org_row {\n  display: flex !important;\n  align-items: center !important;\n  justify-content: space-between !important;\n  position: relative !important;\n  padding: 4px 0 !important;\n}\n\n/* 3. The Pill Badge - exact match to Department Organization */\n.crm_job_org_tree .org_badge {\n  background-color: #dee2e6 !important;\n  color: #212529 !important;\n  border-radius: 50rem !important;\n  min-width: 24px !important;\n  height: 20px !important;\n  display: inline-flex !important;\n  align-items: center !important;\n  justify-content: center !important;\n  font-size: 12px !important;\n  font-weight: 600 !important;\n  padding: 0 6px !important;\n  flex-shrink: 0 !important;\n}\n\n/* 4. The L-Shaped Connector Line - accurately connected */\n.crm_job_org_tree .org_branch_line {\n  position: absolute !important;\n  left: -16px !important;\n  top: -8px !important;\n  width: 12px !important;\n  height: 20px !important;\n  border-left: 1px solid #ced4da !important;\n  border-bottom: 1px solid #ced4da !important;\n  display: block !important;\n}\n```\n\n---\n\nWould you like me to apply this styling update to [form_custom.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/form_custom.css)?"}

{"step_index":6433,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:04:30Z","content":"Look at your screenshot carefully:\n1. **The pill badges ARE appearing now!** They are the grey rounded pills (`[ 1 ]`) next to each role name!\n2. **The two real issues visible in the screenshot are**:\n   - **Problem A (Tree structure flat)**: Notice how `Sales Manager`, `Sales Executive`, `Service Manager`, `Service Engineer` are not nested under `Managing Director`. They are aligned directly below each other because `parent_job_id` wasn't stored/populated for existing roles.\n   - **Problem B (Misplaced L line)**: An orphaned `L` line appeared at the top left of `Managing Director`, but Managing Director is the top root (it shouldn't have an L connector).\n   - **Problem C (Pill alignment)**: The badges are sitting right next to the role names instead of pushed to the far right, because the Odoo `<div class=\"o_field_html\">` container shrinks width.\n\n---\n\n### The Fix:\n\n1. **In `form_custom.css`**:\n   Add this so the HTML field wrapper expands full width and pushes `.org_badge` to the far right edge:\n   ```css\n   .o_field_widget[name=\"job_hierarchy_html\"] {\n       width: 100% !important;\n       display: block !important;\n   }\n   .crm_job_org_tree {\n       width: 100% !important;\n   }\n   .crm_job_org_tree .org_children {\n       margin-left: 20px !important;\n       padding-left: 8px !important;\n       position: relative !important;\n   }\n   ```\n\n2. **In `res_users.py`**:\n   - Only show the `org_branch_line` connector for **child roles** (`is_child=True`), never on the top root role (removes that misplaced L line at top).\n   - Dynamically build the tree based on **Primary Department & Manager toggle** directly so it nests properly even if `parent_job_id` was empty in the database!\n\nDo I have your permission to apply these two adjustments?"}

{"step_index":6438,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:08:22Z","content":"The reason the UI hasn't updated is because of **Problem 2 in `res_users.py`** that we discussed:\n\n### The Real Problem in `res_users.py`:\nIn `res_users.py`:\n1. **The Tree Hierarchy is Flat**: \n   `_compute_parent_job_id` was written with `store=True`. In Odoo, when a stored field is newly added to an existing database, existing records in the database have `parent_job_id = NULL`! Because every record has `parent_job_id = NULL`, the code thinks every single job is a top-level root node! That is why they are rendered directly below each other without nesting.\n2. **The L-shaped branch line**:\n   Because `parent_job_id` was NULL, the recursive loop ran on all 5 nodes at the root level, drawing that broken line.\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Fix in `res_users.py`:\nInstead of relying on an empty stored field in the database, we dynamically determine parent/child roles directly:\n- **Top Level**: Jobs in `Management` department with `is_manager_role=True` (Managing Director).\n- **Level 2 (Managers)**: Jobs with `is_manager_role=True` whose department reports to Management (`Sales Manager`, `Service Manager`).\n- **Level 3 (Staff)**: Jobs with `is_manager_role=False` in that department (`Sales Executive` under Sales Manager, `Service Engineer` under Service Manager).\n\nThis guarantees the tree nests properly with:\n```\nManaging Director                       [ 1 ]\n  └── Sales Manager                     [ 1 ]\n        └── Sales Executive             [ 1 ]\n  └── Service Manager                   [ 1 ]\n        └── Service Engineer            [ 1 ]\n```\n\nAnd every badge will align to the right edge with clean nesting.\n\nMay I update `_compute_job_hierarchy_html` in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py) with this logic now?"}

{"step_index":6455,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:14:02Z","content":"The nesting in your screenshot is now structured cleanly (`Managing Director` ➔ `Sales Manager` ➔ `Sales Executive` and `Service Manager` ➔ `Service Engineer`).\n\n### What was causing the two remaining styling issues:\n1. **The 2-line break on names (`Sales Executive`, `Service Engineer`)**:\n   `max-width: 20rem` was artificially constricting the tree width, and `.org_name` lacked `white-space: nowrap !important`.\n2. **Badge position**:\n   Because of that 20rem cap, the badge was pushed right next to the wrapped name instead of floating to the far right edge of the card.\n\n### Fixed in [form_custom.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/form_custom.css#L150-L200):\n- Removed `max-width: 20rem` so it uses the full 100% width of the column.\n- Added `white-space: nowrap !important` to `.org_name` so every role name remains strictly on **one single line**.\n- Added `margin-left: auto !important` and `flex-shrink: 0` to `.org_badge` so the grey pill badge is pinned to the **far right edge**, exactly matching Department Organization.\n\nYou can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test!"}

{"step_index":6458,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:18:20Z","content":"Looking closely at the two images:\n\n1. **In Department Organization (left image)**:\n   - Notice the vertical line from `Management` goes **all the way down**, and branches off to `Sales` (`├─`) and then turns into `Service` (`└─`).\n   - The line is a clean medium grey (`#adb5bd`).\n2. **In Job Position Hierarchy (right image)**:\n   - There is a gap between `Sales Manager` and `Service Manager` because the parent branch (`.org_children`) doesn't have a continuous vertical spine (`border-left`) connecting them!\n   - Also, `Service Manager` has its own isolated L-hook instead of continuing down from `Managing Director`.\n\n---\n\n### The Clean Solution (In `form_custom.css` only):\n\nInstead of drawing individual disconnected floating boxes, we do it the exact standard tree way:\n1. left: -1.25rem; top: -0.45rem; width: 0.95rem; height: 1.35rem; border-left: 1.5px solid #6c757d; border-bottom: 1.5px solid #6c757d; display: inline-block;\"></span>' if is_child else ''\r\n+                badge_style = \"background-color: #dee2e6; margin-left: auto;\"\r\n+\r\n+                html = f'''\r\n+                    <div style=\"position: relative; margin: 0.55rem 0;\">\r\n+                        {connector}\r\n+                        <div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; width: 100%; min-height: 1.75rem;\">\r\n+                            <span style=\"{name_style}\">{node.name or \"Untitled\"}</span>\r\n+                            <span style=\"{badge_style}\">{node.total_employee}</span>\r\n+                        </div>\r\n+                '''\r\n+\r\n+                children = all_depts.filtered(lambda d: d.parent_id.id == node.id)\r\n+                if children:\r\n+                    html += '<div style=\"position: relative; margin-left: 1.75rem; padding-left: 0.25rem;\">'\r\n+                    for child in children:\r\n+                        html += render_node(child, current_id, is_child=True)\r\n+                    html += '</div>'\r\n+                html += '</div>'\r\n+                return html\r\n+\r\n+            tree_html = render_node(root, dept.id, is_child=False)\r\n+            dept.department_hierarchy_html = f'''\r\n+                <div style=\"width: 100%; display: block; font-family: inherit; padding: 0.25rem 0 1rem 0;\">\r\n+                    {tree_html}\r\n+                </div>\r\n+            '''\r\n+\r\n     def name_get(self):\r\n         \"\"\"Display only the department's own name (e.g. 'Sales') rather than the full parent path.\"\"\"\r\n         result = []\r\n[diff_block_end]\n\nPlease note that the above snippet only shows the MODIFIED lines from the last change. {"step_index":6510,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:37:21Z","content":"### Cause:\nIn standard Odoo 17/18, `hr.view_department_form` does not have an inline `<widget name=\"hr_department_organization\">` tag (it is injected dynamically via an Enterprise/OWL sub-component). You can run `.\\sync.ps1` to test."}

{"step_index":6514,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:38:39Z","content":"Here is the direct answer without touching any code:\n\n### What the \"Pills Design\" Means:\nIn your screenshot, on the right side of **Managing Director**, **Sales Manager**, etc., you see the rounded grey badges with numbers inside them:\n```\n( 1 )\n( 1 )\n```\nThat rounded capsule/oval shape containing the number count is called a **\"pill badge\"** (or badge pill).\n\n---\n\n### Where It Is Applied in Code:\nIt is applied in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L438) inside `_compute_job_hierarchy_html`:\n\n```python\nbadge_style = \"background-color: #dee2e6; color: #212529; border-radius: 50rem; min-width: 1.75rem; height: 1.45rem; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 0.78rem; font-weight: 600; padding: 0 0.45rem; margin-left: auto;\"\n```\n\n- **`border-radius: 50rem`**: Gives it the rounded pill capsule shape (exact same as Odoo's standard badges).\n- **`background-color: #dee2e6`**: Gives it the soft grey background.\n- **`margin-left: auto`**: Pushes it to the far right side of each line."}

{"step_index":6516,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T10:40:14Z","content":"Now I understand your meaning! \n\nYou are talking about the **Active Selected Node Pill Box** (the light-blue highlight box with the colored border on the left side) that was highlighting the currently open record, like:\n\n```css\nbackground: #e0f2fe; \ncolor: #1e3a8a; \nborder-left: 3px solid #0284c7; \nborder-radius: 4px; \npadding: 2px 8px;\nfont-weight: 700;\n```\n\nWhen you have **Sales Manager** open, **Sales Manager** sits inside that nice active highlighted box with the blue left border!\n\nYou want that **exact same highlighted box design** applied to:\n1. **The open Job Position** in the Job Position Hierarchy.\n2. **The open Department** in the Department Hierarchy.\n\n---\n\n### How it will look:\n- Whichever Job Position you are currently viewing will have that nice light-blue badge box with the left colored stripe.\n- Whichever Department you are currently viewing will also have that same nice highlighted badge box.\n- All other parent/child positions remain clean and unhighlighted.\n\nShould I apply this active pill box highlight to both hierarchies for you now?"}

{"step_index":6798,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T11:57:36Z","content":"In Odoo, asset bundles compiled into `web.assets_backend` are cached in the PostgreSQL database table (`ir_attachment`) and do not update just with a server restart unless `-u crm_whitelabel` is explicitly run during boot.\n\nTo bypass asset bundle caching completely:\nI injected the style override directly into the Department XML form view ([`res_users_signature_views.xml`](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L238-L251)):\n\n```xml\n<xpath expr=\"//sheet\" position=\"before\">\n    <style>\n        .o_hr_department_chart .o_treeEntry::before,\n        .o_hr_department_chart .o_treeEntry::after,\n        .o_hr_department_chart [class*=\"treeEntry\"]::before,\n        .o_hr_department_chart [class*=\"treeEntry\"]::after,\n        .o_widget_hr_department_chart [class*=\"treeEntry\"]::before,\n        .o_widget_hr_department_chart [class*=\"treeEntry\"]::after {\n            border-color: #6c757d !important;\n            border-left-color: #6c757d !important;\n            border-bottom-color: #6c757d !important;\n        }\n    </style>\n</xpath>\n```\n\nBecause this is inside the view definition itself, Odoo sends it directly with the form HTML on every single page load, completely eliminating any asset caching issues.\n\nPlease run `.\\sync.ps1` to test."}

{"step_index":6818,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:08:04Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\nhere i have creatd sales another sub department hr so does it will display here or not ?\n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-24T17:38:04+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\crm_whitelabel\\static\\src\\css\\form_custom.css (LANGUAGE_CSS)\nCursor is on line: 160\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\views\\res_users_signature_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\res_users.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\crm_whitelabel\\static\\src\\css\\form_custom.css (LANGUAGE_CSS)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":6819,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:08:05Z","content":"**Yes, absolutely!**\n\nHere is how both display it:\n\n1. **In Department Organization (`hr.department`)**:\n   - Because standard Odoo uses `parent_id` recursively, setting **Sales** as the parent department of **HR** will automatically show **HR** nested as a sub-department under **Sales**.\n\n2. **In Job Position Hierarchy (`hr.job`)**:\n   - If you assign a Job Position to that sub-department (e.g. HR Manager/Executive with parent department Sales), it recursively follows the reporting chain (`parent_job_id`) and displays indented under the Sales role with connected tree branches."}

{"step_index":6823,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:10:10Z","content":"In standard Odoo, the native `hr_department_organization` widget operates with a specific 2-level viewing scope:\n\n1. **Parent Department** (immediate senior)\n2. **Current Department** (the record you are viewing)\n3. **Immediate Child Departments** (direct direct reports only)\n\n### Why HR didn't appear while viewing Management:\nIf you set **Sales** as the parent of **HR**:\n- Tree: `Management` ➔ `Sales` ➔ `HR`\n- When you open the **Management** department form, standard Odoo only renders its direct children (`Finance`, `Sales`, `Service`).\n- When you click on and open the **Sales** department form, you will see `Management` (parent), `Sales` (current), and **`HR`** indented directly under Sales!\n\nTo test and confirm:\nOpen **Departments** ➔ click on **Sales**, and you will see **HR** listed right under Sales with its count and line."}

{"step_index":6825,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:10:47Z","content":"**No.** By default, standard Odoo does **not** show grandchildren (sub-sub departments like HR under Sales) when viewing Management.\n\nIn default Odoo:\n- When viewing **Management**, it only displays direct children (`Sales`, `Finance`, `Service`).\n- It hides deeper levels (sub-sub departments).\n\nIf you want **Management** to show the **entire multi-level tree** (Management ➔ Sales ➔ HR), we can either:\n1. Enable full-depth recursion in Department Organization, OR\n2. Have the custom full tree on Department like on Job Positions."}

{"step_index":6901,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:23:32Z","content":"I apologize for the misunderstanding earlier. \n\nThe screenshot showed the old state because previously the xpath placed the new group **below** the main fields. \n\nHere is what has just been updated to place it in that exact red-circled **upper right** area:\n\n1. **[res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L210-L214)**:\n   - Replaced `<xpath expr=\"//sheet//group[1]\" position=\"inside\">` with:\n     ```xml\n     <xpath expr=\"//widget[@name='hr_department_chart']\" position=\"replace\">\n         <group string=\"Department Organization\">\n             <field name=\"department_hierarchy_html\" nolabel=\"1\" widget=\"html\"/>\n         </group>\n     </xpath>\n     ```\n   - This directly replaces Odoo's default chart widget right where it sits in the **upper-right side** next to the form fields, instead of rendering underneath.\n\n2. **[form_custom.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/form_custom.css#L148-L154)**:\n   - Cleaned up the CSS so the replacement hierarchy tree container won't be hidden.\n\n---\n\n### To deploy and test:\nPlease run your sync script:\n```powershell\n.\\sync.ps1\n```\nThen on the server:\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main && /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm_test.conf -d crm_data_test -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\nAnd hard refresh the browser (`Ctrl + Shift + R`). The tree will now appear directly in the **upper-right section** you circled."}

{"step_index":6982,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:31:51Z","content":"In Odoo and Linux systems, user passwords are stored as one-way cryptographic hashes (typically PBKDF2/bcrypt) and **cannot be decrypted or fetched** in plain text. \n\nHowever, depending on what you need access to, here are the standard administrative methods:\n\n---\n\n### 1. View Master / Admin Password in Config File\nIf you are looking for the Odoo master database manager password (`admin_passwd`):\n```bash\nsudo grep -E \"^(admin_passwd|db_password)\" /etc/crm_test.conf\n```\n*(or your production config file path, e.g., `/etc/odoo.conf`)*\n\n---\n\n### 2. Reset an Odoo User Password via Odoo Shell\nSince you cannot read the existing plain-text password, you can reset it to a new one from your server terminal using the Odoo shell:\n\n```bash\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin shell -c /etc/crm_test.conf -d crm_data_test\n```\nOnce inside the Python shell (`>>>`), run:\n```python\nuser = env['res.users'].search([('login', '=', 'admin')])\nuser.password = 'YourNewPasswordHere'\nenv.cr.commit()\nexit()\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. Send a Password Reset Email\nIf your outgoing mail server is configured, you can trigger a standard password reset directly from the Odoo login screen via the **\"Reset Password\"** link."}

{"step_index":6984,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:32:23Z","content":"In Odoo, user passwords cannot be retrieved or viewed by anyone—even administrators—because they are stored as one-way cryptographic hashes.\n\nIf an administrator needs to provide access or update credentials for another user, the standard administrative procedures are:\n\n---\n\n### Option 1: Reset the Password from the Odoo UI (Admin)\nIf you are logged in as an Administrator:\n1. Go to **Settings** → **Users & Companies** → **Users**.\n2. Select the specific user.\n3. Click the **Action** (gear icon) menu at the top.\n4. Select **Change Password**.\n5. Enter a new password for that user and click **Change Password**.\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: Reset the User's Password via CLI (Server Shell)\nIf you have SSH access to the server, you can set a new password for that user via the Odoo shell:\n\n1. Launch the shell:\n   ```bash\n   /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin shell -c /etc/crm_test.conf -d crm_data_test\n   ```\n2. Replace `'user_email_or_login'` and `'NewSecurePassword123'` with the actual values:\n   ```python\n   user = env['res.users'].search([('login', '=', 'user_email_or_login')])\n   if user:\n       user.password = 'NewSecurePassword123'\n       env.cr.commit()\n       print(\"Password updated successfully.\")\n   else:\n       print(\"User not found.\")\n   exit()\n   ```\n\n---\n\n### Option 3: Send a Password Reset Link\nFrom the user's form view in **Settings** → **Users**, you can click **Send Password Reset Instructions** to email the user a secure link to choose their own password."}

{"step_index":6986,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:33:17Z","content":"It is technically impossible to find or fetch any user's plaintext password via commands.\n\nIn Odoo (and modern database systems), passwords are never stored in readable text anywhere on the server or in the database. Instead, when a user creates or enters a password, Odoo passes it through a one-way mathematical function (a salted cryptographic hash using PBKDF2/SHA512). \n\nIf you query the database directly using PostgreSQL commands:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data_test -c \"SELECT login, password_crypt FROM res_users WHERE login = 'user@example.com';\"\n```\n\nThe database only stores a string that looks like this:\n```text\n$pbkdf2-sha512$25000$rO0E...encrypted_salt_and_hash...\n```\n\nBecause hashes are one-way by design:\n- There is no command or algorithm to reverse the hash back into the original password.\n- Neither the server administrator, Odoo itself, nor the database engine has access to the cleartext string.\n\nIf access is required for that account, the only standard administrative solution is to assign a new password or send a reset email as detailed previously."}

{"step_index":6992,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:47:30Z","content":"To check whether email sending is working on your system:\n\n### 1. In the Codebase:\nThere are **no custom overrides or hardcoded mail servers** in the custom addons. Email handling relies entirely on **standard Odoo core mail services** (`ir.mail_server`).\n\n---\n\n### 2. Check if Outgoing Mail is Working on Your Server:\nTo verify if an outgoing SMTP mail server is active and connected, you can run this command in your server's Odoo shell:\n\n```bash\n/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin shell -c /etc/crm_test.conf -d crm_data_test\n```\nAnd execute:\n```python\nservers = env['ir.mail_server'].search([('active', '=', True)])\nprint(\"Active mail servers found:\", len(servers))\nfor s in servers:\n    print(f\"Server: {s.name} | Host: {s.smtp_host}:{s.smtp_port} | User: {s.smtp_user}\")\n    try:\n        s.test_smtp_connection()\n        print(\" -> Connection Test: SUCCESS\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(\" -> Connection Test FAILED:\", e)\n\n# Check queued/failed emails\nfailed = env['mail.mail'].search_count([('state', '=', 'exception')])\noutgoing = env['mail.mail'].search_count([('state', '=', 'outgoing')])\nsent = env['mail.mail'].search_count([('state', '=', 'sent')])\nprint(f\"Email Status: Sent: {sent} | Queued: {outgoing} | Failed: {failed}\")\nexit()\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. Or Check via Odoo UI:\n1. Log in as an administrator and go to **Settings** → **Technical** (activate developer mode).\n2. Scroll to **Email** → **Outgoing Mail Servers**.\n3. If a server is listed, open it and click **\"Test Connection\"**:\n   - If it says **\"Connection Test Successful\"**, email sending is working.\n   - If no outgoing mail server is configured or the test fails, Odoo cannot send emails (like password reset links or notifications).\n4. You can also view sent/failed messages in **Settings** → **Technical** → **Emails**."}

{"step_index":7000,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:49:37Z","content":"This validation error is happening because there are one or more **Job Positions** currently assigned to the **Finance** department.\n\nIn database foreign key constraints, `department_id` on Job Positions has `ondelete='restrict'`. This prevents accidental deletion of a department while roles are still linked to it.\n\n---\n\n### How to resolve it:\n\n#### Option 1: Delete or Reassign the Job Positions first\n1. Go to **Settings** → **Users & Companies** → **Job Positions** (or HR → Job Positions).\n2. Filter or search for records where Department is **Finance** (e.g. *Finance Manager*, *Accountant*).\n3. Either:\n   - Change their department to another department, OR\n   - Delete those Job Positions first.\n4. Now delete the **Finance** department.\n\n#### Option 2: Change `ondelete` in code to `'cascade'` or `'set null'`\nIf you want Odoo to automatically handle it whenever a department is deleted:\n- **`ondelete='cascade'`**: When a department is deleted, any linked Job Positions are deleted automatically.\n- **`ondelete='set null'`**: When a department is deleted, linked Job Positions keep existing with their department set to empty.\n\nWould you prefer changing `department_id` in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L362) to `cascade` / `set null`, or do you prefer keeping the safety check and deleting the linked Job Position first?"}

{"step_index":7002,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:50:48Z","content":"To test permissions thoroughly across users and managers, here is the structured checklist and testing plan covering all permission controls implemented in your CRM:\n\n---\n\n### 1. The Permissions Under Test\n\n| Permission Area | Options / Granularity | What to Verify When Logged In |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Leads & Quotations** | • `None`<br>• `User: Own Documents Only`<br>• `User: All Documents`<br>• `Administrator` | • `None`: CRM / Sales menu hidden or inaccessible.<br>• `Own`: User only sees Leads/Quotes where Salesperson = them.<br>• `All`: User sees all Leads/Quotes across the company.<br>• `Admin`: User can configure sales stages, settings, etc. |\n| **Service Tickets** | • `None`<br>• `Own`<br>• `All`<br>• `Administrator` | • User only sees tickets assigned to them or their department, vs all tickets. |\n| **AMC Contracts** | • `None`<br>• `Own`<br>• `All`<br>• `Administrator` | • AMC contract visibility and renewal management. |\n| **Customer Creation (CRUD)** | • `Create` (C)<br>• `Update` (U)<br>• `View` (R)<br>• `Delete` (D) | • Try creating a new customer (New button visible/hidden).<br>• Try editing customer details.<br>• Try clicking Action → Delete on a customer record. |\n| **Product Catalog (CRUD)** | • `Create` (C)<br>• `Update` (U)<br>• `View` (R)<br>• `Delete` (D) | • Check Products menu and test Create / Edit / Delete on product items. |\n| **Equipment Master (CRUD)** | • `Create` (C)<br>• `Update` (U)<br>• `View` (R)<br>• `Delete` (D) | • Check Equipment menu and test Create / Edit / Delete. |\n| **Excel Export** | • `No`<br>• `Yes` | • Select records in list view → check if **Export** is present in the Action gear menu. |\n| **Company Creation** | • `No`<br>• `Yes` | • Check if user has permission to create companies in Settings / Contacts. |\n\n---\n\n### 2. Department & Manager Hierarchy Rules Under Test\n\n1. **Staff Role (e.g. Sales Executive)**:\n   - Linked to Department (e.g. `Sales`).\n   - Reports to Department Head (e.g. `Sales Manager`).\n   - Verify: Staff user can only see/edit within their assigned scope (e.g., Own Leads).\n2. **Department Manager / Head (e.g. Sales Manager)**:\n   - Toggle `is_manager_role = True`.\n   - Reports to Senior Manager / Parent Department Head (e.g. `Director / Management`).\n   - Verify: Manager sees their own subordinates' records and their department's data.\n3. **Sub-department Management (`sub_department_ids`)**:\n   - If a manager has managed sub-departments (e.g. Sales managing HR or Regional branches), verify they have visibility into those sub-department records.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Fastest Way to Test Without Changing Passwords\n\nInstead of logging out and typing passwords for each test user:\n1. Log in as **Administrator** (`admin`).\n2. Go to **Settings** → **Users & Companies** → **Users**.\n3. (In developer mode) Odoo provides the standard **\"Switch User\" / \"Log in as\"** button on the user profile or you can use an incognito window with test accounts.\n\nWould you like to start testing a specific role first (e.g., **Sales Executive** vs **Sales Manager**)? We can inspect the exact permission flags currently assigned to each of your test users."}

{"step_index":7008,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:51:46Z","content":"Here is the recommended setup for your **2 Managers** and **2 Employees** to test all permission levels without touching User Admin (ID 2):\n\n---\n\n### Setup Overview\n\n```\nManagement (Admin)\n └── Sales Department\n      ├── Manager: Sales Manager (Manager 1)\n      │     └── Subordinate: Sales Executive (Employee 1)\n      │\n └── Service / Operations Department\n      ├── Manager: Service Manager (Manager 2)\n      │     └── Subordinate: Service Engineer (Employee 2)\n```\n\n---\n\n### 1. Two Managers\n\n#### **Manager 1: Sales Manager**\n* **Department**: Sales  \n* **Is Manager / Head**:  **ON** (Checked)\n* **Reporting Manager**: Admin  \n* **Recommended Permissions**:\n  * **Lead & Quotation**: `User: All Documents` *(Can see all quotations and leads in the sales team)*\n  * **Service Ticket**: `User: Own Documents Only`\n  * **AMC Contract**: `User: All Documents`\n  * **Excel Export**: `Yes`\n  * **Customer**:  `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`, ❌ `Delete`\n  * **Product Catalog**:  `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`, ❌ `Delete`\n  * **Equipment**:  `View`\n\n#### **Manager 2: Service Manager**\n* **Department**: Service / Operations  \n* **Is Manager / Head**:  **ON** (Checked)\n* **Reporting Manager**: Admin  \n* **Recommended Permissions**:\n  * **Lead & Quotation**: `User: Own Documents Only` (or `None`)\n  * **Service Ticket**: `Administrator` or `User: All Documents` *(Can see all tickets in company)*\n  * **AMC Contract**: `Administrator` or `User: All Documents`\n  * **Excel Export**: `Yes`\n  * **Customer**: ❌ `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`, ❌ `Delete`\n  * **Equipment**:  `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`,  `Delete` *(Full Equipment access)*\n  * **Product Catalog**:  `View`\n\n---\n\n### 2. Two Employees (Subordinates)\n\n#### **Employee 1: Sales Executive** (Subordinate to Sales Manager)\n* **Department**: Sales  \n* **Is Manager / Head**: ❌ **OFF** (Regular staff)\n* **Reporting Manager**: `Sales Manager` *(Auto-assigned)*\n* **Recommended Permissions**:\n  * **Lead & Quotation**: `User: Own Documents Only` *(Only sees leads/quotations where salesperson = them)*\n  * **Service Ticket**: `None`\n  * **AMC Contract**: `None`\n  * **Excel Export**: `No` *(Export button hidden in Action menu)*\n  * **Customer**:  `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`, ❌ `Delete` *(Cannot delete customers)*\n  * **Product Catalog**:  `View` *(Read-only)*\n  * **Equipment**:  `View`\n\n#### **Employee 2: Service Engineer** (Subordinate to Service Manager)\n* **Department**: Service / Operations  \n* **Is Manager / Head**: ❌ **OFF** (Regular staff)\n* **Reporting Manager**: `Service Manager` *(Auto-assigned)*\n* **Recommended Permissions**:\n  * **Lead & Quotation**: `None` *(Cannot access sales/quotation records)*\n  * **Service Ticket**: `User: Own Documents Only` *(Only sees tickets assigned to them)*\n  * **AMC Contract**: `User: Own Documents Only`\n  * **Excel Export**: `No`\n  * **Customer**:  `View` *(Read-only)*\n  * **Equipment**:  `Create`,  `Update`,  `View`, ❌ `Delete`\n  * **Product Catalog**:  `View`\n\n---\n\n### What to Verify During the Test:\n\n1. **Hierarchy / Org Tree**:\n   - Open **Sales Manager** → shows **Sales Executive** in \"Assigned Employees\".\n   - Open **Service Manager** → shows **Service Engineer** in \"Assigned Employees\".\n2. **Sales Record Isolation**:\n   - Log in as **Employee 1 (Sales Executive)** → create a Quotation.\n   - Log in as **Employee 2 (Service Engineer)** → verify Employee 1's Quotation is **not visible**.\n   - Log in as **Manager 1 (Sales Manager)** → verify they **can see** Employee 1's Quotation.\n3. **Export Restriction**:\n   - In **Employee 1** list view → select records → **Export** button must **NOT** be in Action menu.\n   - In **Manager 1** list view → **Export** is **available**.\n4. **Delete Restriction**:\n   - Try deleting a Customer as **Employee 1** → delete action is blocked/hidden."}

{"step_index":7010,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-24T12:53:12Z","content":"Here is exactly how to set them up so that **Sales Manager** and **Service Manager** are at the **same level** (Level 1 under Admin / Management), with each employee at **Level 2** directly under their respective manager:\n\n---\n\n### The Level Structure:\n\n```\nLevel 0:  Admin (Top Management)\n           ├── [Level 1] Sales Manager  ───  [Level 2] Sales Executive\n           └── [Level 1] Service Manager ──  [Level 2] Service Engineer\n```\n\nBoth managers are peer department heads at **Level 1**, reporting to Admin.  \nBoth employees are subordinates at **Level 2**, reporting to their department head.\n\n---\n\n### Step-by-Step Configuration:\n\n#### 1. Departments Configuration (**HR → Departments**)\n1. **Sales Department**:\n   - **Parent Department**: `Management` (or Empty)\n   - **Department Head**: Select your `Sales Manager` user.\n2. **Service Department**:\n   - **Parent Department**: `Management` (or Empty, same parent as Sales!)\n   - **Department Head**: Select your `Service Manager` user.\n\n---\n\n#### 2. Level 1 — The Two Peer Managers (**HR → Job Positions**)\n\n* **Job Position 1: Sales Manager**\n  * **Primary Department**: `Sales`\n  * **Is Manager / Head**:  **ON**\n  * **Reporting Manager**: Auto-sets to `Admin`\n  * **Permissions**:\n    * *Lead & Quotation*: `User: All Documents`\n    * *Service Ticket*: `User: Own Documents Only`\n    * *AMC Contract*: `User: All Documents`\n    * *Excel Export*: `Yes`\n\n* **Job Position 2: Service Manager**\n  * **Primary Department**: `Service`\n  * **Is Manager / Head**:  **ON**\n  * **Reporting Manager**: Auto-sets to `Admin`\n  * **Permissions**:\n    * *Lead & Quotation*: `User: Own Documents Only`\n    * *Service Ticket*: `Administrator` or `User: All Documents`\n    * *AMC Contract*: `Administrator` or `User: All Documents`\n    * *Excel Export*: `Yes`\n\n---\n\n#### 3. Level 2 — The Two Subordinate Employees (**HR → Job Positions**)\n\n* **Job Position 3: Sales Executive**\n  * **Primary Department**: `Sales`\n  * **Is Manager / Head**: ❌ **OFF**\n  * **Reporting Manager**: Auto-sets to `Sales Manager`\n  * **Assigned Employees**: Add your **Sales Employee User**\n  * **Permissions**:\n    * *Lead & Quotation*: `User: Own Documents Only`\n    * *Service Ticket*: `None`\n    * *AMC Contract*: `None`\n    * *Excel Export*: `No`\n\n* **Job Position 4: Service Engineer**\n  * **Primary Department**: `Service`\n  * **Is Manager / Head**: ❌ **OFF**\n  * **Reporting Manager**: Auto-sets to `Service Manager`\n  * **Assigned Employees**: Add your **Service Employee User**\n  * **Permissions**:\n    * *Lead & Quotation*: `None`\n    * *Service Ticket*: `User: Own Documents Only`\n    * *AMC Contract*: `User: Own Documents Only`\n    * *Excel Export*: `No`\n\n---\n\n### What this gives you in the UI:\n- **Same Level Managers**: Both Sales Manager and Service Manager display at identical depth under Management in the tree.\n- **Reporting Line**:\n  - `Sales Executive` reports directly to `Sales Manager`.\n  - `Service Engineer` reports directly to `Service Manager`.\n- **Isolation**: Sales staff cannot view Service tickets, and Service staff cannot view Sales quotations."}

{"step_index":7017,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:39:57Z","content":"Here is the exact explanation of why you are seeing these behaviors (without changing any code):\n\n---\n\n### 1. Why Customer \"New\" Button is NOT Showing:\n* Look at **Profile 2 (Employee)** from your previous screenshot:\n  * **Customer Creation**: `Create` was **unchecked** (only `View` was checked).\n* In [res_partner.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_partner.py#L28-L29):\n  ```python\n  if not can_create:\n      doc.attrib['create'] = 'false'\n  ```\n  Because `perm_customer_create` is **False** for employee roles, Odoo dynamically injects `create=\"false\"` into the Customer list view. This **hides the \"New\" button** and blocks customer creation. The permission reflection is working as designed.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why Equipment and Product DO Show \"New\":\n* In your second screenshot for the Employee role:\n  * **Equipment Master**: `Create` is **checked** \n  * **Product Catalog**: `Create` is **checked** \n* Because `Create` is enabled for Equipment and Product on that role, their \"New\" button remains visible. If you uncheck `Create` on Equipment or Product, their \"New\" button will also disappear just like Customer.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Why Lead & Quote, AMC, and Service Show 0 on the Dashboard:\n* In the Employee profile:\n  * **Lead & Quotation**: `User: Own Documents Only`\n  * **Service Ticket**: `User: Own Documents Only`\n  * **AMC Contract**: `User: Own Documents Only`\n* **Reason for Zero**:\n  * \"Own Documents Only\" filters records where **Salesperson / Assigned User / Responsible User = Vishal** (the logged-in user).\n  * If Vishal has not yet been assigned as the salesperson on any Leads/Quotes, AMC contracts, or Service tickets, his count is **0**.\n  * When logged in as **Manager** (who has `User: All Documents`), the dashboard displays the total count for the whole company/department.\n\n---\n\n### Summary of Permission Reflection:\n| Area | Employee Setting | Result in UI |\n|---|---|---|\n| **Customer** | `Create` ❌ Unchecked | **\"New\" button hidden** |\n| **Equipment** | `Create`  Checked | **\"New\" button visible** |\n| **Product** | `Create`  Checked | **\"New\" button visible** |\n| **Leads / Quotes** | `Own Documents Only` | **Shows 0** (until records are assigned to Vishal) |\n| **AMC & Service** | `Own Documents Only` | **Shows 0** (until records are assigned to Vishal) |\n\nThe permission settings configured in the Job Position master reflect directly into the user interface and access rules."}

{"step_index":7027,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:42:53Z","content":"Here is the reason why Vishal's account does not have the manager permissions yet:\n\n### The Cause:\nIn the screenshot, the Job Position has **\"Is Manager / Head\" = ON** with full manager permissions.\n\nHowever, when a job position is a **Manager Role**, Odoo assigns the user through the **Department Head** field, NOT the regular \"Assigned Employees\" list. \n\nThere are 2 checks to ensure Vishal is actually linked to this manager role:\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Check the Department Head Assignment\n1. Go to **HR** → **Departments** (or Settings → Departments).\n2. Open the department (e.g. **Service** or **Sales**).\n3. Check the **Department Head** field:\n   - Is **Vishal** selected as the **Department Head**?\n   - If not, select **Vishal** and click **Save**.\n   *(When you select him as Department Head, the system automatically links him to this Manager role and syncs all the manager permissions down to his user).*\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Check Vishal's User Profile\n1. Go to **Settings** → **Users & Companies** → **Users**.\n2. Open **Vishal**:\n   - Check what is listed under **Job Position** / **Role**.\n   - If it is currently set to `Service Engineer` (the employee role) or empty, change it to the **Manager** role and click **Save**.\n   - Open his **Permissions** tab on the user form: verify that `Create` for Customer is checked.\n\n---\n\n### Why this happened:\nIf Vishal was initially created or assigned to the **Employee (Engineer)** role, his user record still had `perm_customer_create = False`. Once you set him as the **Department Head** in the Department or select the Manager role on his user, the manager permissions (`Create` = True, `All Documents`) will take effect immediately for him."}

{"step_index":7037,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:43:43Z","content":"I found the exact bug in the python code!\n\nLook at lines 89–165 in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L89-L166):\n```python\ngroup_ops = []\n# It built all the security groups in `group_ops` (e.g. Sales All Documents, Contact Creation)...\n# BUT it never called `user.write({'groups_id': group_ops})`!\n# On line 166 it just had `pass`!\n```\n\n### Why this caused all the issues:\n1. **Customer \"New\" button not showing**: The Odoo Contact Manager security group (`base.group_partner_manager`) in `group_ops` was **never assigned** to the user record because `group_ops` was never written.\n2. **Dashboard showing zero**: The sales group (`sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads`) was also in `group_ops` and **never written** to the user's groups, so Odoo's core sales filters didn't give Vishal access to all documents.\n\n---\n\n### The Fix:\nIn `_apply_job_permissions`, line 164 needs to include `'groups_id': group_ops`:\n```python\nif group_ops:\n    user_vals['groups_id'] = group_ops\nuser.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write(user_vals)\n```\n\nYou said **\"do not change anything\"** earlier, so I have not touched the file. \n\nWould you like me to apply this 2-line fix and deploy it so that Vishal gets all his manager groups and permissions immediately?"}
