{"step_index":7063,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:48:50Z","content":"Here is the complete analysis and the direct answers to your observations:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Why Access Errors Occur on \"Lead\" (`crm.lead`) and \"Sales Order\" (`sale.order`):\nLook at the error screenshots:\n> *\"You are not allowed to access 'Lead' (crm.lead) records. Allowed for Sales/Administrator, Sales/User: Own Documents Only.\"*\n\n* **The Cause**: In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L89-L166), when you configure permissions in Job Positions, the code prepares the security groups (`group_ops`) like `sales_team.group_sale_salesman` and `base.group_partner_manager`, but it **forgot to save them to the user record** (it had `pass` instead of `user.write({'groups_id': group_ops})`).\n* **The Result**: \n  - Vishal was **never granted** the underlying Odoo Sales security group.\n  - When he clicks on Leads or Quotes, Odoo throws the Access Error shown in your screenshots.\n  - When this is saved, the access error disappears completely.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Why Quick Action Buttons Open Complete Wizards (Not List View):\nIn your third screenshot, those three blue buttons on the dashboard hero are:\n* **`+ Create Lead`**\n* **`+ Create AMC`**\n* **`+ Create Service Ticket`**\n\nThese buttons are explicitly programmed as **Quick Creation Shortcuts**:\n* `+ Create Lead` opens the multi-step `crm.lead.wizard` popup to create a new lead.\n* `+ Create Service Ticket` opens the `service.ticket.wizard` popup to log a new ticket.\n* To see the **List Views** of existing Leads/Quotes, AMC, or Service Tickets, users click on the **metric cards below** (e.g. clicking the \"Leads\", \"Qualified\", \"AMC\", or \"Service\" stat cards) or use the main navbar menus.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Equipment Master & Products vs Quick Access (Assignee Filter):\n* You noted: *\"equipment see other public this option not available... we have to manage for only assigned user show only items that assigned not all\"*.\n* Right now, in [dashboard.js](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js#L218-L235), Equipment Master does not check for an assigned user domain; it only filters by `company_id`.\n* For regular employees / non-admins, Equipment Master should filter records so users only see and access equipment assigned to them or their department, rather than the public/all list.\n\n---\n\n### 4. Summary of Actions Needed:\n1. **Fix `res_users.py`** to write `groups_id` so Vishal gets `sales_team.group_sale_salesman` and `base.group_partner_manager`. This fixes both the **Access Errors on Lead/Sale Order** and the **Customer \"New\" button**.\n2. **Dashboard Quick Action vs List**: Keep the `+ Create` buttons as creation wizards, and clarify navigation to the list views via the metric cards/menus.\n3. **Equipment Domain Filter**: Restrict the Equipment Master list so non-admin users only see items assigned to their scope.\n\nWould you like me to apply the `groups_id` fix now so Vishal can immediately access Leads, Quotations, and Customers without access errors?"}

{"step_index":7065,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:50:05Z","content":"This is the **exact same issue** confirming the missing `groups_id` write.\n\n### Why this happens:\nThe error message says:\n> **\"You are not allowed to create 'Lead' (crm.lead) records.**  \n> **This operation is allowed for the following groups:**  \n> **- Sales/Administrator**  \n> **- Sales/User: Own Documents Only\"**\n\nIn Odoo, to create or save a Lead, the user's account **must** belong to either `Sales/User: Own Documents Only` or `Sales/Administrator`. \n\nIn [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L84-L165):\n1. `_apply_job_permissions` correctly calculated:\n   ```python\n   g_own = self.env.ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman', raise_if_not_found=False)\n   # and appended (4, g_own.id) or (4, g_all.id) to group_ops\n   ```\n2. **BUT** at the end of the method:\n   ```python\n   user.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write(user_vals)\n   pass\n   ```\n   `group_ops` was **never written to the user** (`user_vals['groups_id'] = group_ops` was omitted).\n3. Therefore, both the Manager and Employee accounts have **no Sales group assigned in Odoo**, causing this exact Access Error whenever they try to open or save a Lead.\n\n---\n\n### The Fix:\nInclude `user_vals['groups_id'] = group_ops` in `_apply_job_permissions` so every user assigned to a role automatically receives their proper Sales & Customer groups.\n\nShould I apply this fix now so creating and saving Leads will work smoothly for both Manager and Employee?"}

{"step_index":7070,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T04:51:30Z","content":"**No, it will still NOT work for the remaining users until we fix that missing line in Python.**\n\nHere is the exact reason why:\n\nEven though you selected **\"User: All Documents\"** in the radio button:\n1. In [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L124-L130), the code identifies the group `sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads` and puts it into the list `group_ops`.\n2. **BUT** on line 164:\n   ```python\n   user.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write(user_vals)\n   ```\n   `user_vals` only contains the custom boolean fields. **`group_ops` is never written to `user`!**\n3. Because Odoo's internal security group is never actually saved onto the user, Odoo considers that user to have **0 sales permissions**, and immediately blocks them with:\n   > *\"Access Error: You are not allowed to access 'Lead' (crm.lead) records.\"*\n\n---\n\n### The 1-minute fix that makes ALL 4 users (2 Managers + 2 Employees) work:\n\nIn [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py#L164), we add:\n```python\nif group_ops:\n    user_vals['groups_id'] = group_ops\nuser.sudo().with_context(skip_sync=True).write(user_vals)\n```\n\nAs soon as this is added:\n- **Both Managers** will immediately get `User: All Documents` + Customer Creation + Lead access with **no errors**.\n- **Both Employees** will immediately get `User: Own Documents Only` + Customer View with **no errors**.\n\nMay I apply this fix right now?"}

Log in as **Admin**.\n  2. Go to **Settings** → **Users & Companies** → **Job Positions**.\n  3. Open the **Manager** role (or Employee role).\n  4. Toggle or re-select **Lead & Quotation** (e.g. click \"User: All Documents\") and click **Save** (Cloud icon / Save button).\n  *(This triggers line 803 in `res_users.py`: `users._apply_job_permissions(job)`, which writes the Sales groups into Vishal's account).*\n\n---\n\n### Reason 2: Verify in Vishal's User Profile\nTo confirm that Vishal has received the group:\n1. Under the **Access Rights** tab, look at **Sales**:\n   - It should say **\"User: All Documents\"** (or \"User: Own Documents Only\").\n   - If it says **\"Internal User\"** and Sales is empty, select **\"User: All Documents\"** and click **Save**.\n\nOnce Sales is set on his account, the Lead creation error will be resolved permanently."}

{\"step_index\":658,\"source\":\"MODEL\",\"type\":\"PLANNER_RESPONSE\",\"status\":\"DONE\",\"created_at\":\"2026-09-18T07:53:41Z\",\"content\":\"Here is the reason why the number does not update on the screen right now, and the exact code to fix it:\\n\\n---\\n\\n### The Problem:\\nCurrently, the number generation is only inside Python's `write()` method:\\n* When a user changes the radio button `Contract Status` from **Draft** to **Active** (or Active to Draft), Python `write()` only runs **after the user clicks Save**.\\n* It does **not** run in real-time as an `@api.onchange`, so the user does not see the number change live on their screen when clicking the radio button!\\n\\n---\\n\\n### The Solution:\\nAdd an `@api.onchange('contract_status')` in **`amc_contract.py`** so that the moment the user clicks **Active** (or **Expired / Renewed / Cancelled**) or switches back to **Draft**, the `AMC No.` (`name`) updates **instantly on the screen**:\\n\\n#### Code to add in [amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py):\\n\\n```python\\n    @api.onchange('contract_status')\\n    def _onchange_contract_status(self):\\n        if self.contract_status == 'draft':\\n            # Switch back to Draft number\\n            if self.draft_name:\\n                self.name = self.draft_name\\n            elif not self.name or not self.name.startswith('Draft-'):\\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract.draft', 'AMC Draft Series', prefix='Draft-')\\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or 'Draft-1'\\n                self.draft_name = self.name\\n        else:\\n            # Switch to Official number (Active, Expired, Renewed, Cancelled)\\n            if self.official_name:\\n                self.name = self.official_name\\n            elif not self.name or self.name.startswith('Draft-') or self.name.lower() in ('draft', 'new'):\\n                seq = self._get_or_create_sequence('amc.contract', 'AMC Numbering Series', prefix=False)\\n                self.name = seq.next_by_id() or '1'\\n                self.official_name = self.name\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Also make `name` readonly in XML so users don't type over it manually:\\nIn [amc_contract_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/amc_contract_views.xml#L13):\\n```xml\\n<h1>\\n    <field name=\\\"name\\\" readonly=\\\"1\\\"/>\\n</h1>\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### What this achieves:\\n1. When user selects **Draft** ➔ `name` immediately shows `Draft-X`.\\n2. When user clicks **Active** (or any non-draft status) ➔ `name` immediately switches to official number (`1`, `2`, `3`...).\\n3. If they switch back from Active to Draft ➔ it restores `Draft-X` without losing it!\\n4. The user sees the change right on their screen before even clicking Save!\\n\\nAs per your rule, I will **not edit any file** until you explicitly tell me to proceed!\"}\n599: {\"step_index\":664,\"source\":\"USER_EXPLICIT\",\"type\":\"USER_INPUT\",\"status\":\"DONE\",\"created_at\":\"2026-09-18T08:00:33Z\",\"content\":\"<USER_REQUEST>\\nwhat id user say i want to chane id ?\\n</USER_REQUEST>\\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-18T13:30:33+05:30.\\n\\nThe user's current state is as follows:\\nActive Document: d:\\\\CRM Github\\\\addons\\\\custom_crm_extended\\\\views\\\\amc_contract_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\\nCursor is on line: 1\\nOther open documents:\\n- d:\\\\CRM Github\\\\addons\\\\custom_crm_extended\\\\views\\\\amc_contract_views.xml (LANGUAGE_XML)\\n- d:\\\\CRM Github\\\\addons\\\\custom_crm_extended\\\\models\\\\amc_contract.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\"}\n600: {\"step_index\":665,\"source\":\"MODEL\",\"type\":\"PLANNER_RESPONSE\",\"status\":\"DONE\",\"created_at\":\"2026-09-18T08:00:33Z\",\"tool_calls\":[{\"name\":\"view_file\",\"args\":{\"AbsolutePath\":\"\\\"d:\\\\\\\\CRM Github\\\\\\\\addons\\\\\\\\custom_crm_extended\\\\\\\\models\\\\\\\\amc_contract.py\\\"\",\"EndLine\":\"238\",\"StartLine\":\"210\",\"toolAction\":\"\\\"Viewing file\\\"\",\"toolSummary\":\"\\\"Check placement of _onchange_contract_status\\\"\"}}]}\nThe above content does NOT show the entire file contents. Dashboard & UI Theme (`crm_whitelabel`)\n* **[dashboard.js](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/dashboard.js)** & **[dashboard.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/xml/dashboard.xml)**:\n  * Quick action buttons (`+ Create Lead`, `+ Create AMC`, `+ Create Service Ticket`).\n  * Stat counters and multi-company filtering.\n* **[dashboard.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/dashboard.css)** & **[form_custom.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/form_custom.css)**:\n  * Fluid responsive column sizing (`clamp()`) for hierarchy tree.\n  * Clean table layout for assigned employees.\n  * Statusbar buttons styling and save button ordering.\n* **[nav_buttons.js](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/js/nav_buttons.js)**:\n  * Top navigation bar controls.\n\n---\n\n### 3. Excel Export (\"Export All Fields\")\n* **[export_all_fields.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/controllers/export_all_fields.py)** & **[controllers/__init__.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/controllers/__init__.py)**:\n  * Backend controller removing model brackets from exported `.xlsx` filenames.\n* **[export_all_form_fields.js](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/static/src/js/export_all_form_fields.js)**:\n  * Gear (⚙️) menu action allowing export of all form fields directly from list view.\n\n---\n\n### 4. AMC, Equipment & Lead Enhancements\n* **[amc_contract.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/amc_contract.py)**:\n  * Real-time draft numbering (`Draft-X`) vs official numbering transition.\n* **[equipment_master.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/equipment_master.py)** & **[equipment_master_wizard.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/equipment_master_wizard.py)**:\n  * Equipment Owner / Model Number naming sync and prefix sequence deduplication.\n* **[crm_lead.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/crm_lead.py)** & **[crm_lead_wizard.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/crm_lead_wizard.py)**:\n  * Lead priority handling and multi-step wizard creation.\n* **[sale_order.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/sale_order.py)** & **[sale_order_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/sale_order_views.xml)**:\n  * Quotation preview and invoice-pending tracking.\n* **[service_ticket_wizard.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/wizard/service_ticket_wizard.py)**:\n  * Non-admin `.sudo()` queries for multi-user ticket assignment.\n* **[multi_company_rules.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/security/multi_company_rules.xml)**:\n  * Equipment and ticket multi-company record rules.\n* **[__manifest__.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/__manifest__.py)**:\n  * Registered new assets (`export_all_form_fields.js`, `user_access_labels.js`).\n\n---\n\n### Summary of Differences:\nThe code in your Git repo already contains all these updates. {"step_index":7164,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:06:48Z","content":"Here is the **exact one-line command** to safely upgrade and activate everything in your **Live Production** system:\n\n```bash\nsudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp ; /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\n```\n\n---\n\n### What this command does step-by-step:\n1. `sudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp` ➔ Safely stops the live service and frees port 8069.\n2. `/opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init` ➔ Upgrades the modules, adds any new database columns/views into your live database (`crm_data`).\n3. `sudo systemctl start crm` ➔ Starts the live production CRM service back up cleanly.\n\nRun this in your **GCP SSH terminal**, and your production system (`:8069`) will have all updated features live!"}

{"step_index":7181,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:13:51Z","content":"Because both ports use the exact same code, the only differences between **Port 8070 (Testing)** and **Port 8069 (Production)** are inside their **PostgreSQL databases** (`crm_data_test` vs `crm_data`).\n\nHere are the exact ways to see the differences between the two ports:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Check Installed/Upgraded Modules Difference (CLI Command)\nRun this single command in GCP SSH to compare which custom modules are installed or updated in Test vs Production:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -c \"\nSELECT 'crm_data_test (8070)' as db, name, state, latest_version \nFROM ir_module_module WHERE name IN ('custom_crm_extended', 'crm_whitelabel')\nUNION ALL\nSELECT 'crm_data (8069)' as db, name, state, latest_version \nFROM ir_module_module WHERE name IN ('custom_crm_extended', 'crm_whitelabel');\n\" -d crm_data_test\n```\n*(This shows if a module is `installed`, its exact version number, and if both databases are on the same version).*\n\n---\n\n### 2. Compare Record Counts (Users, Leads, Jobs, Departments)\nRun this command in GCP SSH to see how the data differs between the two ports:\n\n```bash\nsudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data_test -c \"\nSELECT 'crm_data_test (8070)' AS db,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM res_users WHERE share = false) AS internal_users,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM hr_job) AS job_positions,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM hr_department) AS departments,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM crm_lead) AS total_leads,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM sale_order) AS quotations;\n\" && sudo -u postgres psql -d crm_data -c \"\nSELECT 'crm_data (8069)' AS db,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM res_users WHERE share = false) AS internal_users,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM hr_job) AS job_positions,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM hr_department) AS departments,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM crm_lead) AS total_leads,\n       (SELECT count(*) FROM sale_order) AS quotations;\n\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. Compare Directly in Your Web Browser (Side-by-Side)\nOpen two tabs in your browser:\n* **Tab 1 (Testing)**: `http://34.14.132.247:8070/`\n* **Tab 2 (Production)**: `http://34.14.132.247:8069/`\n\n**What you will see:**\n* **On Port 8070 (Testing)**: You will see your test users (Vishal, test managers/employees), test departments (`HR`, `Finance`), and test leads.\n* **On Port 8069 (Production)**: You will see your real live sales leads, real customers, and live company records without any test clutter."}

{"step_index":7187,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:15:27Z","content":"Because your Odoo server and PostgreSQL database run entirely on your **GCP cloud server** (`34.14.132.247`), your laptop is used purely as a **development client**. You do **not** need to install PostgreSQL or Python/Odoo locally on the new laptop.\n\nHere is the exact setup and configuration needed on your new laptop:\n\n---\n\n### 1. Essential Software to Install:\n1. **Git for Windows**:\n   - Download & install from: [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/)\n   - Required so you can clone, pull, and run your `.\\sync.ps1` script.\n2. **Your IDE / Editor**:\n   - Install **Google Antigravity IDE** (or VS Code).\n3. **SSH Client**:\n   - Windows 10/11 already has OpenSSH built into PowerShell / Command Prompt.\n   - (Optional) PuTTY or your preferred terminal if you use that for GCP SSH.\n\n---\n\n### 2. Git & GitHub Configuration:\nOpen PowerShell on the new laptop and set your Git credentials:\n```powershell\ngit config --global user.name \"crm-ux\"\ngit config --global user.email \"crm@yantradynamics.in\"\n```\n\n---\n\n### 3. Clone Your Repository:\nCreate your folder (e.g. `D:\\CRM Github` or `C:\\CRM Github`) and clone the repo:\n```powershell\ngit clone https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git \"D:\\CRM Github\"\n```\n*(When prompted by Windows Git Credential Manager, log in with your GitHub account / Personal Access Token).*\n\n---\n\n### 4. Enable PowerShell Script Execution (for `.\\sync.ps1`):\nBy default, Windows blocks custom `.ps1` scripts from running. Run this once in PowerShell as Administrator:\n```powershell\nSet-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser\n```\nNow `.\\sync.ps1` will run smoothly without any permission errors.\n\n---\n\n### 5. GCP SSH Access:\nMake sure you can connect to your server from the new laptop:\n* Either through the **GCP Cloud Console Web SSH** button in your browser,\n* Or copy your SSH private key (`id_rsa`) to `C:\\Users\\<YourUser>\\.ssh\\` if you connect via PowerShell SSH:\n  ```powershell\n  ssh crm@34.14.132.247\n  ```\n\n---\n\n### 6. Bookmark Your Ports:\n* **Testing CRM**: `http://34.14.132.247:8070`\n* **Production CRM**: `http://34.14.132.247:8069`\n\nOnce these 6 steps are done, your new laptop is 100% ready to edit code, push with `.\\sync.ps1`, and deploy to GCP!"}

Open your browser on the new laptop and go to:  \n   👉 **[console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com)**\n2. Select your project and go to **Compute Engine** → **VM instances**.\n3. Next to your CRM instance (`34.14.132.247`), simply click the **\"SSH\"** button.\n4. A terminal window opens directly in your browser.  \n   *(No SSH keys, no downloads, and no configuration required!)*\n\n---\n\n### Option 2: If you connect directly from Terminal / PowerShell (Using SSH Key)\nIf you prefer running `ssh crm@34.14.132.247` directly inside PowerShell:\n\n1. **Check your old laptop**:\n   - Go to `C:\\Users\\Admin\\.ssh\\` (or your username folder on the old laptop).\n   - Copy the files inside that `.ssh` folder (especially `id_rsa` or your key file).\n2. **On your new laptop**:\n   - Paste those files into `C:\\Users\\<YourNewUsername>\\.ssh\\`.\n3. Now open PowerShell and connect immediately:\n   ```powershell\n   ssh crm@34.14.132.247\n   ```\n\n---\n\n### Option 3: Using Google Cloud CLI (`gcloud`)\nIf you want to use the official Google Cloud tool:\n1. Download and install **Google Cloud CLI** on your new laptop.\n2. Open PowerShell and run:\n   ```powershell\n   gcloud auth login\n   ```\n   *(Logs in with your Google account in the browser)*\n3. Connect anytime with:\n   ```powershell\n   gcloud compute ssh <instance-name> --zone=<your-zone>\n   ```\n   Google will automatically create and sync all SSH keys for you without any manual copying.\n\n---\n\n### Recommendation:\nStart with **Option 1 (Browser SSH)** or copy the `.ssh` folder (**Option 2**). Both work immediately with your existing VM!"}

{"step_index":7193,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:18:49Z","content":"If you already use your **Google Account** in GCP on your old laptop, then on your new laptop it is even simpler!\n\n### Here is all you need to do on the new laptop:\n\n1. **Open your browser** (Chrome / Edge).\n2. **Sign in with that same Google Account**.\n3. Go to GCP Console:\n   👉 **https://console.cloud.google.com/compute/instances**\n4. You will see your running VM instance (`34.14.132.247`).\n5. Just click the **\"SSH\"** button on the right side.\n\nGoogle Cloud automatically authenticates your Google account and opens the terminal window right in your browser. \n\nYou can run all your usual commands there directly:\n```bash\ncd /home/crm/odoo-custom && git pull && sudo systemctl restart crm-test\n```\n\n### Summary of What the VM Needs:\n- **No changes to the VM**: The VM continues running on Google Cloud 24/7 as usual.\n- **No special setup**: Because GCP knows your Google account, it will let you connect via the browser SSH button from any laptop in seconds."}

{"step_index":7195,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:19:15Z","content":"On the **VM side (GCP server)**:\n* **You don't need to do ANYTHING for Git.**\n* The VM already has Git installed and configured. It already connects to your GitHub repository `https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git`.\n* When you run `git pull` or `git reset --hard origin/main` in the GCP SSH window, it will continue to work exactly as it does right now.\n\n---\n\nOn the **New Laptop side**:\nBecause it is a brand new machine, it just needs the Git program installed so your local folder and `.\\sync.ps1` work:\n\n1. **Install Git for Windows**:\n   - Download: https://git-scm.com/download/win (just install with default settings).\n2. **Clone the code to your new laptop**:\n   - Open PowerShell and run:\n     ```powershell\n     git clone https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git \"D:\\CRM Github\"\n     ```\n   - A browser window will pop up asking: **\"Sign in with your browser\"**.\n   - Click it (since you are signed into GitHub with your Google account, it logs you in with 1 click).\n3. **Set your name & email once in PowerShell**:\n   ```powershell\n   git config --global user.name \"crm-ux\"\n   git config --global user.email \"crm@yantradynamics.in\"\n   ```\n\n### That's all!\n- **New Laptop**: edits files ➔ runs `.\\sync.ps1` ➔ pushes to GitHub.\n- **VM**: runs in GCP ➔ pulls from GitHub ➔ restarts services."}
{"step_index":7196,"source":"USER_EXPLICIT","type":"USER_INPUT","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:20:01Z","content":"<USER_REQUEST>\nsync.ps1 use git or github?\n</USER_REQUEST>\n<ADDITIONAL_METADATA>\nThe current local time is: 2026-09-25T10:50:01+05:30.\n\nThe user's current state is as follows:\nActive Document: d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\res_users.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\nCursor is on line: 157\nOther open documents:\n- d:\\CRM Github\\addons\\custom_crm_extended\\models\\res_users.py (LANGUAGE_PYTHON)\n</ADDITIONAL_METADATA>"}
{"step_index":7197,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:20:01Z","content":"**`sync.ps1` uses BOTH — here is how they work together:**\n\nLook at the 4 lines inside your [sync.ps1](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/sync.ps1):\n\n```powershell\n1: git add .\n2: git commit -m \"Update code for testing\"\n3: git push origin main\n```\n\n---\n\n### Step-by-Step Breakdown:\n\n1. **`git add .` and `git commit` (USES GIT - LOCAL)**:\n   - **Git** is the program installed on your laptop.\n   - It takes the files you changed on your hard drive and packages them into a local snapshot (commit).\n\n2. **`git push origin main` (USES GITHUB - CLOUD)**:\n   - **GitHub** is the online website (`https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git`).\n   - Git takes that snapshot from your laptop and sends (pushes) it over the internet to **GitHub**.\n\n3. **In GCP SSH (VM pulls from GITHUB)**:\n   - When you run `git pull` on your VM, the VM connects to **GitHub** and downloads those changes.\n\n---\n\n### Summary:\n* **Git** is the engine running the commands on your laptop.\n* **GitHub** is the cloud bridge where your code is stored so the GCP server can download it.\n* Therefore, installing **Git on your new laptop** is what allows `sync.ps1` to communicate with **GitHub**."}

{"step_index":7199,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:21:01Z","content":"Here is the **complete, exact 3-step setup for Git** on your new laptop. It takes only 2 minutes:\n\n---\n\n### Step 1: Install Git (Software)\n1. Download the installer from: **https://git-scm.com/download/win**\n2. Run the `.exe` file.\n3. Keep clicking **Next** on all prompts and click **Install**.\n*(This installs the `git` command into PowerShell and Windows terminal).*\n\n---\n\n### Step 2: Configure Your Name & Email\nOpen **PowerShell** on your new laptop and paste these 2 commands:\n\n```powershell\ngit config --global user.name \"crm-ux\"\ngit config --global user.email \"crm@yantradynamics.in\"\n```\n*(This tells Git who is making the commits, exactly matching your current setup).*\n\n---\n\n### Step 3: Link to Your GitHub Account (One-Time Login)\nIn PowerShell, clone your project into your preferred folder (e.g. `D:\\CRM Github`):\n\n```powershell\ngit clone https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git \"D:\\CRM Github\"\n```\n\n1. A small popup window will appear: **\"GitHub Credential Manager\"**.\n2. Click **\"Sign in with your browser\"**.\n3. Your browser will open. Since you are logged into your Google account, click **\"Authorize GitCredentialManager\"**.\n\n---\n\n### Step 4: Allow `.\\sync.ps1` to Run in PowerShell\nWindows by default blocks PowerShell scripts. Run this **one command** in PowerShell:\n\n```powershell\nSet-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser\n```\n\n---\n\n### Done!\nAfter these steps:\n- You open **`D:\\CRM Github`** in your IDE.\n- You edit your code.\n- You type `.\\sync.ps1` in PowerShell, and it pushes directly to GitHub just like on your old laptop."}

{"step_index":7203,"source":"MODEL","type":"PLANNER_RESPONSE","status":"DONE","created_at":"2026-09-25T05:29:37Z","tool_calls":[{"name":"write_to_file","args":{"ArtifactMetadata":{"RequestFeedback":false,"Summary":"Complete chronological chat summary and handoff documentation covering user management, department hierarchy, permission syncing, production migration diffs, and new laptop setup guide.","UserFacing":true},"CodeContent":"# CRM Chat Transcript & Development Summary (24-25 Sept 2026)\n\n## 1. Project Overview & Environments\n- **Local Dev Path**: `D:\\CRM Github`\n- **GCP Server Path**: `/home/crm/odoo-custom/addons` (IP: `34.14.132.247`)\n- **Testing Instance**: Port `8070` | DB: `crm_data_test` | Service: `crm-test` | Config: `/etc/crm_test.conf`\n- **Production Instance**: Port `8069` | DB: `crm_data` | Service: `crm` | Config: `/etc/crm.conf`\n\n---\n\n## 2. Key Accomplishments & Technical Fixes\n\n### A. Department Hierarchy Alignment (Form Upper Right)\n- **Problem**: Default Odoo 2-level widget was hidden via CSS, but custom tree rendered below the form fields, creating an awkward empty gap.\n- **Fix**:\n  - Replaced `<xpath expr=\"//widget[@name='hr_department_chart']\" position=\"replace\">` directly inside [res_users_signature_views.xml](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/views/res_users_signature_views.xml#L210-L215).\n  - Replaced static pixel widths with dynamic viewport clamp: `max-width: clamp(18rem, 28vw, 32rem)` in both [form_custom.css](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/crm_whitelabel/static/src/css/form_custom.css) and [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py).\n  - Result: Beautiful multi-level tree (Management -> Sales -> HR) sitting tightly in the upper-right section next to form fields.\n\n### B. User Permission Matrix & Access Error Resolution\n- **Problem**: When non-admin users (e.g. Vishal as Manager, or regular staff) attempted to create/save Leads, Quotations, or Customers, Odoo blocked them with:\n  > `Access Error: You are not allowed to access/create 'Lead' (crm.lead) records.`\n- **Root Cause**:\n  - In `_apply_job_permissions` in [res_users.py](file:///d:/CRM%20Github/addons/custom_crm_extended/models/res_users.py), Odoo security groups (e.g., `sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads`, `base.group_partner_manager`) were calculated into `group_ops` but never written to `user.write({'groups_id': group_ops})` (`pass` was executed instead).\n- **Fix**:\n  - Attached `user_vals['groups_id'] = group_ops` so that assigning a Job Position automatically synchronizes the underlying Odoo core security groups to the user profile safely.\n  - Protected superusers `(2, 10, 11)` and `base.group_system` with hardcoded bypass.\n\n### C. Permission Profile Matrix\n\n| Role | Lead & Quote | Service Ticket | AMC Contract | Customer | Equipment | Product | Excel Export |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|:---:|\n| **Managers** (Sales/Service) | `User: All Documents` | `User: All Documents` | `User: All Documents` | Create, Update, View | Create, Update, View | Create, Update, View | Yes |\n| **Employees** (Staff) | `User: Own Documents Only` | `User: Own Documents Only` | `User: Own Documents Only` | View (Read-Only) | Create, Update, View | Create, Update, View | Yes |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Production Deployment & Difference Analysis\n- **Codebase Sharing**: Both Port `8070` (Test) and Port `8069` (Live) share the exact same repository folder `/home/crm/odoo-custom/addons`.\n- **Changes Upgraded to Production (Since Sept 18 commit `61b317a`)**:\n  - **26 Files Changed** (+2,131 lines added, -155 removed).\n  - Multi-level department/job hierarchy computes.\n  - Job Position to User permission synchronization.\n  - Export all fields from list view without model brackets (`.xlsx`).\n  - Real-time AMC draft vs official number switching.\n  - Dashboard quick action buttons and responsive styling.\n- **Production Upgrade Command**:\n  ```bash\n  sudo systemctl stop crm && sudo fuser -k 8069/tcp ; /opt/crm/venv/bin/python3 /opt/crm/odoo-bin -c /etc/crm.conf -d crm_data -u custom_crm_extended,crm_whitelabel --stop-after-init && sudo systemctl start crm\n  ```\n\n---\n\n## 4. New Laptop Setup Guide\n\nYour GCP VM and PostgreSQL database run entirely in the cloud (`34.14.132.247`). You **do NOT need** Python, PostgreSQL, or Odoo installed locally on the new laptop.\n\n### Quick Setup Steps:\n1. **Install Git for Windows**:\n   - Download: [git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win) (click Next on default prompts).\n2. **Configure Git Identity in PowerShell**:\n   ```powershell\n   git config --global user.name \"crm-ux\"\n   git config --global user.email \"crm@yantradynamics.in\"\n   ```\n3. **Clone the Repository**:\n   ```powershell\n   git clone https://github.com/crm-ux/CRM-UX.git \"D:\\CRM Github\"\n   ```\n   - When prompted by GitHub Credential Manager, click **\"Sign in with your browser\"** (authenticate with your Google account).\n4. **Enable Script Execution (for `.\\sync.ps1`)**:\n   ```powershell\n   Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser\n   ```\n5. **GCP VM SSH Connection**:\n   - Open browser, navigate to GCP Console: `console.cloud.google.com/compute/instances`\n   - Log in with your Google Account and click the **\"SSH\"** button next to your VM instance.\n6. **Open in Antigravity IDE**:\n   - Open the cloned folder `D:\\CRM Github` and resume development immediately!\n","Description":"Created Markdown summary document of the entire chat session and setup guide.","Overwrite":true,"TargetFile":"d:/CRM Github/CHAT_SESSION_SUMMARY_25_SEP.md","toolAction":"Creating file","toolSummary":"Write complete chat session summary markdown file"}}]}
